questions.chapter_title: The Past, Present, and Future
questions.stem: A patient chooses to have the certified nurse-midwife (CNM) provide care during her pregnancy. What does the CNM‘s scope of practice include?
questions.rationale: The CNM provides comprehensive prenatal and postnatal care, attends uncomplicated deliveries, and ensures that a backup physician is available in case of unforeseen problems.

questions.chapter_title: The Past, Present, and Future
questions.stem: Which medical pioneer discovered the relationship between the incidence of puerperal fever and unwashed hands?
questions.rationale: Ignaz Semmelweis deduced that puerperal fever was septic, contagious, and transmitted by the unwashed hands of physicians and medical students.

questions.chapter_title: The Past, Present, and Future
questions.stem: A pregnant woman who has recently immigrated to the United States comments to the nurse, “Tam afraid of childbirth. It is so dangerous. I am afraid I will die.” What is the best nursing response reflecting cultural sensitivity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Maternal mortality in the United States is extremely low.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Anesthesia is available to relieve pain during labor and childbirth.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Tell me why you are afraid of childbirth.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Your condition will be monitored during labor and delivery.”

questions.rationale: Asking the patient about her concerns helps promote understanding and individualizes patient care.

questions.chapter_title: The Past, Present, and Future
questions.stem: An urban area has been reported to have a high perinatal mortality rate. What information does this provide?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Maternal and infant deaths per 100,000 live births per year

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deaths of fetuses weighing more than 500 g per 10,000 births per year

choices.label: C
choices.text: Deaths of infants up to 1 year of age per 1000 live births per year

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fetal and neonatal deaths per 1000 live births per year

questions.rationale: The perinatal mortality rate includes fetal and neonatal deaths per 1000 live births per year.

questions.chapter_title: The Past, Present, and Future
questions.stem: What is the focus of current maternity practice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hospital births for the majority of women

choices.label: C
choices.text: Separation of labor rooms from delivery rooms

choices.label: D
choices.text: A quality family experience for each patient

questions.rationale: Current maternity practice focuses on a high-quality family experience for all families, traditional or otherwise.

questions.chapter_title: The Past, Present, and Future
questions.stem: Who advocated the establishment of the Children‘s Bureau?
questions.rationale: Lillian Wald is credited with suggesting the establishment of a federal Children‘s Bureau.

questions.chapter_title: The Past, Present, and Future
questions.stem: What was the result of research done in the 1930s by the Children‘s Bureau?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Children with heart problems are now cared for by pediatric cardiologists.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Child Abuse and Prevention Act was passed.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hot lunch programs were established in many schools.

questions.rationale: School hot lunch programs were developed as a result of research by the Children‘s Bureau on the effects of economic depression on children.

questions.chapter_title: The Past, Present, and Future
questions.stem: What government program was implemented to increase the educational exposure of preschool children?
questions.rationale: Head Start programs were established to increase educational exposure of preschool children.

questions.chapter_title: The Past, Present, and Future
questions.stem: What guidelines define multidisciplinary patient care in terms of expected outcome and timeframe from different areas of care provision?
questions.rationale: Clinical pathways, also known as critical pathways or care maps, are collaborative guidelines that define patient care across disciplines. Expected progress within a specified timeline is identified.

questions.chapter_title: The Past, Present, and Future
questions.stem: A nursing student has reviewed a hospitalized pediatric patient chart, interviewed her mother, and collected admission data. What is the next step the student will take to develop a nursing care plan for this child?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Identify measurable outcomes with a timeline.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Choose specific nursing interventions for the child.

choices.label: D
choices.text: State nursing actions related to the child‘s medical diagnosis.

questions.rationale: The nurse uses assessment data to select appropriate nursing diagnoses. Outcomes and interventions are then developed to address the relevant nursing diagnoses.

questions.chapter_title: The Past, Present, and Future
questions.stem: A nursing student on an obstetric rotation questions the floor nurse about the definition of the LVN/LPN scope of practice. What resource can the nurse suggest to the student?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Association of Women‘s Health, Obstetric and Neonatal Nurses

questions.rationale: The scope of practice of the LVN/LPN is published by the state‘s board of nursing.

questions.chapter_title: The Past, Present, and Future
questions.stem: What was recommended by Karl Credé in 1884?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All women should be delivered in a hospital setting.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chemical means should be used to combat infection.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Podalic version should be done on all fetuses.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Silver nitrate should be placed in the eyes of newborns.

questions.rationale: In 1884 Karl Credé recommended the use of 2% silver nitrate in the eyes of newborns to reduce the incidence of blindness.

questions.chapter_title: The Past, Present, and Future
questions.stem: What is the purpose of the White House Conference on Children and Youth?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Set criteria for normal growth patterns.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Examine the number of live births in minority populations.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Raise money to support well-child clinics in rural areas.

questions.rationale: White House Conferences on Children and Youth are held every 10 years to promote comprehensive child welfare.

questions.chapter_title: The Past, Present, and Future
questions.stem: How many hours of hospital stay does legislation currently allow for a postpartum patient who has delivered vaginally without complications?
questions.rationale: Postpartum patients who deliver vaginally stay in the hospital for an average of 48 hours; patients who have had a cesarean delivery usually stay 4 days.

questions.chapter_title: The Past, Present, and Future
questions.stem: How does the clinical pathway or critical pathway improve quality of care?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Outlines expected progress with stated timelines

questions.rationale: Critical pathways outline expected progress with stated timelines. Any deviation from those timelines is called a variance.

questions.chapter_title: The Past, Present, and Future
questions.stem: A patient asks the nurse to explain what is meant by “gene therapy.” What is the nurse‘s best response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gene therapy can replace missing genes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gene therapy evaluates the parent‘s genes.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gene therapy can change the sex of the fetus.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gene therapy supports the regeneration of defective genes.

questions.rationale: Gene therapy can replace missing or defective genes.

questions.chapter_title: The Past, Present, and Future
questions.stem: The nurse is clarifying information to a patient regarding diagnosis-related groups (DRGs). What is the nurse‘s best response when the patient asks how DRGs reduce medical care costs?

choices.label: A
choices.text: By determining payment based on diagnosis

choices.label: B
choices.text: By requiring two medical opinions to confirm a diagnosis

choices.label: D
choices.text: By defining a person who will require hospitalization

questions.rationale: DRGs determine the amount of payment and length of hospital stay based on the diagnosis.

questions.chapter_title: The Past, Present, and Future
questions.stem: How does electronic charting ensure comprehensive charting more effectively than handwritten charting?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Provides a uniform style of chart.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Requires certain responses before allowing the user to progress.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All documentation is reflective of the nursing care plan.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Requires a daily audit by the charge nurse.

questions.rationale: Comprehensive electronic documentation is ensured by requiring specific input in designated categories before the user can progress through the system.

questions.chapter_title: The Past, Present, and Future
questions.stem: The nurse reminds family members that the philosophy of family-centered care is to provide control to the family over health care decisions. What is the appropriate term for this type of control?
questions.rationale: The term empowerment refers to the control a family has over its own health care decisions.

questions.chapter_title: The Past, Present, and Future
questions.stem: A patient in the prenatal clinic is concerned about losing her job because of her pregnancy. The nurse instructs her that the Family Medical Leave Act (FMLA) allows an employee tobe absent from work without pay. How many weeks does the FMLA allow a woman to recover from childbirth or care for a sick family member without loss of benefits or pay status?
questions.rationale: The FMLA allows for employees to leave work for up to 12 weeks to recover from childbirth or to care for an ill family member without losing benefits or pay status.

questions.chapter_title: The Past, Present, and Future
questions.stem: What term appropriately describes the nurse who is able to adapt health care practices to meet the needs of various cultures?
questions.rationale: The nurse who is able to adapt health care to meet the needs of various cultures is said to be culturally competent.

questions.chapter_title: The Past, Present, and Future
questions.stem: What is one major advantage to the application of critical thinking?
questions.rationale: Critical thinking results in problem prevention in designing nursing care.

questions.chapter_title: The Past, Present, and Future
questions.stem: What services are birthing centers able to provide? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Birthing centers are capable of providing full-service obstetric care, classes for new mothers, and family planning. Birthing centers do not offer adoption services.

questions.chapter_title: The Past, Present, and Future
questions.stem: What developments in the early 20th century encouraged women to seek hospitalization for childbirth? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: In the early 1900s, the development of specialized obstetric instruments, better modes of anesthesia, and the physician‘s reliance on hospital services were instrumental in encouraging women to seek hospitalization for childbirth.

questions.chapter_title: The Past, Present, and Future
questions.stem: What non—family-centered policies were prevalent in the 1960s? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: C
choices.text: Delay of reunion of mother and infant

choices.label: E
choices.text: Restrictions of visitations by minor children

questions.rationale: Hospital policies in the 1960s provided a separate waiting room for fathers while the mother went through labor in a sedated state. The reunion of mother and infant was delayed for several hours because of the sedation. Visiting hours were rigid and disallowed the visitation of minor children.

questions.chapter_title: The Past, Present, and Future
questions.stem: The nurse is aware that there is a legal responsibility to report certain diseases and conditions to county or state health authorities. Which would be included? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: The nurse has a legal responsibility to report communicable diseases (such as tuberculosis and sexually transmitted diseases), foodborne infections, child abuse, and threats of suicide.

questions.chapter_title: The Past, Present, and Future
questions.stem: Practical nursing students are using critical thinking skills to study for an upcoming test. What will these students include when studying? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Using critical thinking when studying involves understanding facts before memorizing, prioritizing information to be memorized, relating facts to other facts, using all five senses, reviewing before tests, and reading critically. Critical thinking does not involve assumption as does general thinking.

questions.chapter_title: The Past, Present, and Future
questions.stem: What factors have played a role in meeting the goals of Healthy People 2030 as it relates the goals for outcomes of pregnancy? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Early prenatal care, fetal surgery, use of prenatal glucocorticoids, technology, and NICU care have played a role in increasing the positive outcome of pregnancy, and the goals of Healthy People 2030 may well be met. Increase in surgical births and multiple gestations do not work toward meeting the goals of Healthy People 2030.

questions.chapter_title: The Past, Present, and Future
questions.stem: A community health nurse is providing specialized care to patients in the home setting. What kind of specialized care may this nurse be providing? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Glucose monitoring, heparin therapy, and total parenteral nutrition are categorized as specialized care that may be provided by the community health nurse. Family education and provision of referral are categorized as therapeutic care.

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: A 14-year-old boy is at the pediatric clinic for a checkup. What physical changes of puberty will the nurse indicate are related to the production of testosterone?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Stimulation of production of white cells and platelets

choices.label: B
choices.text: Promotion of growth of small bones

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increase in muscle mass and strength

choices.label: D
choices.text: Decrease in production of sebaceous gland secretions

questions.rationale: Testosterone increases muscle mass, promotes strength and growth of long bones, and enhances production of red blood cells.

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: The nurse is educating high school students about puberty. What will the nurse indicate regulates the production of sperm and secretion hormones?
questions.rationale: The testes have two functions: manufacture of spermatozoa and secretion of androgens.

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: The nurse is speaking with a couple trying to conceive a child. What will the nurse remind the couple is a factor that can decrease sperm production?

choices.label: C
choices.text: The penis and testes being small

questions.rationale: The scrotum is suspended away from the perineum to lower the temperature of the testes for sperm production.

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: When describing the female reproductive tract to a pregnant woman, the nurse would explain that which uterine layer is involved in implantation?
questions.rationale: The endometrium is the inner mucosal layer of the uterus that is governed by cyclical hormonal changes. It is functional during menstruation and during the implantation of a fertilized ovum.

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: A group of nursing students plans to teach a class of sixth-grade girls about menstruation. What correct information will the nursing students teach to the class?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Menarche usually occurs around 12 years of age.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ovulation occurs regularly from the very first cycle.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A regular cycle is established by the third period.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Typically, menstrual flow is heavy and lasts up to 10 days.

questions.rationale: The beginning of menstruation, called menarche, occurs at about 12 years of age. Early cycles are irregular and anovulatory.

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: A 10-year-old girl asks the nurse, “What is the first sign of puberty?” What is the correct nursing response?
questions.rationale: The first outward change of puberty in girls is the development of breasts at about 10 to 11 years of age.

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: A 12-year-old female patient experienced menarche 3 months ago. Her mother voices concern to the pediatric office nurse regarding the irregularity of her daughter‘s menstrual cycle. What is the nurse‘s best response?

choices.label: B
choices.text: “I will talk to the pediatrician about a gynecological referral.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Tcan only discuss this with your daughter.”

questions.rationale: Early cycles are often irregular and may be anovulatory. Regular cycles are usually established within 6 months to 2 years of the menarche. In an average cycle, the flow (menses) occurs every 28 days, plus or minus 5 to 10 days.

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: Which hormone initiates the maturation of the ovarian follicle?
questions.rationale: Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) stimulates the maturation of a follicle.

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: What statement indicates a woman has correct information about oogenesis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Women make fewer ova as they age.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Women have all of their ova at the time they are born.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Ova production begins at birth and continues until puberty.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “New ova are made every month from puberty to climacteric.”

questions.rationale: Oogenesis (formation of immature ova) does not occur after fetal development. Females are born with about 2 million immature ova, which rapidly reduce by adulthood.

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: A pregnant woman asks the nurse, “Will I be able to have a vaginal delivery?” The nurse knows that which is the most favorable pelvic type for vaginal birth?
questions.rationale: The gynecoid pelvis is the typical female pelvis and is most favorable for vaginal birth.

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: A mother is anxious about her ability to breastfeed after her child is born because of her small breast size. What would be an important point to teach this mother?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Milk is produced in ducts and lobules regardless of breast size.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Supplementing breastfeeding with formula allows the infant to receive adequate nutrition.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Breast size can be increased with exercise.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Drinking extra milk during pregnancy allows breasts to produce adequate amounts of milk.

questions.rationale: Breast size does not influence the ability to secrete milk.

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: For what is the decrease in estrogen and progesterone during the menstrual cycle responsible?
questions.rationale: The fall in estrogen and progesterone causes the endometrium to break down, resulting in menstruation.

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: The nurse is assisting with pelvic inlet measurements on a pregnant woman. What measurement will provide the nurse with information about whether the woman can deliver vaginally?
questions.rationale: This measurement determines if the fetus can pass through the birth canal.

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: The nurse has explained menstruation to a 13-year-old girl. What statement indicates the girl needs additional education?

choices.label: B
choices.text: “My cycle should get regular in 6 months.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “T should expect heavy bleeding with clots.”

questions.rationale: Clots are not normally seen in menstrual discharge. A normal menstrual flow is 30 to 40 mL blood and 30 to 50 mL serous fluid.

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: A mother asks the nurse, “When will I know my child has entered puberty?” What will the nurse state based on an understanding of changes associated with puberty?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Your daughter will have her first period.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “You'll recognize puberty by the mood swings.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “The child becomes interested in the opposite sex.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Secondary sex characteristics, such as pubic hair, appear.”

questions.rationale: Puberty begins when the secondary sex characteristics appear. Puberty ends when mature sperm are formed in the male and when regular menstrual cycles occur in the female.

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: A nurse is planning to teach couples about the physiology of the sex act. What correct information will the nurse provide?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Fertilization of an ovum requires penetration by several sperm.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “An ovum must be fertilized within 24 hours of ovulation.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “It takes 4 to 5 days for sperm to reach the fallopian tubes.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Sperm live for only 24 hours following ejaculation.”

questions.rationale: After ovulation, the egg lives for only 24 hours. Sperm must be available during that time if fertilization is to occur. Physiology of the Sex Act

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: A newly married couple tells the nurse they would like to wait a few years before starting a family. Which statement made by the man indicates an understanding about sexual activity and pregnancy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “My wife can‘t get pregnant if] withdraw before climax.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “A man can secrete semen before ejaculation.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “TIfwe don‘t have intercourse very often, my wife won‘t get pregnant.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Tt is safe to ejaculate outside the vagina.”

questions.rationale: Semen may be secreted during sexual intercourse before ejaculation.

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: The nurse is aware that the diagonal conjugate is 12 cm. What is the measurement in centimeters of the obstetric conjugate?
questions.rationale: The obstetric conjugate is approximately 1.5 to 2 cm shorter than the diagonal conjugate.

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: The nurse uses a diagram to demonstrate the fimbriae when teaching nursing students about the female anatomy. What is true about fimbriae?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They form the passageway for the sperm to meet the ovum.

choices.label: B
choices.text: They are the site of fertilization.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They are fingerlike projections that “capture” the ovum.

choices.label: D
choices.text: They propel the egg through the fallopian tube.

questions.rationale: Fimbriae are the fingerlike projections from the infundibulum that “capture” the ovum at ovulation and conduct it into the fallopian tube.

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: What will the nurse explain to a 12-year-old patient when describing what characterizes nocturnal emissions?
questions.rationale: Nocturnal emissions, also known as “wet dreams,” occur without sexual stimulation and contain no sperm. Testosterone levels are constant until midlife.

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: The nurse is educating a pregnant patient who expects to breastfeed. The nurse knows that when a patient breastfeeds, which portions of the breast secrete milk?
questions.rationale: The alveoli secrete milk.

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: Where are the secretions responsible for nourishing sperm excreted from?
questions.rationale: The Cowper‘s gland secretions nourish the sperm.

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: What signifies the end of puberty for a male?
questions.rationale: Puberty ends for a male when mature sperm are formed by the testes.

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: How long does sperm remain viable in the female reproductive tract?
questions.rationale: Sperm can remain viable in the reproductive tract of the female for as long as 4 to 5 days.

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: The nurse encourages the members of a prenatal class to seriously consider breastfeeding. What does breast milk provide in addition to nourishment for the infant?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Stimulus for red blood cell production

questions.rationale: Breast milk provides maternal antibodies to the infant that give the child acquired immunity from some diseases for several months.

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: A female patient reports her menstrual cycle consistently occurs every 32 days. What day of her cycle can the woman anticipate ovulation?
questions.rationale: Ovulation occurs when a mature ovum is released from the follicle about 14 days before the onset of the next menstrual period.

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: The nurse conducting a sex education class for junior high students describes some cultural rites celebrating the entry to adulthood. What information would the nurse include? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Some cultures celebrate the entry to adulthood with rites such as displays of strength, bravery, self-reliance, and self-defense. Ritual circumcisions and bar and bat mitzvahs are also entry rites to adulthood. Lack of such rituals can sometimes confuse young people because there is no evidence of acceptance as an adult.

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: The nurse is reading a pregnant patient‘s history and physical. What information does the nurse recognize might indicate the need for a cesarean delivery? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Pelvic conditions that may predispose to a cesarean delivery are childhood rickets, pelvic fracture, and immobile coccyx.

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: What are considered to be functions of the fallopian tubes? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Passage for sperm to meet ova

choices.label: D
choices.text: Restriction for only one ovum to enter uterus

questions.rationale: The fallopian tube provides passage for both sperm and ova, offering an optimum place for fertilization and a safe environment for the zygote.

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: The nurse is providing an in-service to students beginning their obstetric clinical rotation. Using a diagram, the nurse points out parts of the female pelvis. What will the nurse include? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: The bones of the pelvis are two innominates, the sacrum, and the coccyx.

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: The nurse explains that testosterone is responsible for males exceeding females in which aspects? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Testosterone has the following effects not directly related to sexual reproduction: increases muscle mass and strength, promotes growth of long bones, increases basal metabolic rate, enhances production of red blood cells, produces enlargement of vocal cords, and affects the distribution of body hair. These effects result in greater strength and stature and a higher hematocrit level in males than in females.

questions.chapter_title: Human Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
questions.stem: A patient is being seen by her health care provider for a suspected vaginal infection. What will the nurse include when educating this patient on factors that affect the vaginal pH? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: The vagina is self-cleansing and during the reproductive years maintains a normal acidic pH of 4 to 5. The self-cleansing activity may be altered by antibiotic therapy, frequent douching, and excessive use of vaginal sprays, deodorant sanitary pads, or deodorant tampons.

questions.chapter_title: Fetal Development
questions.stem: What is the total number of chromosomes contained in a mature sperm or ovum?
questions.rationale: Gametes (sex cells) contain 23 chromosomes.

questions.chapter_title: Fetal Development
questions.stem: A pregnant woman states, “My husband hopes I will give him a boy because we have three girls.” What will the nurse explain to this woman?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The sex chromosome of the fertilized ovum determines the gender of the child.

choices.label: B
choices.text: When the sperm and ovum are united, there is a 75% chance the child will be a girl.

choices.label: C
choices.text: When the pH of the female reproductive tract is acidic, the child will be a girl.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ifa sperm carrying a Y chromosome fertilizes an ovum, then a boy is produced.

questions.rationale: When a Y-bearing sperm fertilizes an ovum, a male child is produced.

questions.chapter_title: Fetal Development
questions.stem: What is the most common site for fertilization?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Outer third of the fallopian tube near the ovary

choices.label: D
choices.text: Area of the fallopian tube farthest from the ovary

questions.rationale: Fertilization takes place in the outer third of the fallopian tube, which is closest to the ovary.

questions.chapter_title: Fetal Development
questions.stem: The embryo is termed a fetus at which stage of prenatal development?
questions.rationale: The fetus (third stage of prenatal development) begins at the ninth week and continues until the 40th week of gestation or until birth.

questions.chapter_title: Fetal Development
questions.stem: The nurse is reviewing fetal circulation with a pregnant patient and explains that blood circulates through the placenta to the fetus. What vessel(s) carry blood to the fetus?
questions.rationale: The umbilical vein transports richly oxygenated blood from the placenta to the fetus.

questions.chapter_title: Fetal Development
questions.stem: Where is the usual location for implantation of the zygote?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Upper section of the posterior uterine wall

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lower portion of the uterus near the cervical os

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inner third of the fallopian tube near the uterus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lateral aspect of the uterine wall

questions.rationale: The zygote usually implants in the upper section of the posterior uterine wall.

questions.chapter_title: Fetal Development
questions.stem: What is the embryonic membrane that contains fingerlike projections on its surface, which attach to the uterine wall?
questions.rationale: The chorion is a thick membrane with fingerlike projections (villi) on its outermost surface.

questions.chapter_title: Fetal Development
questions.stem: Which hormone is responsible for converting the endometrium into decidual cells for implantation?
questions.rationale: At high levels, progesterone maintains the endometrial lining for implantation of the zygote.

questions.chapter_title: Fetal Development
questions.stem: A pregnant patient asks the nurse when her infant‘s heart will begin to pump blood. What will the nurse reply?
questions.rationale: The fetal heart begins to pump by week 3 of gestation.

questions.chapter_title: Fetal Development
questions.stem: What organ does the ductus venosus shunt blood away from in fetal circulation?
questions.rationale: Fetal blood bypasses the liver through the ductus venosus by carrying blood directly to the inferior vena cava.

questions.chapter_title: Fetal Development
questions.stem: What complication can result from untreated respiratory distress in the newborn?
questions.rationale: Respiratory distress can cause increased pressure in the right ventricle, causing reopening of the foramen ovale.

questions.chapter_title: Fetal Development
questions.stem: During an ultrasound, two amnions and two placentas are observed. What will be the most likely result of this pregnancy?
questions.rationale: Dizygotic twins always have two amnions and two chorions (placentas).

questions.chapter_title: Fetal Development
questions.stem: A woman who is 25 weeks pregnant asks the nurse what her fetus looks like. What does the nurse explain is one physical characteristic present in a 25-week-old fetus?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Skin that is pink and smooth

questions.rationale: By 25 weeks, the body of the fetus is covered with lanugo, the eyes are open, the skin is wrinkled, and the fetus has definite periods of movement and sleeping.

questions.chapter_title: Fetal Development
questions.stem: At what point in prenatal development do the lungs begin to produce surfactant?
questions.rationale: During week 25, the alveoli begin to produce surfactant, which enables the alveoli to stay open for adequate lung oxygenation to occur.

questions.chapter_title: Fetal Development
questions.stem: A woman missed her menstrual period 1 week ago and has come to the doctor‘s office fora pregnancy test. Which placental hormone is measured in pregnancy tests?
questions.rationale: Human chorionic gonadotropin is the basis for most pregnancy tests. It is detectable in maternal blood as soon as implantation occurs, usually 7 to 9 days after fertilization.

questions.chapter_title: Fetal Development
questions.stem: When preparing to teach a class about prenatal development, the nurse would include information about folic acid supplementation. What is folic acid known to prevent?
questions.rationale: It is now known that folic acid supplements can prevent neural tube defects such as spina bifida.

questions.chapter_title: Fetal Development
questions.stem: The nurse is educating a class of expectant parents about fetal development. What is considered fetal age of viability?
questions.rationale: By 20 weeks of gestation, the lungs have matured enough for the fetus to survive outside the uterus (age of viability).

questions.chapter_title: Fetal Development
questions.stem: The nurse is presenting a conference on gene dominance. What does the nurse report as the percentage of children carrying the dominant gene if one parent has a dominant gene and the other parent does not?
questions.rationale: If one parent has a dominant trait and the other does not, then 50% of the children will inherit the trait.

questions.chapter_title: Fetal Development
questions.stem: The nurse explains that the birth weight of monozygotic twins is frequently below average. What is the most likely cause?
questions.rationale: The single placenta may not be able to provide adequate nutrition to two fetuses.

questions.chapter_title: Fetal Development
questions.stem: The school nurse is counseling a group of adolescent girls. What does the nurse explain about sperm ejaculated near the cervix?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They are destroyed by the acidic pH of the vagina.

choices.label: B
choices.text: They survive up to 5 days and can cause pregnancy.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They lose their motility in about 12 hours after intercourse.

choices.label: D
choices.text: They are usually pushed out of the vagina by the muscular action of the vaginal wall.

questions.rationale: Sperm ejaculated near the cervix can survive up to 5 days and cause pregnancy even before ovulation.

questions.chapter_title: Fetal Development
questions.stem: What does the nurse explain can affect the survival of the X- and Y-bearing sperm after intercourse?
questions.rationale: Estrogen levels and the pH of the female reproductive tract can affect the survival of the X- and Y-bearing sperm as well as their motility.

questions.chapter_title: Fetal Development
questions.stem: Of what is the normal umbilical cord comprised?

choices.label: A
choices.text: | artery carrying blood to the fetus and 1 vein carrying blood away from the fetus

choices.label: B
choices.text: 1 artery carrying blood to the fetus and 2 veins carrying blood away from the fetus

choices.label: C
choices.text: 2 arteries carrying blood away from the fetus and | vein carrying blood to the fetus

choices.label: D
choices.text: 2 arteries carrying blood to the fetus and 2 veins carrying blood away from the fetus

questions.rationale: The umbilical cord is comprised of 2 arteries carrying blood away from the fetus and 1 vein carrying blood to the fetus.

questions.chapter_title: Fetal Development
questions.stem: What part of the fetal body derives from the mesoderm?
questions.rationale: The mesoderm is responsible for the development of muscles. Nails and oil glands derive from the ectoderm. The lining of the bladder derives from the endoderm.

questions.chapter_title: Fetal Development
questions.stem: A couple just learned they are expecting their first child and are curious if they are having a boy ora girl. At what point of development can the couple first expect to see the sex of their child on ultrasound?
questions.rationale: The fetal period begins at the 10th week, and by the 10th week the external genitalia are visible to ultrasound examination.

questions.chapter_title: Fetal Development
questions.stem: A nurse is teaching a lesson on fetal development to a class of high school students and explains the primary germ layers. What are the germ layers? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: The zygote transforms its embryonic disc into three layers: the ectoderm, the mesoderm, and the endoderm.

questions.chapter_title: Fetal Development
questions.stem: What are the functions of amniotic fluid? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: D
choices.text: Acting as a reservoir for nutrients

choices.label: E
choices.text: Acting as a cushion for the fetus

questions.rationale: The amniotic fluid provides maintenance of even temperature; prevents amnion from adhering to fetal skin; allows buoyancy, symmetrical growth, and fetal movement; and acts as a cushion for the fetus. Although the fetus does swallow amniotic fluid, it has no nutritional value.

questions.chapter_title: Fetal Development
questions.stem: A patient at the obstetric office has just learned she is pregnant with dizygotic twins. What facts will the nurse include when educating this patient? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dizygotic twins are the same sex.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dizygotic pregnancies tend to repeat in families.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Dizygotic twin incidence decreases with maternal age.

questions.rationale: Dizygotic twins tend to repeat in families and have separate chorions. They can be the same sex or different sexes and have their own placenta. Incidence increases with maternal age.

questions.chapter_title: Fetal Development
questions.stem: The normal volume of amniotic fluid is approximately mL att 37 weeks‘ gestation.
questions.rationale: The volume of amniotic fluid steadily increases from about 30 mL at 10 weeks of pregnancy to 350 mL at 20 weeks. The volume of fluid is about 1000 mL at 37 weeks. In the latter part of pregnancy, the fetus may swallow up to 400 mL of amniotic fluid per day and normally excretes urine into the fluid.

questions.chapter_title: Prenatal Care and Adaptations to Pregnancy
questions.stem: A woman who is 7 weeks pregnant tells the nurse that this is not her first pregnancy. She has a 2-year-old son and had one previous spontaneous abortion. How would the nurse document the patient‘s obstetric history using the TPALM system?
questions.rationale: Refer to Box 4-1 in the textbook for the TPALM system of identifying gravida and para.

questions.chapter_title: Prenatal Care and Adaptations to Pregnancy
questions.stem: A woman calls her health care provider to schedule prenatal visits in an uncomplicated pregnancy. How frequently will the nurse assist the patient to schedule these appointments?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Every 3 weeks until the 6th month, then every 2 weeks until delivery

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every 4 weeks until the 7th month, after which appointments will become more frequent

choices.label: D
choices.text: Every 2 to 3 weeks for the entire pregnancy

questions.rationale: Monthly visits are scheduled up to 28 weeks, and then visits increase to every 2 weeks through 36 weeks. From 36 weeks until delivery, visits are weekly.

questions.chapter_title: Prenatal Care and Adaptations to Pregnancy
questions.stem: During the physical examination for the first prenatal visit, it is noted that Chadwick‘s sign is present. What is Chadwick‘s sign?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bluish or purplish discoloration of the vulva, vagina, and cervix

choices.label: C
choices.text: Darkening of the areola and breast tenderness

questions.rationale: Chadwick‘s sign is the purplish or bluish discoloration of the cervix, vulva and vagina.

questions.chapter_title: Prenatal Care and Adaptations to Pregnancy
questions.stem: After the examination is completed, the patient asks the nurse why Chadwick‘s signoccurs during pregnancy. What would the nurse explain as the cause of Chadwick‘s sign?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Vascular congestion in the pelvic area

questions.rationale: Chadwick‘s sign is caused by increased vascular congestion in the cervical and vaginal area.

questions.chapter_title: Prenatal Care and Adaptations to Pregnancy
questions.stem: The nurse has explained physiological changes that occur during pregnancy. Which statement indicates that the woman understands the information?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Blood pressure goes up toward the end of pregnancy.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “My breathing will get deeper and a little faster.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “T‘ll notice a decreased pigmentation in my skin.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “There will be a curvature in the upper spine area.”

questions.rationale: The pregnant woman breathes more deeply, and her respiratory rate may increase slightly.

questions.chapter_title: Prenatal Care and Adaptations to Pregnancy
questions.stem: A woman reports that her last normal menstrual period began on August 5, 2013. What is this woman‘s expected delivery date using Nagele‘s rule?
questions.rationale: To determine the expected date of delivery, count backward 3 months from the first day of the last menstrual period, then add 7 days and change the year if necessary.

questions.chapter_title: Prenatal Care and Adaptations to Pregnancy
questions.stem: During the second prenatal visit, the nurse attempts to locate the fetal heartbeat with an electronic Doppler device. How early might fetal heart tones be detected with an electronic Doppler device?
questions.rationale: The fetal heartbeat can be detected as early as 10 weeks of pregnancy using a Doppler device.

questions.chapter_title: Prenatal Care and Adaptations to Pregnancy
questions.stem: Ina routine prenatal visit, the nurse examining a patient who is 37 weeks pregnant notices that the fetal heart rate (FHR) has dropped to 120 beats/minute from a rate of 160 beats/minute earlier in the pregnancy. What is the nurse‘s first action?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ask if the patient has taken a sedative.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Turn the patient to her right side.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Record the rate as a normal finding.

questions.rationale: The FHR at term ranges from a low of 110 to 120 beats/minute to a high of 150 to 160 beats/minute. This should be recorded as normal. The FHR drops in the late stages of pregnancy.

questions.chapter_title: Prenatal Care and Adaptations to Pregnancy
questions.stem: A woman‘s prepregnant weight is determined to be average for her height. What will the nurse advise the woman regarding recommended weight gain during pregnancy?
questions.rationale: The recommended weight gain for a woman of normal weight before pregnancy is 25 to 35 pounds.

questions.chapter_title: Prenatal Care and Adaptations to Pregnancy
questions.stem: When the nurse tells a pregnant woman that she needs 1200 mg of calcium daily during pregnancy, the woman responds, “I don‘t like milk.” What dietary adjustments could the nurse recommend?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Choose more fresh fruits, particularly citrus fruits.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Include molasses and whole-grain breads in the diet.

questions.rationale: For women who do not like milk, other sources of calcium include enriched cereals, legumes, nuts, dried fruits, green leafy vegetables, and canned salmon and sardines that contain bones.

questions.chapter_title: Prenatal Care and Adaptations to Pregnancy
questions.stem: A pregnant woman is experiencing nausea in the early morning. What recommendations would the nurse offer to alleviate this symptom?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Eat three well-balanced meals per day and limit snacks.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Drink a full glass of fluid at the beginning of each meal.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Have crackers handy at the bedside, and eat a few before getting out of bed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Eat a bland diet and avoid concentrated sweets.

questions.rationale: The nurse can recommend eating dry toast or crackers before getting out of bed in the morning to alleviate nausea during pregnancy.

questions.chapter_title: Prenatal Care and Adaptations to Pregnancy
questions.stem: The patient who is 28 weeks pregnant shows a 10-pound weight gain from 2 weeks ago. What is the nurse‘s initial action?
questions.rationale: The marked weight gain may be an indication of pre-eclampsia. The blood pressure should be assessed before notifying the physician.

questions.chapter_title: Prenatal Care and Adaptations to Pregnancy
questions.stem: The patient remarks that she has heard some foods will enhance brain development of the fetus. The nurse replies that foods high in docosahexaenoic acid—omega 3 fatty acid (DHA) are thought to enhance brain development. What food can the nurse recommend?
questions.rationale: Foods rich in DHA are red meat, flounder, halibut, and soybean and canola oil. Frying fish negatively alters the DHA.

questions.chapter_title: Prenatal Care and Adaptations to Pregnancy
questions.stem: The nurse encourages adequate intake of folic acid for women of childbearing age before and during pregnancy. What is folic acid thought to decrease the incidence of in fetal development?
questions.rationale: Folic acid can reduce the incidence of neural tube defects such as spina bifida and anencephaly.

questions.chapter_title: Prenatal Care and Adaptations to Pregnancy
questions.stem: A woman tells the nurse that she is quite sure she is pregnant. The nurse recognizes which as a positive sign of pregnancy?
questions.rationale: Positive indications are caused only by the developing fetus and include fetal heart activity, visualization by ultrasound, and fetal movements felt by the examiner.

questions.chapter_title: Prenatal Care and Adaptations to Pregnancy
questions.stem: At her initial prenatal visit, a woman asks, “When can I hear the baby‘s heartbeat?” At what gestational age can the fetal heartbeat be auscultated with a specially adapted stethoscope or fetoscope?
questions.rationale: The fetal heartbeat can be heard with a fetoscope between the 18th and 20th weeks of pregnancy.

questions.chapter_title: Prenatal Care and Adaptations to Pregnancy
questions.stem: A woman pregnant for the first time asks the nurse, “When will I begin to feel the baby move?” What is the nurse‘s best response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “You may notice the baby moving around the 4th or Sth month.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “You'll feel something by the end of the first trimester.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “The baby will be big enough for you to feel in your 8th month.”

questions.rationale: Quickening, fetal movement felt by the mother, is first perceived at 16 to 20 weeks of gestation.

questions.chapter_title: Prenatal Care and Adaptations to Pregnancy
questions.stem: A pregnant woman inquires about exercising during pregnancy. What information should the nurse include when planning to educate this woman?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Exercise elevates the mother‘s temperature and improves fetal circulation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Exercise increases catecholamines, which can prevent preterm labor.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A regular schedule of moderate exercise during pregnancy is beneficial.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pregnant women should limit water intake during exercise.

questions.rationale: In general, moderate exercise several times a week, from the 8th week through delivery, is advised during pregnancy.

questions.chapter_title: Prenatal Care and Adaptations to Pregnancy
questions.stem: An ultrasound confirms that a 16-year-old girl is pregnant. How does the need for prenatal care and counseling for adolescents differ from other age populations?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A pregnant adolescent is experiencing two major life transitions at the same time.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Adolescents who get pregnant are more likely to have other chronic health problems.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Adolescents are at greater risk for multifetal pregnancies.

choices.label: D
choices.text: At this age, a pregnant adolescent will accept the nurse‘s advice.

questions.rationale: The pregnant adolescent must cope with two of life‘s most stress-laden transitions simultaneously: adolescence and parenthood.

questions.chapter_title: Prenatal Care and Adaptations to Pregnancy
questions.stem: At what age is a woman who becomes pregnant for the first time described as an “elderly primip”?
questions.rationale: A woman over the age of 35 who becomes pregnant for the first time is described as an “elderly primip.”

questions.chapter_title: Prenatal Care and Adaptations to Pregnancy
questions.stem: The nurse explains that the softening of the cervix and vagina is a probable sign of pregnancy. What is the appropriate term for this sign?
questions.rationale: Goodell‘s sign is one of the probable signs of pregnancy and describes a softened cervix and vagina.

questions.chapter_title: Prenatal Care and Adaptations to Pregnancy
questions.stem: When obtaining a prenatal history on a pregnant patient the nurse notes a family history of sickle cell disease. Given this information, what lab test can the nurse anticipate the physician will order?
questions.rationale: Hemoglobin electrophoresis identifies the presence of sickle cell trait or disease (in women of African or Mediterranean descent). It is ordered in the first trimester, if indicated.

questions.chapter_title: Prenatal Care and Adaptations to Pregnancy
questions.stem: A pregnant woman is attending her second prenatal visit. Prenatal lab work indicates she is not immune to the rubella virus. What is the most appropriate nursing intervention?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Provide the rubella vaccine as ordered by the physician immediately.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inform the woman she should receive the vaccine in the hospital after delivery.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hold all immunizations until 1 month postpartum.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Encourage the patient to decide whether or not to get the rubella vaccine prenatally.

questions.rationale: The rubella vaccine is contraindicated during pregnancy. A woman should be instructed to avoid pregnancy for at least 1 month following rubella immunization. It is not necessary to hold all immunizations until 1 month postpartum.

questions.chapter_title: Prenatal Care and Adaptations to Pregnancy
questions.stem: A woman who is 37 weeks pregnant reports feeling dizzy when lying on her back. What does the nurse explain as the most likely cause of this symptom?
questions.rationale: Supine hypotension syndrome, also called aortocaval compression or vena cava syndrome, may occur if the woman lies on her back. Symptoms of supine hypotension syndrome include faintness, lightheadedness, dizziness, and agitation.

questions.chapter_title: Prenatal Care and Adaptations to Pregnancy
questions.stem: A woman who is 36 weeks pregnant tells the nurse she plans to take a 12-hour flight to Hawaii. What would the nurse recommend that the patient do during the flight? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Wear tight-fitting clothing to promote venous return.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Eat a large meal before boarding the flight.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Request a seat with greater leg room.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Drink at least 4 ounces of water every hour.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Get up and walk around the plane frequently.

questions.rationale: Because of the increase in clotting potential, the pregnant patient is prone to a thromboembolism. Adequate hydration, frequent position changes, and movement decrease the risk.

questions.chapter_title: Prenatal Care and Adaptations to Pregnancy
questions.stem: The nurse cautions the patient that, because of hormonal changes in late pregnancy, the pelvic joints relax. What does this result in? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: A waddling gait and joint instability are the only signs that relate to joint changes. The other discomforts are related to the enlarging uterus with its attendant weight.

questions.chapter_title: Prenatal Care and Adaptations to Pregnancy
questions.stem: The nurse assesses the progress from the announcement stage of fatherhood to the acceptance stage when the patient reports which actions by the father? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: C
choices.text: Spends leisure time with his friends.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Traded his sports car for a sedan.

questions.rationale: Active planning for an infant is an indication of the acceptance stage. Concentration on a hobby and spending time away from home are indicators of nonacceptance.

questions.chapter_title: Prenatal Care and Adaptations to Pregnancy
questions.stem: What nursing interventions are appropriate for the prenatal patient in terms of prenatal care? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Nutritional counseling, reinforcing and discussing the responsibility of parenthood, reducing risk factors for the pregnant woman and the fetus, and improving health practices are all goals of prenatal care.

questions.chapter_title: Prenatal Care and Adaptations to Pregnancy
questions.stem: The nurse recognizes which behavior characteristic(s) of women in their first trimester of pregnancy? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Showing off photos, feeling ambivalence about the pregnancy, fragile emotions, and fatigue and sleepiness are all characteristic of behaviors seen in the first trimester. Women are not focused on their infant; they are focused on themselves and the physical changes they are experiencing.

questions.chapter_title: Prenatal Care and Adaptations to Pregnancy
questions.stem: The nurse reminds the prenatal patient that she should add. kcal to her daily intake to nourish the fetus.
questions.rationale: The recommended dietary intake increase is 300 kcal a day.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: A pregnant patient tells the nurse that she has been nauseated and vomiting. How will the nurse explain that hyperemesis gravidarum is distinguished from morning sickness?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hyperemesis gravidarum usually lasts for the duration of the pregnancy.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hyperemesis gravidarum causes dehydration and electrolyte imbalances.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sensitivity to smells is usually the cause of vomiting in hyperemesis gravidarum.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The woman with hyperemesis gravidarum will have persistent vomiting without weight loss.

questions.rationale: Dehydration and electrolyte imbalances result from persistent nausea and vomiting associated with hyperemesis gravidarum. Dehydration impairs the perfusion to the placenta.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: A woman is 9 weeks pregnant and experiencing heavy bleeding and cramping. She reports passing some tissue. Cervical dilation is noted on examination. What is the most likelycause of these symptoms?
questions.rationale: Signs and symptoms of an incomplete abortion are similar to those of an inevitable abortion, but some tissue is passed.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: The nurse finds a woman crying after she has undergone a dilation and evacuation (D&E) for a missed abortion. What is the most appropriate statement by the nurse?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “There is usually something wrong with the fetus when this happens early in pregnancy.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Now there. You can try to conceive on your next cycle.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “I‘m here if you need to talk.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “You are young and strong. I know you can have a healthy pregnancy.”

questions.rationale: An effective technique when communicating with a woman experiencing pregnancy loss is to say, “I‘m here if you need to talk.” The nurse listens and acknowledges the woman‘s grief.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: A woman who is 8 weeks pregnant becomes concerned when she has light vaginal bleeding accompanied by abdominal pain. An ectopic pregnancy is confirmed by ultrasound. Which statement indicates that the woman understands the explanation of an ectopic pregnancy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “The chorionic villi develop vesicles within the uterus.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “The placenta develops in the lower part of the uterus.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “The fetus dies in the uterus during the first half of the pregnancy.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “The embryo is implanted in the fallopian tube.”

questions.rationale: Ectopic pregnancy occurs when the fertilized ovum is implanted outside of the uterine cavity.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: An ultrasound on a woman who is 32 weeks pregnant reveals the placenta implanted over the entire cervical os. What does the nurse understand best describes this condition?
questions.rationale: A total placenta previa describes a condition in which the placenta completely covers the cervical opening.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: What symptom presented by a pregnant women is indicative of abruptio placentae?
questions.rationale: Bleeding accompanied by abdominal or lower back pain is a typical manifestation of abruptio placentae.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: What situation would concern the nurse about the presence of Rh incompatibility?
questions.rationale: Rh incompatibility can occur only if the mother is Rh negative and the fetus is Rh positive.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: A primigravida in her first trimester is Rh negative. What will this woman receive to prevent anti-Rh antibodies from forming?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Rhimmune globulin at 28 weeks and within 72 hours after the birth of an Rh-positive infant

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rh immune globulin now and again in the last trimester

questions.rationale: An Rh-negative woman would receive Rh immune globulin at 28 weeks of gestation and within 72 hours after the birth of an Rh-positive infant or abortion.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: A woman seeking prenatal care relates a history of macrosomic infants, two stillbirths, and polyhydramnios with each pregnancy. What does the nurse recognize these factors highly suggest?
questions.rationale: Large (macrosomic) infants over 9 pounds are linked to gestational diabetes.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: A nurse is providing prenatal education. The nurse will explain that pregnancy affects glucose metabolism in what way?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Placental hormones increase the resistance of cells to insulin.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Insulin cells cannot meet the body‘s demands as the woman‘s weight increases.

choices.label: C
choices.text: There is a decreased production of insulin during pregnancy.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The speed of insulin breakdown is decreased during pregnancy.

questions.rationale: Hormones and enzymes produced by the placenta increase the resistance of cells to insulin.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: Why does the woman taking oral hypoglycemic agents to control diabetes mellitus need to take insulin during pregnancy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Insulin can cross the placental barrier to the fetus.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Insulin does not cross the placental barrier to the fetus.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oral agents do not cross the placenta.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral agents are not sufficient to meet maternal insulin needs.

questions.rationale: Oral hypoglycemic agents are not used during pregnancy, because they can cross the placenta, possibly resulting in fetal birth defects or hypoglycemia.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: A pregnant woman comes to the clinic stating that she has been exposed to hepatitis B. She is afraid that her infant will also contract hepatitis B. What will the nurse explain to this woman?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The infant will be given a single dose of hepatitis immune globulin after birth.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The infant will be able to use the antibodies from the immunizations given to the patient before delivery.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The infant will not have hepatitis B because the virus does not pass through the placental barrier.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The infant will be immune to hepatitis B because of the mother‘s infection.

questions.rationale: The infant will be given immune globulin immediately after birth for temporary immunity followed by hepatitis B vaccine. Immunization is not recommended for women who are pregnant.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: What will the nurse begin with when asking a patient about drug use during a prenatal history?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Do you smoke, drink alcohol, or use drugs?”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Do you ever use prescription or street drugs?”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “What over-the-counter and prescription drugs have you taken in the past 3 months?”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “We need to know if you take drugs so we can help your baby.”

questions.rationale: Screening for drug use should begin in a nonthreatening way by asking about prescription and OTC medications and how the information can help provide safe and appropriate prenatal care.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: The nurse assesses a pregnant woman for pregnancy-induced hypertension. What is the first sign of fluid retention suggestive of this complication?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Swelling of the feet and ankles

questions.rationale: Sudden, excessive weight gain is the first sign of fluid retention; facial swelling and swelling of the feet, legs, and hands follow weight gain.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: A patient with gestational hypertension is exhibiting all of the signs below. What should the nurse report immediately?
questions.rationale: Visual disturbances indicate worsening pregnancy-induced hypertension and must be reported promptly for effective intervention to prevent preeclampsia and convulsion.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: A patient who is 28 weeks pregnant presents with consistent hypertension. What need would the home health nurse make the first priority?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased fluid intake to ensure adequate hydration

choices.label: D
choices.text: Instruction about the effect of diuretics

questions.rationale: Bed rest reduces the flow of blood to skeletal muscles, making more blood available to the placenta and enhancing fetal oxygenation.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: The nurse is caring for a pregnant woman diagnosed with preeclampsia. What will the nurse explain is the objective of magnesium sulfate therapy for this patient?

choices.label: D
choices.text: To act as a saline cathartic

questions.rationale: Magnesium sulfate is a central nervous system depressant given to prevent seizures. Distribution of this document is illegal extra per year? ius

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: The nurse is caring for a pregnant woman receiving an intravenous infusion with magnesium sulfate. What is the highest priority nursing intervention?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Count respirations and report a rate of less than 12 breaths/minute.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Count respirations and report a rate of more than 20 breaths/minute.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Check blood pressure and report a rate of less than 100/60 mm Hg.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Monitor urinary output and report a rate of less than 100 mL/hr.

questions.rationale: Excessive magnesium sulfate may cause respiratory depression.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: What drug will the nurse plan to have available for immediate IV administration whenever magnesium sulfate is administered to a maternity patient?
questions.rationale: Calcium gluconate reverses the effects of magnesium sulfate and should be available for immediate use when a woman receives magnesium sulfate.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: A woman who is 35 weeks pregnant has a total placenta previa. She asks the nurse, “Will I be able to deliver vaginally?” What explanation by the nurse is the most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Yes, you can deliver vaginally until 36 weeks.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “A vaginal delivery can be attempted, but if bleeding occurs, a cesarean section will be done.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “A cesarean section is performed when the mother has a total placenta previa.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “There is no reason why you cannot have a vaginal delivery.”

questions.rationale: A cesarean delivery is done for a partial or total placenta previa.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: The nurse teaches a woman who is 8 weeks pregnant about how rubella can affect the developing fetus. What can result from maternal rubella during pregnancy?
questions.rationale: Rubella can have devastating effects on the developing fetus. Some effects of rubella on the embryo or fetus include microcephaly, mental retardation, cardiac defects, cataracts, and deafness.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: What symptom reported by a pregnant patient would lead the nurse to suspect pyelonephritis?
questions.rationale: Pyelonephritis is a particularly serious infection in pregnancy. Signs and symptoms include high fever, chills, flank pain or tenderness, nausea, and vomiting.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: The nurse is caring for a prenatal patient diagnosed with a placenta previa. What is the best position for this patient?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Flat on her back with knees flexed to help prevent hemorrhage

choices.label: B
choices.text: On her side to prevent supine hypotension

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inthe semi-Fowler‘s position to prevent supine hypotension

choices.label: D
choices.text: In the knee-chest position to reduce pressure on the placenta

questions.rationale: The prenatal patient with placenta previa is best placed on her side with a pillow for support. This position not only reduces stress on the placenta but also reduces the possibility of supine hypotension.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: The young prenatal patient with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) says, “I am frightened that I will have to deal with insulin injections for the rest of my life.” What is the best response by the nurse?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “After delivery your doctor will prescribe oral hypoglycemic medication to control your disease. Pills are so much simpler than insulin injections.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “After a while those insulin injections won‘t seem so bad.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Tt will most likely resolve 6 weeks or so after the baby is born.”

questions.rationale: GDM usually resolves by 6 weeks after delivery.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: The nurse is preparing a pregnant patient for an abdominal ultrasound at 8 weeks‘ gestation. What intervention will the nurse implement before this diagnostic test?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Instruct the patient to take nothing by mouth after midnight the night before the test.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Encourage the patient to drink 1 to 2 quarts of water before the test.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Instruct the patient to remove all jewelry.

questions.rationale: Ultrasound uses high-frequency sound waves to visualize structures within the body; the examination may use a transvaginal probe or an abdominal transducer; abdominal ultrasound during early pregnancy requires a full bladder for proper visualization (have the woman drink 1 to 2 quarts of water before the examination).

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: The nurse is caring for a macrosomic newborn of a diabetic patient. What complications will the nurse assess for in the newborn?
questions.rationale: The fetus responds to the hyperglycemia from the mother‘s blood and produces increased insulin. This insulin may cause hypoglycemia in the infant after it is no longer exposed to the mother‘s blood.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: The nurse educates prenatal patients about the threat of TORCH infections. Which infections are included in this classification? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: The TORCH infections are toxoplasmosis, rubella, cytomegalovirus, and herpes simplex.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: The nurse emphasizes to a patient with a high-risk pregnancy that the impact of such a pregnancy might result in which problems? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: High-risk pregnancies may produce problems such as disruption of family roles, financial pressures, delayed attachment to the infant, alteration in child care practices, and frustration with activity restriction.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: A patient who is 30 weeks pregnant delivers a stillborn child in the emergency department (ED). What should the ED nurse offer the patient? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: B
choices.text: An opportunity to hold the infant

choices.label: D
choices.text: A memento (footprint or lock of hair)

questions.rationale: The patient should be offered privacy, an opportunity to hold the infant, support group information, and a memento. A warm beverage is not a priority at this time.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: What would the nurse include in a teaching plan for the pregnant patient who has iron deficiency anemia and has been placed on iron supplements? (Se/ect all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Citrus fruits enhance absorption of iron.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Milk will disguise the taste of the iron.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The iron therapy will continue for about 3 months.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tea should be avoided while taking iron.

questions.rationale: Calcium, bran, and milk interfere with the absorption of iron. Vitamin C helps with the absorption of iron, the therapy usually lasts 3 months, and the tannic acid in tea does interfere with the absorption of iron.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: The nurse takes into consideration that the patient with placenta previa is at risk for postpartum infection for what reasons? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Vaginal organisms can invade the placenta.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The amniotic fluid can become infected.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The placenta is an excellent growth medium.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The misplaced placenta weakens the uterine wall.

questions.rationale: Vaginal organisms reach the placenta through the cervix. Once there, the organisms can multiply in the nutrient-rich environment of the placenta. The weak musculature of the lower segment of the uterus will cause postpartum hemorrhage rather than infection.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: The nurse is obtaining history and physical information on a new patient attending her first prenatal visit. After recording current height, weight, and BMI, it is determined that the patient is obese. What complications related to obesity will the nurse assess this patient for during pregnancy? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: The obese woman who is pregnant has a high risk for developing complications during pregnancy such as gestational diabetes, hypertension, cardiac problems, pre-eclampsia, and respiratory problems.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Pregnancy
questions.stem: A woman, gravida 3, para 2, is attending her fourth prenatal visit and confides in the nurse that she is battered by her husband. She is assessed to have multiple bruises at various stages of healing. What nursing actions are appropriate for the nurse to implement? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Tell the husband that authorities will be notified immediately.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Determine if children are being hurt.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Determine factors that increase the risk of injury.

questions.rationale: The woman being assessed for abuse is taken to a private area. The nurse determines whether there are factors that increase the risk for severe injuries or homicide, such as drug use by the abuser, a gun in the house, prior use of a weapon, or violent behavior by the abuser outside the home. The nurse also determines whether children are being hurt. It is vital that the abuser not find out that the woman has reported the abuse or that she intends to leave.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: What does the nurse note when measuring the frequency of a laboring woman‘s contractions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: How long the patient states the contractions last

choices.label: B
choices.text: The time between the end of one contraction and the beginning of the next

choices.label: C
choices.text: The time between the beginning and the end of one contraction

choices.label: D
choices.text: The time between the beginning of one contraction and the beginning of the next

questions.rationale: The frequency of contractions is the elapsed time from the beginning of one contraction to the beginning of the next contraction.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Why is the relaxation phase between contractions important?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The laboring woman needs to rest.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The uterine muscles fatigue without relaxation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The contractions can interfere with fetal oxygenation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The infant progresses toward delivery at these times.

questions.rationale: Blood flow from the mother into the placenta gradually decreases during contractions. During the interval between contractions, the placenta refills with oxygenated blood for the fetus.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: What contraction duration and interval does the nurse recognize could result in fetal compromise?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Duration shorter than 30 seconds, interval longer than 75 seconds

choices.label: B
choices.text: Duration shorter than 90 seconds, interval longer than 120 seconds

choices.label: C
choices.text: Duration longer than 90 seconds, interval shorter than 60 seconds

choices.label: D
choices.text: Duration longer than 60 seconds, interval shorter than 90 seconds

questions.rationale: Persistent contraction durations longer than 90 seconds or contraction intervals less than 60 seconds may reduce fetal oxygen supply.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Vaginal examination reveals the presenting part is the infant‘s head, which is well flexed on the chest. What is this presentation?
