questions.rationale: In the vertex presentation, the fetal head is the presenting part. The head is fully flexed on the chest.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: What does meconium-stained amniotic fluid indicate when the infant is in a vertex presentation?
questions.rationale: Green-stained amniotic fluid means that the fetus passed the first stool before birth, and it is an indicator of fetal compromise.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Itis determined that the presenting part of the fetus is the buttocks. At delivery the fetus‘ships are flexed and the knees are extended. How would the nurse record this presentation?
questions.rationale: When a fetus presents in a frank breech position, the legs are flexed at the hips and extend toward the shoulders.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Ata prenatal visit, a primigravida asks the nurse how she will know her labor has started. The nurse knows that what indicates the beginning of true labor?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Contractions that are relieved by walking

choices.label: B
choices.text: Discomfort in the abdomen and groin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Regular contractions becoming more frequent and intense

questions.rationale: In true labor, contractions gradually develop a regular pattern and become more frequent, longer, and more intense.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: While discussing labor and delivery during a prenatal visit, a primigravida asks the nurse when she should go to the hospital. What is the nurse‘s most informative response?
questions.rationale: Ruptured membranes are an indication that the woman should go to the hospital or birthing center.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: The nurse is caring for a woman in the first stage of labor. What will the nurse remind the patient about contractions during this stage of labor?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They get the infant positioned for delivery.

choices.label: B
choices.text: They push the infant into the vagina.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They dilate and efface the cervix.

choices.label: D
choices.text: They get the mother prepared for true labor.

questions.rationale: The first stage of labor describes the time from the onset of labor until full dilation of the cervix.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A woman is 7 cm dilated, and her contractions are 3 minutes apart. When she begins cursing at her birthing coach and the nurse, what does the nurse assess as the most likely explanation for the woman‘s change in behavior?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Labor has progressed to the transition phase.

choices.label: B
choices.text: She lacked adequate preparation for the labor experience.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The woman would benefit from a different form of analgesia.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The contractions have increased from mild to moderate intensity.

questions.rationale: Ifa woman suddenly loses control and becomes irritable, suspect that she has progressed to the transition stage of labor.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: What is the function of contractions during the second stage of labor?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Align the infant into the proper position for delivery.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Push the infant out of the mother‘s body.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Separate the placenta from the uterine wall.

questions.rationale: The contractions push the infant out of the mother‘s body as the second stage of labor ends with the birth of the infant.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: What marks the end of the third stage of labor?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Expulsion of the placenta and membranes

questions.rationale: The third stage of labor extends from the birth of the infant until the placenta is detached and expelled.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Why should the nurse encourage the mother to void during the fourth stage of labor?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A full bladder could interfere with cervical dilation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A full bladder could obstruct progress of the infant through the birth canal.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A full bladder could obstruct the passage of the placenta.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A full bladder could predispose the mother to uterine hemorrhage.

questions.rationale: A full bladder immediately after birth can cause excessive bleeding because it pushes the uterus upward and interferes with contractions.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: The nurse observes the patient bearing down with contractions and crying out, “The baby is coming!” What is the best nursing intervention?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Stay with the woman and use the call bell to get help.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Send the woman‘s partner to locate a registered nurse.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Assist with deep breathing to slow the labor process.

questions.rationale: If birth appears to be imminent, the nurse should not leave the woman and should summon help with the call bell.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: The nurse observes on the fetal monitor a pattern of a 15-beat increase in the fetal heart rate that lasts 15 to 20 seconds. What does this pattern indicate?
questions.rationale: Accelerations in the fetal heart rate suggest that the fetus is well oxygenated.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: What is the most appropriate statement from the nurse when coaching the laboring woman with a fully dilated cervix to push?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “At the beginning ofa contraction, hold your breath and push for 10 seconds.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Take a deep breath and push between contractions.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Begin pushing when a contraction starts and continue for the duration of the contraction.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “At the beginning of a contraction, take two deep breaths and push with the second exhalation.”

questions.rationale: When the cervix is fully dilated, the woman should take a deep breath and exhale at the beginning of a contraction, and then take another deep breath and push while exhaling.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: What is the most important nursing intervention during the fourth stage of labor?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Monitor the frequency and intensity of contractions.

questions.rationale: Immediately after giving birth, every woman is assessed for signs of hemorrhage.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: One hour postdelivery the nurse notes the new mother has saturated three perineal pads. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Check the fundus for position and firmness.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Change the pads and chart the time.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Time how long it takes to soak one pad.

questions.rationale: Increased lochia may indicate hemorrhage. The fundus should be assessed for firmness. One pad an hour is an acceptable rate for immediate postdelivery.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: While caring for a laboring woman, the nurse notices a pattern of variable decelerations in fetal heart rate with uterine contractions. What is the nurse‘s initial action?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reposition the woman on her side.

questions.rationale: Repositioning the woman is the first response to a pattern of variable decelerations. If the decelerations continue, then oxygen should be administered and/or the flow rate of oxygen should be increased.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: How should the nurse intervene to relieve perineal bruising and edema following delivery?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Place an ice pack on the area for 12 hours.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Place a warm pack on the perineal area for 24 hours.

questions.rationale: An ice pack can be placed on the mother‘s perineum to reduce bruising and edema for 12 hours followed by a warm pack after the first 12 to 24 hours after delivery.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: At 1 and 5 minutes of life, a newborn‘s Apgar score is 9. What does the nurse understand that a score of 9 indicates?

choices.label: B
choices.text: The newborn may have physical disabilities.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The newborn will have above average intelligence.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The newborn is in stable condition.

questions.rationale: Apgar scoring is a system for evaluating the infant‘s need for resuscitation at birth. Five categories are evaluated on a scale from 0 to 2, with the highest score being 10. A score of 9 indicates that the newborn is stable.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A nursing student assisting a woman in labor asks the instructor, “What does it mean when the baby is at minus | station?” After being given an explanation by the nursing instructor, what statement by the student indicates an accurate understanding of station?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Fetal head is above the ischial spines.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Fetal head is below the ischial spines.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Fetal head is engaged in the mother‘s pelvis.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Fetal head is visible at the perineum.”

questions.rationale: Station describes the level of the presenting part in the pelvis. It is estimated in centimeters from the level of the ischial spines. Minus stations are above the ischial spines.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: The nurse formulates a nursing diagnosis for a woman in the fourth stage of labor. What is the most appropriate nursing diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Pain related to increasing frequency and intensity of contractions

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fear related to the probable need for cesarean delivery

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dysuria related to prolonged labor and decreased intake

choices.label: D
choices.text: Risk for injury related to hemorrhage

questions.rationale: In the fourth stage of labor, a priority nursing action is identifying and preventing hemorrhage.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: The nurse is caring for a patient who is not certain if she is in true labor. How might the nurse attempt to stimulate cervical effacement and intensify contractions in the patient?

choices.label: A
choices.text: By offering the patient warm fluids to drink

choices.label: B
choices.text: By helping the patient to ambulate in the room

choices.label: C
choices.text: By seating the patient upright in a straight-back chair

choices.label: D
choices.text: By positioning the patient on her right side

questions.rationale: Ambulation will stimulate effacement and intensify contractions if the patient is in true labor.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: What is the best nursing action to implement when late decelerations occur?
questions.rationale: The major objective of care for late decelerations is to increase maternal oxygen. IV fluids are increased to increase placental perfusion, oxytocin drips are stopped, and the patient is positioned to prevent supine hypotension.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: What is the nurse primarily concerned about maintaining in the initial care of the newborn?
questions.rationale: Thermoregulation is necessary to keep heat loss minimal and oxygen consumption low. Hypothermia can cause cold stress, which leads to hypoxia.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A pregnant woman, gravida 2, para 1, tells the nurse she desires a VBAC (vaginal birth after cesarean section) with this pregnancy. What is the primary concern regarding complications for this patient during labor and birth?
questions.rationale: Nursing care for women who plan to have a VBAC is similar to that for women who have had no cesarean births. The main concern is that the uterine scar will rupture, which can disrupt the placental blood flow and cause hemorrhage. Observation for signs of uterine rupture should be part of the nursing care for all laboring women, regardless of whether they have had a previous cesarean birth.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: The physician performs an amniotomy on a laboring woman. What will be the nurse‘s priority assessment immediately following this procedure?
questions.rationale: The FHR should be assessed for at least 1 full minute after the membranes rupture and must be recorded and reported. Marked slowing of the rate or variable decelerations suggests that the fetal umbilical cord may have descended with the fluid gush and is being compressed. Fluid amount should be assessed and recorded but is not the top priority. Maternal blood pressure and deep tendon reflexes are not appropriate assessments following rupture of membranes.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: While caring for an Arab woman in labor, the nurse should provide cultural sensitivity through which interventions? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: C
choices.text: Arrange for the husband/partner to participate in labor.

questions.rationale: Arab women are extremely modest, usually have a low pain tolerance, and wear various protective and religious amulets. The husband is in attendance but not as a participant. Arabs prefer female caregivers. If a male is in attendance, then the husband will remain in the room as long as the male is there.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: What are the advantages of a freestanding birth center? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Advantages of a freestanding birth center include a homelike setting and lower costs, because the center does not require expensive departments such as emergency or critical care. Freestanding birth centers are not designed for high-risk patients, are not attended by certified obstetricians, and do not have immediate emergency access.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: What do late decelerations indicate? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: This nonreassuring pattern indicates uteroplacental insufficiency and fetal heart compression. Prolonged decelerations indicate cord compression and early decelerations indicate head compressions.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Mother and Infant During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A pregnant woman arrives at the emergency department (ED) and reports she is in labor. After a thorough examination and diagnostic testing, it is determined to be false (prodromal) labor. What signs and symptoms would lead the nurse to suspect false (prodromal) labor? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Painless tightening of abdominal muscles (Braxton Hicks contractions) and cervix thick and not effaced lend to the determination of false (prodromal) labor. Leaking of vaginal fluid may indicate rupture of membranes and is a sign of true labor. Contractions that intensify with ambulation and pink spotting (bloody show) are signs of true labor.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A nurse is teaching a childbirth preparation class. The group is discussing individual expression of labor pain. What statement is accurate about a patient‘s expression of pain?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It reduces the patient‘s perception of pain.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is intensified by the vertex position of the fetus.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It can be completely controlled by nonpharmacological techniques.

questions.rationale: Culture influences how women feel about birth and what is an acceptable response to pain.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: What chemical substance(s) produced in the body acts as a natural pain reliever?
questions.rationale: Endorphins are natural body substances that are similar to morphine and may explain why laboring women need smaller doses of analgesia.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A nurse instructs a woman‘s labor coach to comfort her by firmly pressing on her lower back. What is this technique?
questions.rationale: Sacral pressure refers to firm pressure against the lower back to relieve some of the pain of back labor.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A woman who is 6 cm dilated has the urge to push. What will the nurse instruct the woman to do during the contraction?
questions.rationale: Ifa laboring woman feels the urge to push before the cervix is fully dilated, then she is taught to blow in short breaths to avoid bearing down.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Several hours into labor, a woman complains of dizziness, numbness, and tingling of her hands and mouth. What does the nurse recognize these symptoms signify?
questions.rationale: Hyperventilation is sometimes a problem if a woman is breathing rapidly.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: What is the most appropriate nursing action to take when a laboring woman hyperventilates?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Help her breathe into her cupped hands.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Place her flat on her back.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Initiate oxygen at 2 liters via mask.

questions.rationale: Measures to combat hyperventilation include breathing into cupped hands or a paper bag or holding breath for a few seconds. All of these techniques decrease PCO?.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A woman in the transition phase of labor requests a narcotic analgesic medication for pain relief. What should the nurse explain regarding giving a narcotic analgesic medication at this stage of labor?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It can cause medication given at later stages to be ineffective.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It will have no complications for the mother or infant.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It may result in respiratory depression to the newborn.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It will speed up labor and increase pain.

questions.rationale: The risk of narcotic analgesics is that they cross the placenta and can cause fetal respiratory depression.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: What would the nurse guide a labor coach to do to comfort a woman tensing her muscles with contractions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Offer warm liquids to the patient.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Assist the patient to the knee-chest position.

questions.rationale: Panting relaxes the abdominal wall and distracts the patient. It would not be helpful to offer fluids or to attempt conversation during contractions. Walking intensifies contractions.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A woman in labor will receive general anesthesia prior to cesarean section. The nurse reminds the patient that food and fluids need to be restricted for several hours prior to delivery. What will this prevent?
questions.rationale: The major adverse effect of general anesthesia is aspiration of stomach contents.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: What assessment should be taken immediately after the anesthesiologist administers an epidural block to a laboring woman?
questions.rationale: Blood pressure is checked every 5 minutes when the epidural block is first begun. Bladder assessment is also important but not an initial assessment.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A woman in labor has had an epidural block for pain relief. The nurse will be assessing carefully for what associated side effect of this type of regional anesthesia?
questions.rationale: A side effect of an epidural block is urine retention, because the anesthesia interferes with the woman'‘s ability to have an urge to void. The patient may have to be catheterized.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Which narcotic antagonist is used to reverse narcotic-induced respiratory depression?
questions.rationale: Naloxone (Narcan) is used to reverse respiratory depression caused by narcotics.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: The nurse is preparing a teaching plan for a woman receiving a subarachnoid block before delivery. What nursing action will be included in this plan to prevent the associated side effect of this type of anesthesia?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Walk with assistance as soon as possible.

questions.rationale: The woman would be advised to remain flat for several hours after the block to decrease the chance of postspinal headache.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A woman requests a pudendal block to manage her labor pain. What statement by the woman indicates a need for further explanation about the pudendal block?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “TI‘m having a contraction. Can I get the pudendal block now?”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “I'll get the pudendal block right before I deliver.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “The nurse-midwife will insert the needles into my vagina.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “It takes a few minutes after the medicine is administered to make me feel numb.”

questions.rationale: The pudendal block does not block pain from contractions and is given just before birth.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: An 18-year-old primigravida is 4 cm dilated and her contractions are 5 minutes apart. She received little prenatal care and had no childbirth preparation. She is crying loudly and shouting, “Please give me something for the pain. I can‘t take the pain!” What is the priority nursing diagnosis?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Knowledge deficit related to the birth experience

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ineffective coping related to inadequate preparation for labor

choices.label: D
choices.text: Risk for injury related to lack of prenatal care

questions.rationale: The most important issue for this woman, at this time, is effective pain management.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: The nurse who encourages the gate control theory of pain control would advise a woman in labor and her partner to use which nonpharmacological method of pain management?
questions.rationale: According to the gate control theory, stimulating large-diameter nerve fibers temporarily interferes with conduction of impulses through small-diameter fibers. Massage is a technique that stimulates large-diameter fibers and “closes the gate.”

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: When a pregnant woman arrives at the labor suite, she tells the nurse that she wants to have an epidural for delivery. What is a contraindication to an epidural block?
questions.rationale: An epidural block is not used if a woman has abnormal blood clotting.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: The nurse coaches the primigravida not to bear down until the cervix is completely dilated. What may premature bearing down cause?
questions.rationale: Bearing down against a cervix that is not dilated can cause edema and laceration to the cervix.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: What is the Dick-Read method of childbirth preparation based on?
questions.rationale: The Dick-Read method depends on the use of relaxation techniques to reduce the discomforts of labor.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: The nurse is instructing a Lamaze class on abdominal breathing and tells a patient that her baseline respiratory rate is 22 breaths per minute. What should be the patient‘s rate while performing slow breathing? a 9 bo ce 15
questions.rationale: The range of respirations should be no lower than half of the base rate and no more rapid than double the base rate.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: What is the least amount of sensation that one perceives as pain?
questions.rationale: Pain threshold is the least amount of sensation that one perceives as pain. Thresholds are different for each individual.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: The nurse is caring for a laboring patient who is not reporting pain. What sign would alert the nurse of the need for pain relief?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Covering her face with her hands

questions.rationale: Facial grimacing may be an indicator of unexpressed pain.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A patient who received an epidural block asks why her blood pressure is taken so often. What is the nurse‘s best response to explain the frequent blood pressure assessments?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They ensure that unsafe levels of hypertension do not occur.

choices.label: B
choices.text: They help assess for the need for further pain relief.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They monitor the progress of labor.

questions.rationale: The hypotension that accompanies an epidural block may cause inadequate perfusion of the placenta, leading to fetal hypoxia.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A laboring patient requests hot and cold applications be applied to her abdomen for pain control. How will this intervention act to control pain?

choices.label: D
choices.text: By stimulation of large nerve fibers

questions.rationale: The gate control theory explains how pain impulses reach the brain for interpretation. It supports several nonpharmacological methods of pain control. According to this theory, pain is transmitted through small-diameter nerve fibers. However, the stimulation of large-diameter nerve fibers temporarily interferes with the conduction of impulses through small-diameter fibers. Techniques to stimulate large-diameter fibers and “close the gate” to painful impulses include massage, palm and fingertip pressure, and heat and cold applications.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: When caring for the laboring patient, the nurse determines that the fetus is located in the right occiput posterior (ROA). What will the nurse anticipate?
questions.rationale: If the fetal occiput is in a posterior pelvic quadrant, each contraction pushes it against the mother‘s sacrum, resulting in persistent and poorly relieved back pain (back labor). Labor is often longer with this fetal position.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: What typical types of classes are available to help expectant parents prepare for parenthood? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Prenatal classes include such topics as infant care, breastfeeding, gestational diabetes, exercising, and sibling and grandparent preparation. Yoga and financial information are not traditional content for prenatal instruction.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: What breathing techniques would the nurse teach the prenatal patient to help her focus during labor in order to reduce pain? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: First-stage breathing includes the techniques of modified paced breathing and patterned paced breathing, which are types of abdominal breathing techniques. These patterns of breathing will help a woman in labor to focus and reduce pain perception. The fourth stage of labor is the woman‘s recovery stage and does not require a breathing technique.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: How does the pain of childbirth differ from other types of pain? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Childbirth pain is part of a normal process.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Childbirth pain seldom needs narcotic relief.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Position changes relieve pain and facilitate delivery.

questions.rationale: Childbirth pain differs from other types of pain, because it is part of a normal, natural, and expected process, can be relieved by change of position, declines immediately following birth, and is self-limiting. Childbirth pain requires pharmacological management with narcotics in many cases. Childbirth Pain

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Which are nonpharmacological forms of pain relief? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Skin stimulation, diversion and distraction, and breathing techniques are the bases of nonpharmacological pain control. Although exercise and practices such as yoga and Pilates are beneficial, they are not means of pain control.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Which position(s) and exercise(s) will the nurse teach as beneficial in combating discomfort in the later stages of pregnancy? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Pelvic rock, tailor sitting, and shoulder curling are beneficial to the muscles that will have to adapt to the extra weight and changed posture of later pregnancy. Leg lifts and sit-ups are not beneficial, because they both increase intra-abdominal pressure.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: The nurse is providing a conference on nonpharmacological pain control methods. What major advantages of nonpharmacological pain control methods will the nurse include in the presentation? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: C
choices.text: They do not dull the excitement of the birth experience.

choices.label: D
choices.text: They do not have the potential to cause allergic reactions.

choices.label: E
choices.text: They do not have to be delayed until labor is well established.

questions.rationale: All the options mentioned are benefits of nonpharmacological pain control methods with the exception of sedating the mother.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: The nurse is caring for a woman with epidural anesthesia for pain control during a vaginal delivery. A risk for injury related to epidural anesthesia has been identified by the nursing staff. What interventions are appropriate for the nurse to implement related to this diagnosis? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Assess leg movement and sensation before ambulating.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Observe for signs of impending birth.

questions.rationale: To prevent the risk for injury related to epidural anesthesia, the nurse should assess for movement, sensation, and leg strength before ambulating, ambulate cautiously with an assistant, assist the woman to change positions regularly, and observe for signs that birth may be near: increase in bloody show, perineal bulging, and/or crowning.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Management of Pain During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: The physician has ordered Fentanyl (Sublimaze) for a woman in labor and has asked the nurse to provide patient education. What will the nurse include in the educational plan? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is not the same drug as sufentanil.

questions.rationale: Fentanyl has a rapid onset and short duration of action. Fentanyl, sufentanil, and alfentanil are not the same drugs. Fentanyl can cause respiratory depression but less than meperidine. It is not administered by mouth.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: What nursing assessment should be reported immediately after an amniotomy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fetal heart rate is regular at 154 beats/minute.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Amniotic fluid is clear with flecks of vernix.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Amniotic fluid is watery and pale green.

questions.rationale: Amniotic fluid should be clear. Green fluid indicates the fetus has passed meconium, which is associated with fetal compromise.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A woman 2 weeks past her expected delivery date is receiving an oxytocin infusion to induce labor and begins to have contractions every 90 seconds. What is the nurse‘s initial action?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Continue the infusion and report the findings to the physician.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Turn her on her left side and reassess the contractions.

questions.rationale: Oxytocin is discontinued if signs of fetal compromise or excessive uterine contractions occur.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: What nursing care should be provided to a woman with a third-degree laceration immediately after delivery?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Elevation of hips to prevent edema

questions.rationale: Ice is applied to the perineum to reduce bruising and edema.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: After several hours of labor, a nursing assessment reveals that a woman‘s cervix is 5 cm dilated, but contractions are becoming shorter and less frequent. What is this labor pattern considered?
questions.rationale: The woman with labor dysfunction related to decreased uterine muscle tone begins labor normally, but contractions diminish after the active phase.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A labor dysfunction due to decreased uterine muscle tone occurs in a patient who is dilated to 5 cm with membranes intact. What action by the physician will the nurse anticipate?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Order a sedative for the patient.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Plan to do an emergency cesarean section.

questions.rationale: Medical treatment for hypotonic labor dysfunction includes an amniotomy as the first remedy if the membranes are intact.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: An infant is delivered with the use of forceps. What should the nurse assess for in the newborn?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Loss of hair from contact with forceps

questions.rationale: Pressure from forceps may injure the infant‘s facial nerve, which is evidenced by facial asymmetry.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Anew mother is distressed and tearful about the elevated dome over her infant‘s posterior fontanelle. The nurse responds, “This condition will resolve itself in a few days.” What is the cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Prolonged pressure against the partially dilated cervix

choices.label: B
choices.text: Small leak of fluid through the posterior fontanelle

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pressure of the forceps during delivery

choices.label: D
choices.text: The effect of the vacuum extractor

questions.rationale: The “chignon” is due to the effect of the vacuum extractor and will disappear in a few days.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A frustrated patient in labor has been affected by decreased uterine muscle tone and reports, “My doctor won‘t induce my labor because of some silly score. He said I was a 4. What kind of magic number do I need?” What is the lowest Bishop score the patient should have prior to induction?
questions.rationale: The Bishop score evaluates the suitability of the patient for a vaginal delivery. A minimum score of 6 is recommended by the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG).

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A woman is having a difficult labor because the fetus is presenting in the right occipital position (ROP). What position will the nurse promote to encourage fetal rotation and pain relief?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Prone with legs supported and give her a back massage

choices.label: B
choices.text: Supine with legs bent at the knee

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sitting up and leaning forward on the overbed table

questions.rationale: A position that favors fetal rotation and descent and that is helpful for the woman with back labor is to sit or kneel leaning forward on a support.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: The initial vaginal examination of a woman admitted to the labor unit reveals that the cervix is dilated 9 cm. The panicked woman begs the nurse, “Please give me something.” What is the most appropriate pain-relief intervention for a woman in precipitate labor?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Get an order for an intravenous narcotic.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Notify the anesthesiologist for an epidural block.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Stay and breathe with her during contractions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tell her to bear with it because she is close to delivery.

questions.rationale: The nurse would stay with the woman experiencing precipitate labor and breathe with her during contractions to help the woman focus and cope with each contraction.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A woman who is 33 weeks pregnant is admitted to the obstetric unit because her membranes ruptured spontaneously. What complication should the nurse closely assess for with this patient?
questions.rationale: Infection of the amniotic sac, called chorioamnionitis, may cause prematurely ruptured membranes, or it may be a consequence of rupture, because the barrier to the uterine cavity is broken.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: The nurse is administering terbutaline (Brethine) to a pregnant woman to prevent preterm labor. The nurse would assess for which adverse effect?
questions.rationale: Maternal tachycardia is the common negative side effect of terbutaline, which should be corrected with a dose of propranolol.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Which statement indicates a woman understands activity limitations for the management of preterm labor?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “After my shower in the morning, I do the laundry and straighten up the house; then I rest.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Ipack a picnic basket and put it next to the sofa so I do not have to get up for food during the day.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Thave a 2-year-old to care for, but I try to rest as much as I can.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “TI get really bored at home, so I go to the shopping mall for just a little while.”

questions.rationale: Lengthy activity restrictions are often needed to prevent preterm birth. The nurse can help the woman identify ways to organize necessary activities and maximize rest.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A student nurse questions the instructor regarding what alteration should be made for the assessment of the fundus of a new postoperative cesarean section patient. What is the best response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The fundus is not assessed until the second postoperative day.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The fundus is assessed by “walking” fingers from the side of the uterus to the midline.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The fundus is assessed only if large clots appear in lochia.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The fundus is assessed only once every shift.

questions.rationale: Assessment of the fundus following a cesarean section is done as usual, but using especially gentle fundal massage.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A pulsating structure is felt during a vaginal examination of a woman in labor. How would the nurse position the woman to prevent compression of a prolapsed cord?

choices.label: A
choices.text: On her right side with knees flexed

choices.label: B
choices.text: On her left side with a pillow placed between her legs

choices.label: C
choices.text: Onher back with her head lower than the rest of her body

choices.label: D
choices.text: Supine with her legs elevated and bent at the knee

questions.rationale: The Trendelenburg‘s (head down) position displaces the fetus upward to stop compression of the prolapsed cord.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Several hours after delivery, the nurse finds a woman crying. The woman says repeatedly, “My baby is beautiful, but I was planning on a vaginal delivery. Instead I needed an emergency C-section.” What is the most appropriate nursing diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anxiety related to the development of postpartum complications

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ineffective individual coping related to unfamiliarity with procedures

choices.label: C
choices.text: Risk for ineffective parenting related to emergency cesarean section

choices.label: D
choices.text: Grieving related to loss of expected birth experience

questions.rationale: Women who have cesarean births usually need greater support than those who have vaginal births. They may feel grief, guilt, or anger, because the expected course of birth did not occur.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A pregnant woman‘s membranes ruptured prematurely at 34 weeks. She will be discharged to her home for the next few weeks. What would the nurse planning discharge instruction teach the woman to do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Report any increase in fetal activity.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Notify her obstetrician if she has a temperature above 37.8°C (100°F).

choices.label: C
choices.text: Massage her breasts to promote uterine relaxation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rest in a side-lying Trendelenburg‘s position with hips elevated.

questions.rationale: For the woman with premature rupture of membranes (PROM) who is not having labor induced right away, teaching combines information about infection and preterm labor. The woman should monitor her temperature and report a temperature greater than 37.8°C (100°F).

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A woman who is 24 weeks pregnant is placed on an intravenous infusion of magnesium sulfate. What side effect should the nurse inform the patient that she might experience?
questions.rationale: Magnesium sulfate is the drug of choice for initiating therapy to stop labor. The patient will notice a warm flush with the initiation of the drug.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: When a woman is admitted to the labor and delivery unit, she tells the nurse that she is anxious about delivery, the welfare of her infant, and how quickly she will recover. How can anxiety affect labor?

choices.label: A
choices.text: By decreasing a woman‘s pain sensitivity

choices.label: B
choices.text: By reducing blood flow to the uterus

choices.label: C
choices.text: By increasing the ability to tolerate pain

choices.label: D
choices.text: By enhancing maternal pushing through greater muscle tension

questions.rationale: Excessive anxiety reduces uterine blood flow, making uterine contractions less effective, and creates muscle tension that counteracts the expulsion powers of contractions.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: During a strenuous labor, the woman asks for some pain remedy for the sudden pain between her scapulae that seems to occur with every breath she takes. What is the best nursing action?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Turn the patient to her back and flex her knees.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Suggest that the coach give her a back rub.

questions.rationale: Sudden pain between the scapulae during a strenuous labor is an indicator of uterine rupture. This should be reported immediately.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: What does the nurse explain is used to soften the cervix with a “cervical ripening” agent?
questions.rationale: Prostaglandin gel is inserted in the cervix and the woman remains in bed for 1 to 2 hours, being monitored for uterine contractions.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: The nurse is caring for a patient who is threatening preterm labor and has been given glucocorticoids. What is the purpose of glucocorticoid administration?
questions.rationale: Glucocorticoids assist with improving the lung maturity of a fetus that is preterm.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: The nurse arrives at the start of a shift on the labor unit to find a census of four patients in active labor. Which laboring patient should the nurse attend to first?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 18-year-old primigravida with a fetal breech presentation

choices.label: B
choices.text: 25-year-old multigravida with history of previous cesarean section

choices.label: C
choices.text: 35-year-old multigravida with history of precipitate birth

questions.rationale: A precipitate birth is completed in less than 3 hours. Labor often begins abruptly and intensifies quickly, rather than having a more subtle onset and gradual progression. Contractions may be frequent and intense, often from the onset. If the woman‘s tissues do not yield easily to the powerful contractions, she may have uterine rupture, cervical lacerations, or hematoma. Fetal breech presentation, history of cesarean section, and multifetal pregnancy have associated risk factors, but not as immediate as precipitate birth.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: The nurse is caring for a patient diagnosed with hypotonic labor dysfunction. What will the nurse expect when caring for this patient?
questions.rationale: A woman with hypotonic labor dysfunction will be encouraged to change position frequently to enhance contractions. With hypotonic labor uterine resting tone is decreased and IV fluids are increased. Painful and poorly coordinated contractions occur with hypertonic labor.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: What sign(s) of infection should the nurse assess for after an amniotomy?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increase of fetal heart rate (FHR) from 160 to 174 beats/minute

choices.label: C
choices.text: Flecks of vernix in the amniotic fluid

questions.rationale: Increase in the FHR above 160 beats/minute frequently precedes a woman‘s temperature elevation. All the other options are normal findings for late pregnancy.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: What are the rationales for labor induction? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Maternal diabetes and placental insufficiency are rationales for induction. The other options are contraindications for labor induction.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Which interventions could a nurse apply to help stimulate contractions? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Encouraging the patient to sit upright

choices.label: E
choices.text: Allowing the patient to vent frustration

questions.rationale: Sitting upright, ambulating, and stimulating the nipples may encourage progression of labor. Offering emotional support and allowing patient to vent frustration are supportive to the patient but do not stimulate more effective labor.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: What complications of overstimulation of uterine contractions may occur? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Impaired placental exchange of oxygen and nutrients

questions.rationale: The most common complications are impaired placental exchange and uterine rupture, but water intoxication can occur due to fluid retention.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: How might the nurse instruct the patient to stimulate her nipples in an attempt to increase the quality of uterine contractions? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Place a warm, moist washcloth over the breast.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Brush the nipples with a dry washcloth.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Apply suction to the nipples with a breast pump.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Press the palms of her hands down on her breasts.

questions.rationale: Brushing nipples with a dry washcloth, gently pulling nipples, and applying suction to nipples with a breast pump are all effective methods of nipple stimulation, which will increase the quality of uterine contractions.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A woman is 37 weeks pregnant and questioning the nurse about possible induction of labor at term. What conditions would contraindicate labor induction? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Labor induction is contraindicated with placenta previa or a prolapsed umbilical cord. Gynecoid pelvis is the most favorable shape for vaginal delivery. Induction can be attempted as a VBAC after a horizontal cesarean incision but is contraindicated with a classic (vertical) incision. Gestational diabetes is not a contraindication for labor induction.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A woman is preparing for administration of a cervical ripening agent. What nursing actions will the nurse anticipate implementing? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Record a baseline fetal heart rate.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Instruct patient to ambulate immediately afterward.

questions.rationale: The cervical ripening procedure should be explained to the woman and her family. A fetal heart rate baseline is recorded. An intravenous (IV) line with saline or heparin sodium (Hep-Lock) may be placed in case uterine tachysystole (hyperstimulation) occurs and IV tocolytics (drugs that reduce uterine contractions) are needed. After insertion of the prostaglandin gel, the woman remains on bed rest for 1 to 2 hours and is monitored for uterine contractions. Vital signs and fetal heart rate are also recorded.

questions.chapter_title: The Family After Birth
questions.stem: The nurse is assessing a newborn. Which sign would indicate hypoglycemia?
questions.rationale: There are many signs of hypoglycemia in the newborn. One is a high-pitched cry.

questions.chapter_title: The Family After Birth
questions.stem: What would the nurse expect to find when assessing the fundus of the uterus immediately after delivery?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Well-contracted with its upper border at or just below the umbilicus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Well-contracted with its upper border three or four fingerbreadths above the umbilicus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Relaxed with its upper border level with the umbilicus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Relaxed with its upper border two or three fingerbreadths below the umbilicus

questions.rationale: Immediately after the placenta is expelled, the uterine fundus can be felt as a firm mass, about the size of a grapefruit, at the level of the umbilicus.

questions.chapter_title: The Family After Birth
questions.stem: What statement made by a new mother indicates she needs additional information about breastfeeding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Tlet the baby nurse 10 to 15 minutes on the first breast and then switch to the other breast.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “The baby needs to nurse at least 5 minutes on the breast to get the hindmilk.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “The baby has been nursing every 2 to 3 hours.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Ifthe baby gets fussy between feedings, I give her a bottle of water.”

questions.rationale: Supplemental feedings of formula or water should not be offered to a healthy newborn who is breastfeeding.

questions.chapter_title: The Family After Birth
questions.stem: After delivery, the nurse‘s assessment reveals a soft, boggy uterus located above the level of the umbilicus. What is the most appropriate nursing intervention?
questions.rationale: A poorly contracted uterus should be massaged until firm to prevent hemorrhage.

questions.chapter_title: The Family After Birth
questions.stem: What type of lochia will the nurse assess initially after delivery?
questions.rationale: The initial vaginal discharge after delivery is called lochia rubra. It is red and moderately heavy. Lochia rubra lasts for up to 3 days postpartum.

questions.chapter_title: The Family After Birth
questions.stem: A woman will be discharged 48 hours after a vaginal delivery. When planning discharge teaching, the nurse would include what information about lochia?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lochia should disappear 2 to 4 weeks postpartum.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is normal for the lochia to have a slightly foul odor.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A change in lochia from pink to bright red should be reported.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A decrease in flow will be noticed with ambulation and activity.

questions.rationale: A return to bright red lochia rubra may indicate a late postpartum hemorrhage and must be reported.

questions.chapter_title: The Family After Birth
questions.stem: What instruction should the nurse teach the postpartum woman about perineal self-care?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Perform perineal self-care at least twice a day.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cleanse with warm water in a squeeze bottle from front to back.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Remove perineal pads from the rectal area toward the vagina.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use cool water to decrease edema of the perineum.

questions.rationale: Cleansing from front to back prevents contamination from the rectal area.

questions.chapter_title: The Family After Birth
questions.stem: A postpartum woman is not immune to rubella. What will the nurse expect?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The rubella virus vaccine should be administered before discharge.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The woman should receive the rubella virus vaccine at her 6-week postpartum checkup.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The woman should be instructed not to get pregnant until she receives the rubella vaccine.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No intervention is indicated at this time because the woman is not at risk for rubella.

questions.rationale: The woman who is not immune to rubella is immunized in the immediate postpartum period, because there is no danger of her being pregnant.

questions.chapter_title: The Family After Birth
questions.stem: Which statement indicates the new mother is breastfeeding correctly?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Twill alternate breasts when feeding the baby.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “I keep the baby on a 4-hour feeding schedule.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Tlet the baby stay on the first breast only 5 minutes.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “T put only the nipple in the baby‘s mouth when I am breastfeeding.”

questions.rationale: Alternating breasts for feeding increases milk production, particularly hindmilk, which has a higher protein and fat content.

questions.chapter_title: The Family After Birth
questions.stem: The nurse is counseling a lactating mother about diet. What would the nurse include with this information?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Consume 500 more calories than her usual prepregnancy diet.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Eat less meat and more fruits and vegetables.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Drink 3 to 4 tall glasses of fluid daily.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Eat 1000 more calories than her usual prepregnancy diet.

questions.rationale: To maintain nutrient stores while breastfeeding, the mother needs 500 additional calories each day over her prepregnancy diet.

questions.chapter_title: The Family After Birth
questions.stem: A woman asks about resumption of her menstrual cycle after childbirth. What should the nurse respond?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A woman will not ovulate in the absence of menstrual flow.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most nonlactating women resume menstruation about 2 months postpartum.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Generally, a woman does not ovulate in the first few cycles after childbirth.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The return of menstruation is delayed when a woman does not breastfeed.

questions.rationale: Menstrual periods resume in about 6 to 8 weeks if the woman is not breastfeeding.

questions.chapter_title: The Family After Birth
questions.stem: In what situation will the physician order RaoGAM?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anunsensitized Rh-negative mother has an Rh-positive infant.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A sensitized infant has a rising bilirubin level.

choices.label: D
choices.text: An unsensitized infant exhibits no outward signs.

questions.rationale: The Rh-negative woman should receive RhoGAM within 72 hours after the birth of an Rh-positive infant.

questions.chapter_title: The Family After Birth
questions.stem: After birth, the nurse quickly dries and wraps the newborn in a blanket. How does this action prevent heat loss?
questions.rationale: Newborns lose heat quickly after birth as fluid evaporates from their bodies.

questions.chapter_title: The Family After Birth
questions.stem: What will the nurse‘s instructions for a new mother to care for the infant‘s umbilical cord include?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Keeping the area covered with a sterile dressing

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dressing the stump with antibiotic ointment at every diaper change

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fastening the diaper low to allow for air circulation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Giving the newborn a daily tub bath until the cord falls off

questions.rationale: Diaper placement below the umbilical stump allows for drying by air circulation.

questions.chapter_title: The Family After Birth
questions.stem: Anew mother states her preference to formula feed her newborn. What will the nurse planning discharge instructions tell her to help suppress lactation and promote comfort?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Wear a well-fitting bra continuously for several days.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Stand in a warm shower, letting the water spray over the breasts.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Express small amounts of milk from the breasts several times a day.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Massage the breasts when they ache.

questions.rationale: When a mother does not wish to breastfeed, a snug bra worn around the clock can help alleviate discomfort from engorgement.

questions.chapter_title: The Family After Birth
questions.stem: On the second postpartum day, a mother bathed her newborn for the first time. She tells the nurse, “I don‘t think I did it right.” What postpartum psychological stage is this woman most likely in based on this comment?
questions.rationale: In phase 2, taking hold, the mother begins to initiate action and becomes interested in caring for the infant. In doing so, she may become critical of her performance.

questions.chapter_title: The Family After Birth
questions.stem: A primipara tells the nurse, “My afterpains get worse when I am breastfeeding.” What is the most appropriate nursing response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “T‘ll get you some aspirin to relieve the cramping that you feel.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Afterpains are more intense with your first baby.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Breastfeeding releases a hormone that causes your uterus to contract.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “A change of position when you‘re breastfeeding might help.”

questions.rationale: Breastfeeding mothers may have more afterpains because infant suckling causes the posterior pituitary to release oxytocin, which is a hormone that contracts the uterus.

questions.chapter_title: The Family After Birth
questions.stem: A new mother has decided not to breastfeed her newborn. What information will the nurse include when planning to teach the mother about formula feeding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Positioning the bottle so that the nipple is full of formula during the entire feeding

choices.label: B
choices.text: Heating the infant formula in a microwave

choices.label: C
choices.text: Burping the infant after 4 ounces and again when the bottle is empty

choices.label: D
choices.text: Propping a bottle for a feeding

questions.rationale: The nipple of the bottle should be kept full of formula to reduce the amount of air the infant swallows.

questions.chapter_title: The Family After Birth
questions.stem: In the recovery room, the nurse checks the newly delivered woman‘s fundus following a cesarean section. How would the nurse proceed with this assessment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Palpate from the midline to the side of the body.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Palpate from the symphysis to the umbilicus.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Palpate from the side of the uterus to the midline.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Massage the abdomen in a circular motion.

questions.rationale: The fundus is checked gently by walking the fingers from the side of the uterus to the midline.

questions.chapter_title: The Family After Birth
questions.stem: The nurse instructed a postpartum woman about storing and freezing breast milk. What statement by the woman leads the nurse to determine that the teaching was effective?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Tcan thaw frozen breast milk in the microwave.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “I‘ll put enough breast milk for one day in a container.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Breast milk can be stored in glass containers.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Breast milk can be kept in the refrigerator for up to 3 months.”

questions.rationale: Breast milk can be safely stored in glass or clear hard plastic containers.

questions.chapter_title: The Family After Birth
questions.stem: What should the nurse implement for security purposes when bringing the infant from the nursery to the mother?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ask the mother to identify herself verbally.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Check the band number of the infant with that of the mother.

questions.rationale: The nurse should check the band number of the infant with that of the mother by asking the mother to verbally read the number.

questions.chapter_title: The Family After Birth
questions.stem: Below what blood glucose level is the newborn considered hypoglycemic?
questions.rationale: A blood glucose level of less than 40 mg/dL is considered hypoglycemic. If the screening sample is below 40 mg/dL, a venous sample will be drawn. After the blood has been drawn, the infant should be fed to prevent a further drop.

questions.chapter_title: The Family After Birth
questions.stem: The nurse is caring for a woman of Middle Eastern descent on the first postpartum day. Education is provided regarding instruction on use of a sitz bath. What documentation best indicates that the woman has understood the provided instruction?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Patient indicated understanding by nodding head with instruction.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Family member indicates patient understands procedure.

questions.rationale: The nurse may need an interpreter to understand and provide optimal care to the woman and her family. If possible, when discussing sensitive information the interpreter should not be a family member, who might interpret selectively. The interpreter should not be of a group that is in social or religious conflict with the patient and her family, an issue that might arise in many Middle Eastern cultures. It is also important to remember that an affirmative nod from the woman may be a sign of courtesy to the nurse rather than a sign of understanding or agreement.

questions.chapter_title: The Family After Birth
questions.stem: A woman has given birth to an unresponsive newborn that NICU staff are attempting to revive. The patient and her husband are grief stricken and request the child be baptized immediately. What is the nurse‘s most appropriate action?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ask the physician to baptize the newborn.

questions.rationale: If the condition of a newborn is poor, the parents may wish to have a baptism performed. The minister or priest is notified. However, this is an emergency, so the nurse may perform the baptism by pouring water on the infant‘s forehead while saying, “I baptize you in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.” If there is any doubt as to whether the infant is alive, the baptism is given conditionally: “If you are capable of receiving baptism, I baptize you in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.” The physician is attending to the patient‘s immediate health needs.

questions.chapter_title: The Family After Birth
questions.stem: A woman required a cesarean section for safe delivery of her newborn. She is planning to breastfeed and verbalized concern about pain. What is the best suggestion by the nurse?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Consider formula feeding for the first few days.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Pumping breast milk would be best for now.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Take pain medication 30 to 40 minutes prior to nursing.”

questions.rationale: The best answer is to encourage use of the football hold to decrease pressure on the operative site. There is no indication for the woman to formula feed or pump. Some pain medications should not be taken when breastfeeding.

questions.chapter_title: The Family After Birth
questions.stem: Which assessments would lead the nurse to determine the gestational age of the infant as preterm? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Vernix only in the body creases

questions.rationale: The only signs of preterm are the thin skin and the slowly responding ear.

questions.chapter_title: The Family After Birth
questions.stem: The nurse is giving a shower to a patient who had a cesarean section 2 days previously. What interventions should be included before, during, and after the shower? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Leave abdominal dressing open to air.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Position patient with back to water stream.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cover infusion site with rubber glove.

questions.rationale: The patient should be evaluated for ambulatory ability, and the abdominal dressing and infusion site should be covered with a waterproof cover. The patient should be provided a shower chair and positioned with her back to the water stream.

questions.chapter_title: The Family After Birth
questions.stem: What postpartum exercises should the nurse teach a patient who had a vaginal delivery yesterday? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Exercises for postpartum involution such as abdominal tighteners, head lifts, pelvic tilts, and Kegel exercises are acceptable. Leg lifts are too strenuous early in the postpartum period.

questions.chapter_title: The Family After Birth
questions.stem: While instructing a new mother on formula preparations, the nurse would include what types? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Formula choices are ready-to-use, concentrated liquid formula that will be diluted according to the infant‘s needs, and powdered formula that is mixed as needed. Cow‘s milk and canned evaporated milk are unsuitable, because they are nutritionally inadequate and stress the kidneys.

questions.chapter_title: The Family After Birth
questions.stem: The nurse is instructing a woman at 6 months postpartum on weaning her infant from breastfeeding. What interventions will the nurse suggest? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Eliminate one feeding at a time.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Expect the need for comfort feeding.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Formula will need to be provided to substitute for feeding.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pump breasts in place of eliminated feeding.

questions.rationale: When weaning a newborn from breastfeeding, the mother should eliminate the favorite feeding last. One feeding should be eliminated at a time, and the need for comfort feeding should be expected. In younger infants formula will need to be substituted. The mother should not be instructed to pump in place of eliminated feeding or the breasts will continue to produce milk.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications After Birth
questions.stem: What is the first sign of hypovolemic shock from postpartum hemorrhage?
questions.rationale: Tachycardia is usually the first sign of inadequate blood volume.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications After Birth
questions.stem: Although the nurse has massaged the uterus every 15 minutes, it remains flaccid, and the patient continues to pass large clots. What does the nurse recognize these signs indicate?
questions.rationale: Atony describes a lack of normal muscle tone. If the uterus is atonic, then muscle fibers are flaccid and will not compress bleeding vessels.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications After Birth
questions.stem: What should the nurse’s first action be when postpartum hemorrhage from uterine atony is suspected?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Teach the patient how to massage the abdomen and then get help.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Start IV fluids to prevent hypovolemia and then notify the registered nurse.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Begin massaging the fundus while another person notifies the physician.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ask the patient to void and reassess fundal tone and location.

questions.rationale: When the uterus is boggy, the nurse should immediately massage it until it becomes firm.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications After Birth
questions.stem: The nurse assesses a boggy uterus with the fundus above the umbilicus and deviated to the side. What should the nurse‘s next assessment be?
questions.rationale: Bladder distention can cause uterine atony. The uterus is massaged to firmness and then the bladder is emptied.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications After Birth
questions.stem: Massage and putting the infant to the breast of a postpartum patient have been ineffective in controlling a boggy uterus. What will the nurse anticipate might be ordered by the physician?
questions.rationale: Oxytocin (Pitocin) is the most common drug ordered to control uterine atony.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications After Birth
questions.stem: A 4-week postpartum patient with mastitis asks the nurse if she can continue to breastfeed. What is the nurse‘s most helpful response?

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Pump the breasts to continue milk production, but do not give breast milk to the infant.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Begin all feedings with the affected breast until the mastitis is resolved.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Breastfeeding can continue unless there is abscess formation.”

questions.rationale: The woman with mastitis can continue to breastfeed unless an abscess forms.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications After Birth
questions.stem: A woman had a vaginal delivery two days ago and is preparing for discharge. What will the nurse plan to teach the woman to report to help prevent postpartum complications?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Change in lochia from red to white

questions.rationale: Increased temperature is a sign of infection. The other choices are normal in the postpartum period.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications After Birth
questions.stem: One day after discharge, the postpartum patient calls the clinic complaining of a reddened area on her lower leg, temperature elevation of 37°C (99.8°F), rust-colored lochia, and sore breasts. What does the nurse suspect from these symptoms?
questions.rationale: The complaints related to the leg are indicative of phlebitis. The other signs are normal in the postpartum patient.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications After Birth
questions.stem: Which statement indicates to the nurse on a postpartum home visit that the patient understands the signs of late postpartum hemorrhage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “My discharge would change to red after it has been pink or white.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “If Ihave a postpartum hemorrhage, I will have severe abdominal pain.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Tshould be alert for an increase in bright red blood.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “TI would pass a large clot that was retained from the placenta.”

questions.rationale: When the nurse teaches the postpartum woman about normal changes in lochia, it is important to explain that a return to red bleeding after it has changed to pink or white may indicate a late postpartum hemorrhage.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications After Birth
questions.stem: During a postpartum assessment, a woman reports her right calf is painful. The nurse observes edema and redness along the saphenous vein in the right lower leg. Based on this finding, what does the nurse explain the probable treatment will involve?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Application of ice to the affected leg

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gentle massage of the affected leg

choices.label: D
choices.text: Passive leg exercises twice a day

questions.rationale: Anticoagulant therapy is continued with heparin or warfarin (Coumadin) for 6 weeks after birth to minimize the risk of embolism.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications After Birth
questions.stem: What statement by the patient leads the nurse to determine a woman with mastitis understands treatment instructions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Twill apply cold compresses to the painful areas.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “I will take a warm shower before nursing the baby.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Twill nurse first on the affected side.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Twill empty the affected breast every 8 hours.”

questions.rationale: Moist heat promotes blood flow to the area, comfort, and complete emptying of the breast.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications After Birth
questions.stem: What is the best response to a postpartum woman who tells the nurse she feels “tired and sick all of the time since I had the baby 3 months ago”?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “This is a normal response for the body after pregnancy. Try to get more rest.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “I'll bet you will snap out of this funk real soon.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Why don‘t you arrange for a babysitter so you and your husband can have a night out?”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Let‘s talk about this further. lam concerned about how you are feeling.”

questions.rationale: Ifa postpartum woman seems depressed, it is important to explore her feelings to determine if they are persistent and pervasive.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications After Birth
questions.stem: The nurse is caring for a woman who had a cesarean birth yesterday. Varicose veins are visible on both legs. What nursing action is the most appropriate to prevent thrombus formation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Have the woman sit in a chair for meals.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Monitor vital signs every 4 hours and report any changes.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Tell the woman to remain in bed with her legs elevated.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Assist the woman with ambulation for short periods of time.

questions.rationale: Early ambulation and range-of-motion exercises are valuable aids to prevent thrombus formation in the postpartum woman.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications After Birth
questions.stem: Five days after a spontaneous vaginal delivery, a woman comes to the emergency room because she has a fever and persistent cramping. What does the nurse recognize as the possible cause of these signs and symptoms?
questions.rationale: Fever after 24 hours following delivery is suggestive of an infection. Severe cramping and fever are manifestations of endometritis.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications After Birth
questions.stem: At her 6-week postpartum checkup, a woman mentions to the nurse that she cannot sleep and is not eating. She feels guilty because sometimes she believes her infant is dead. What does the nurse recognize as the cause of this woman‘s symptoms?
