questions.rationale: Major depression is a disorder characterized by deep feelings of worthlessness, guilt, serious sleep, and appetite disturbances, and sometimes delusions about the infant being dead.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications After Birth
questions.stem: Three weeks after delivering her first child, a woman tells the nurse, “I waited so long for this baby and now that she is here, I can‘t believe how different my life is from what I expected.” What is the best nursing response to the woman‘s statement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “How is your partner adjusting to the change?”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Thear this from a lot of first-time mothers.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Have you told anyone else about your feelings?”

questions.rationale: The nurse may help the woman by being a sympathetic listener. The nurse should elicit the new mother‘s feelings about motherhood and her infant.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications After Birth
questions.stem: After a prolonged labor, a woman vaginally delivered a 10-pound, 3-ounce infant boy. What complication should the nurse be alert for in the immediate postpartum period?
questions.rationale: Delivering a large infant and a prolonged labor are risk factors for hematoma formation.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications After Birth
questions.stem: A woman has had persistent lochia rubra for 2 weeks after her delivery and is experiencing pelvic discomfort. What does the nurse explain is the usual treatment for subinvolution?
questions.rationale: Medical treatment for subinvolution is selected to correct the cause. Treatment may include dilation of the cervix and curettage to remove retained placental fragments from the uterine wall.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications After Birth
questions.stem: The 1-day postpartum patient shows a temperature elevation, cough, and slight shortness of breath on exertion. What action should the nurse implement based on these symptoms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Notify the charge nurse of a possible upper respiratory infection.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Notify the physician of a possible pulmonary embolism.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Document expected postpartum mucous membrane congestion.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Medicate with antipyretic remedy for elevated temperature.

questions.rationale: Symptoms of early pulmonary embolism may not be dynamic. The cough with shortness of breath and temperature elevation is a clue to this possible complication.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications After Birth
questions.stem: While caring for a postpartum patient who had a vaginal delivery yesterday, the nurse assesses a firm uterine fundus and a trickle of bright blood. How does the nurse most likely feel and react to this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Concerned and reports a probable cervical laceration

choices.label: B
choices.text: Attentive and massages the uterus to expel retained clots

choices.label: C
choices.text: Distressed and reports a possible clotting disorder

choices.label: D
choices.text: Satisfied with the normal early postpartum finding

questions.rationale: The bright trickle of blood with a firm uterus suggests a cervical laceration.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications After Birth
questions.stem: The nurse assesses a positive Homans‘ sign when the patient‘s leg is flexed and footsharply dorsiflexed. Where does the patient report that the pain is felt?
questions.rationale: A pain in the calf of the leg when the leg is flexed and the foot is dorsiflexed is a positive Homans‘ sign. Homans‘ sign is suggestive of a deep vein thrombosis.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications After Birth
questions.stem: The new mother who had a vaginal delivery yesterday has a white blood cell count of 30,000 cells/dL. What action should the nurse implement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Notify the charge nurse of a possible infection.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Prepare to put the patient in isolation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Have the infant removed from the room and returned to the nursery.

questions.rationale: The patient should be assessed further for other signs of infection, because a white blood cell (WBC) count of 20,000 to 30,000 cells/dL is normal in the early postpartum period.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications After Birth
questions.stem: A postpartum patient experiences anaphylactic shock. What is the most likely cause?
questions.rationale: Anaphylactic shock is caused by allergic responses to drugs administered. Cardiogenic shock may be caused by pulmonary embolism or hypertension. Hypovolemic shock could be caused by blood clotting disorders.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications After Birth
questions.stem: A woman is prescribed Coumadin (warfarin) to treat deep vein thrombosis. What will the nurse instruct this woman is the antidote for warfarin overdose?
questions.rationale: The antidote for warfarin overdose is vitamin K.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications After Birth
questions.stem: A nurse is discussing risk factors for postpartum shock with a childbirth preparation class. What will the nurse include in this education session? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Hypertension is not a cause for postpartum shock; all the other options can cause shock.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications After Birth
questions.stem: The nurse assesses the perineal pad placed on a 3-hour postdelivery patient and finds that there is no lochia on it. What would the nurse expect to find on further assessment? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: A firm fundus the size of a grapefruit

questions.rationale: Large clots that form in a flaccid uterus can obstruct the flow of lochia. A full bladder is a major cause of a uterus that is boggy.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications After Birth
questions.stem: The nurse instructs the postpartum patient that her nutritional intake should include which food(s) particularly supportive to healing? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Legumes and foods containing vitamin C are conducive to healing. Starches are not.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications After Birth
questions.stem: What will the nurse teach a nursing mother to do to reduce the risk of mastitis? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Limit fluid intake to 1 liter per day.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Empty both breasts with each feeding.

questions.rationale: Nursing mothers should take in about 3 liters of fluid a day. All the other options are interventions to reduce the risk of mastitis and milk accumulation in the breast.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications After Birth
questions.stem: A woman is diagnosed with a urinary tract infection in the postpartum period. What foods can the nurse encourage to increase the acidity of urine? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Apricots, cranberry juice, plums, and prunes can increase the acidity of urine. Apples are not considered to increase acidity of urine.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications After Birth
questions.stem: A postpartum patient is experiencing hypovolemic shock. What interventions can the nurse anticipate? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Placement of an indwelling Foley catheter

questions.rationale: Medical management for the patient experiencing hypovolemic shock includes stopping blood loss, giving IV fluids to maintain circulating volume and replace fluids, giving blood transfusions to replenish erythrocytes, and assessment of oxygen saturation. Anticoagulants would not be given.

questions.chapter_title: Nursing Care of Women with Complications After Birth
questions.stem: The nurse weighs a saturated perineal pad and finds it to weigh 15 grams. The nurse is aware that this indicates a blood loss of. mL.
questions.rationale: The weight of 1 g ina perineal pad is equal to 1 mL of blood loss.

questions.chapter_title: The Nurse’s Role in Women’s Health Care
questions.stem: The nurse is preparing a community education program on preventive health care for women. What common screening test will the nurse plan on explaining to the women attending the program?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Breast examination by a health professional

questions.rationale: Mammography is a screening test used to detect breast cancer. A breast examination is a focused assessment, not a test. A breast self-examination is important, but not a screening test. A breast biopsy is a diagnostic test versus a test performed for basic screening purposes.

questions.chapter_title: The Nurse’s Role in Women’s Health Care
questions.stem: The nurse reviews the procedure for breast self-examination (BSE) with a 25-year-old woman who has a family history of breast cancer. When reviewing the procedure, when will the nurse indicate as the best time for a woman to perform a breast self-examination?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A few days before her period

choices.label: C
choices.text: On the last day of menstrual flow

choices.label: D
choices.text: One week after the beginning of her period

questions.rationale: The best time for BSE is 1 week after the beginning of the menstrual period.

questions.chapter_title: The Nurse’s Role in Women’s Health Care
questions.stem: A woman asks the nurse, “How do oral contraceptives prevent pregnancy?” What will the nurse explain about the combination of estrogen and progesterone in oral contraceptives?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Makes cervical mucus hostile to sperm

choices.label: D
choices.text: Acts as a barrier by destroying sperm

questions.rationale: Oral contraceptives contain a combination of estrogen and progesterone that suppresses ovulation. Distribution of this document is illegal extra per year ius

questions.chapter_title: The Nurse’s Role in Women’s Health Care
questions.stem: What should a woman expect after insertion of an intrauterine device (IUD)?

choices.label: C
choices.text: A string should be felt in the vagina.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The device should be changed every 2 years.

questions.rationale: A woman should feel for the string periodically, especially after her period, to confirm the presence of the IUD.

questions.chapter_title: The Nurse’s Role in Women’s Health Care
questions.stem: What information will the nurse provide when educating a woman about the correct use of a diaphragm?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use of a spermicidal cream or jelly is not recommended.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Leave in place for at least 6 hours after intercourse.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Remove immediately after intercourse for douching.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is effective for up to 48 hours if positioned properly.

questions.rationale: To act as a barrier, the diaphragm must be left in place for at least 6 hours after intercourse and can be left in place up to, but no more than 24 hours.

questions.chapter_title: The Nurse’s Role in Women’s Health Care
questions.stem: The nurse is providing sexual education to a group of high school students. What will the nurse explain is the most effective choice of birth control for preventing pregnancy and sexually transmitted diseases?
questions.rationale: Abstinence is 100% effective in preventing pregnancy and sexually transmitted diseases.

questions.chapter_title: The Nurse’s Role in Women’s Health Care
questions.stem: On day 13 of a 28-day cycle, a woman‘s basal body temperature is 36.5°C (97.7°F). What will her temperature measurement most likely be if ovulation takes place on day 14?
questions.rationale: At the time of ovulation, body temperature will increase slightly, about 0.2°C (0.4°F).

questions.chapter_title: The Nurse’s Role in Women’s Health Care
questions.stem: The nurse tells a woman who is trying to conceive to check her cervical mucus for changes. What will she expect the characteristic of cervical mucus to be a few days before ovulation?
questions.rationale: Within a few days of ovulation, cervical mucus will become clear and slippery to aid the passage of sperm into the cervix.

questions.chapter_title: The Nurse’s Role in Women’s Health Care
questions.stem: The nurse is discussing cervical mucus changes with a woman who wishes to use natural family-planning methods. What information about cervical mucus at ovulation will the woman indicate to the nurse, demonstrating that learning has taken place?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cervical mucus enhances the motility of the sperm.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cervical mucus indicates endometrial readiness for implantation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cervical mucus facilitates movement of the ovum through the fallopian tube.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cervical mucus provides vaginal lubrication during intercourse.

questions.rationale: Around the time of ovulation, the slippery, clear cervical mucus enhances the motility of the sperm.

questions.chapter_title: The Nurse’s Role in Women’s Health Care
questions.stem: In the week before her menstrual period, a woman experiences irritability, anxiety, and difficulty concentrating. What remedy might the nurse suggest to relieve thesesymptoms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Drink tea or hot chocolate before going to bed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Take a daily folic acid and vitamin C supplement.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Include complex carbohydrates and fiber in the diet.

questions.rationale: A diet rich in complex carbohydrates and fiber is recommended for premenstrual dysmorphic disorder.

questions.chapter_title: The Nurse’s Role in Women’s Health Care
questions.stem: Ather regular gynecological examination, a woman tells the nurse that she is concerned about osteoporosis. What suggestion can the nurse make to this patient?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Take a vitamin E supplement daily.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Do isometric exercises that can be practiced every day.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Include more dairy products and green, leafy vegetables in her diet.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Try to limit her intake of caffeine.

questions.rationale: Foods rich in calcium include milk, dairy products, and green, leafy vegetables.

questions.chapter_title: The Nurse’s Role in Women’s Health Care
questions.stem: A 48-year-old woman tells the nurse, “I missed my period last month. Am I in menopause?” The nurse knows that at which point is a woman considered to be menopausal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Her periods have stopped for 1 year.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Her periods have been irregular and light for 12 months.

choices.label: C
choices.text: She has symptoms of vasomotor instability.

choices.label: D
choices.text: She experiences symptoms of decreased estrogen, such as dyspareunia.

questions.rationale: When a woman‘s menstrual periods have stopped for 1 year, she is considered menopausal.

questions.chapter_title: The Nurse’s Role in Women’s Health Care
questions.stem: The nurse is planning to teach a woman about perimenopause. What would the nurse include regarding lowered estrogen level?

choices.label: C
choices.text: It raises the level of low-density lipoproteins.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It raises the level of high-density lipoproteins.

questions.rationale: Estrogen increases the amount of high-density lipoproteins that carry cholesterol from body cells to the liver for excretion. With lowered levels of estrogen, low-density lipoproteins increase, causing an increase in the incidence of heart attacks and strokes.

questions.chapter_title: The Nurse’s Role in Women’s Health Care
questions.stem: What side effect would the nurse instruct a woman to look for when starting hormone replacement therapy (HRT)?
questions.rationale: Patients initiating HRT are reminded to have regular follow-up care and report headaches, vision changes, symptoms of thrombophlebitis, and cardiac symptoms.

questions.chapter_title: The Nurse’s Role in Women’s Health Care
questions.stem: What will the nurse advise when a woman asks what she can do to reduce the discomfort of hot flashes?

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Increase the amount of calcium and vitamin D in your diet.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Drink plenty of fluids, particularly caffeinated beverages.”

questions.rationale: Cotton allows easier passage of air than synthetic fabrics. Layering allows the woman to take off or put on clothes when symptoms occur.

questions.chapter_title: The Nurse’s Role in Women’s Health Care
questions.stem: Which statement made by the nurse would teach an adolescent using tampons how to prevent toxic shock syndrome (TSS)?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Super-absorbency tampons are effective for overnight absorption.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tampons should be changed at least every 4 hours.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gloves should be worn when changing tampons.

choices.label: D
choices.text: TSS can be prevented by using a pad for the first 2 days of menstrual flow.

questions.rationale: Tampons should be changed every 4 hours, because a blood-soaked tampon is an excellent environment for bacteria.

questions.chapter_title: The Nurse’s Role in Women’s Health Care
questions.stem: What statement by a man considering a vasectomy indicates a need for further information?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Sterility does not occur immediately after the procedure.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “We will need to use some form of birth control for about a month afterward.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “The procedure involves the use of local anesthesia.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “T‘ll need to remain in the hospital for a few days.”

questions.rationale: A vasectomy takes about 20 minutes and is performed on an outpatient basis under local anesthesia.

questions.chapter_title: The Nurse’s Role in Women’s Health Care
questions.stem: At her 6-week postpartum checkup, a woman states, “I am wondering about birth control. I used oral contraceptives before, and I‘m breastfeeding now. Can I use the pill again?” What is the nurse‘s best response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “You should know that oral contraceptives increase your milk production.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Oral contraceptives can be taken once lactation is well established.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “You don‘t need to use any form of birth control as long as you are breastfeeding.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Oral contraceptives are contraindicated for the lactating woman.”

questions.rationale: Oral contraceptives decrease breast milk production and are contraindicated until lactation is well established. Women who breastfeed their infants usually will not ovulate for 10 weeks and do not need contraception until that time.

questions.chapter_title: The Nurse’s Role in Women’s Health Care
questions.stem: A 21-year-old college student has come to see the nurse practitioner for treatment of a vaginal infection. Physical assessment reveals inflammation of the vagina and vulva, and vaginal discharge has a cottage cheese appearance. With what are these findings consistent?
questions.rationale: The signs and symptoms of candidiasis include inflammation of the vagina and vulva and a cottage cheese appearance to the vaginal discharge.

questions.chapter_title: The Nurse’s Role in Women’s Health Care
questions.stem: The nurse is providing an informational session on oral contraceptives. Which of the following decrease effectiveness of oral contraceptives?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Iron preparations for treatment of anemia

questions.rationale: Anticonvulsants decrease the effectiveness of oral contraceptives.

questions.chapter_title: The Nurse’s Role in Women’s Health Care
questions.stem: The nurse is instructing a man considering a vasectomy. What instruction will the nurse provide to address the postoperative time period?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Intercourse should be delayed for 6 weeks.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sperm will still be ejaculated for a month.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Erections will be difficult to maintain.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Monthly sperm counts for a year will be necessary.

questions.rationale: Because sperm are distal to the severed vas deferens, sperm will be in the ejaculate for about a month. A sperm count after that period of time should be performed to confirm the absence of sperm. Intercourse does not have to be delayed, but an alternate method of contraception should be used. Erections and sexual pleasure are not affected by a vasectomy.

questions.chapter_title: The Nurse’s Role in Women’s Health Care
questions.stem: A woman diagnosed with endometriosis reports “painful intercourse.” What is the appropriate medical term for the nurse to document when describing this symptom?
questions.rationale: Dyspareunia is the term for painful sexual intercourse. Dyspnea is shortness of breath. Dysmenorrhea is painful menstruation. Dysrhythmia is irregular heart rhythm.

questions.chapter_title: The Nurse’s Role in Women’s Health Care
questions.stem: The nurse is educating a woman diagnosed with premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD). What is the best type of diet for the nurse to recommend?
questions.rationale: Treatment of PMDD includes a diet rich in complex carbohydrates and fiber (to lengthen effects of the carbohydrate meal).

questions.chapter_title: The Nurse’s Role in Women’s Health Care
questions.stem: The nurse instructs a woman taking oral contraceptives to report which possible side effects? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: The memory aid ACHES is helpful: abdominal pain, chest pain, headaches, eye problems, and speech disturbances. Weight gain is an expected side effect of oral contraceptives.

questions.chapter_title: The Nurse’s Role in Women’s Health Care
questions.stem: The nurse cautions that women with a history of which disorders are not candidates for HRT? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Persons who are absolutely restricted from HRT are those with melanoma, estrogen-dependent breast cancers, chronic liver disorders, thromboembolic disease, and seizure disorders.

questions.chapter_title: The Nurse’s Role in Women’s Health Care

choices.label: A
choices.text: Drink 8 oz. of water following dosage.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lay down for 30 minutes after taking.

choices.label: C
choices.text: This medication has no known side effects.

questions.rationale: Alendronate (Fosamax) may be prescribed. Esophageal and gastric irritation are common side effects of alendronate, and the woman should be instructed to drink 8 ounces of plain water and sit upright for 30 minutes after taking the drug and before eating a meal. Weight-bearing exercises such as walking, hiking, stair climbing, and dancing are advisable. High-impact exercises should be avoided.
questions.stem: A woman is prescribed to take alendronate (Fosamax) for osteoporosis postmenopause. What information will the nurse provide when educating this patient on alendronate (Fosamax)? (Select all that apply.)

questions.chapter_title: The Term Newborn
questions.stem: While inspecting a newborn‘s head, the nurse identifies a swelling of the scalp that doesnot cross the suture line. How would the nurse refer to this finding when documenting?
questions.rationale: A cephalohematoma is caused by a collection of blood beneath the periosteum of the cranial bone. It does not cross the suture line.

questions.chapter_title: The Term Newborn
questions.stem: What is the nurse‘s best response to a mother who is voicing concern about the molding ofher 2- day-old infant?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Molding doesn‘t cause any problems. Don‘t worry about it.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Did you deliver vaginally or by cesarean section?”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “The baby‘s head conformed to the shape of the birth canal. It will go away soon.”

questions.rationale: The newborn‘s head may be out of shape from molding. This refers to the shaping of the fetal head to conform to the size and shape of the birth canal.

questions.chapter_title: The Term Newborn
questions.stem: What symptom assessed in the newborn shortly after delivery should be reported?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cyanosis of the hands and feet

questions.rationale: Sternal retractions are evidence that the newborn is in respiratory distress and should be reported immediately.

questions.chapter_title: The Term Newborn
questions.stem: When the newborn‘s crib was moved suddenly, the nurse noticed that his legs flexed and arms fanned out, and then both came back toward the midline. How would the nurse interpret this behavior?

choices.label: C
choices.text: An abnormality of the musculoskeletal system

questions.rationale: The Moro reflex is a normal neonatal reflex. It is elicited when the infant‘s crib is jarred. The infant responds by drawing the legs up, fanning the arms, and then bringing the arms to the midline in an embrace position.

questions.chapter_title: The Term Newborn
questions.stem: A first-time mother reports that she is experiencing difficulty breastfeeding her newborn. Which neonatal reflex would the nurse teach the mother to elicit to facilitate breastfeeding?
questions.rationale: The rooting reflex causes the infant‘s head to turn in the direction of anything that touches the cheek in anticipation of food.

questions.chapter_title: The Term Newborn
questions.stem: What will the nurse expect when assessing the anterior fontanelle of a healthy, full-term newborn?
questions.rationale: The anterior fontanelle is diamond shaped and located at the junction of the two parietal and two frontal bones. It should not be raised or sunken, and it closes between 12 and 18 months of age.

questions.chapter_title: The Term Newborn
questions.stem: What statement indicates the parent understands the guidelines for bathing a newborn?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “T‘lluse a mild soap to clean all of the body parts.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Iam going to add bath oil to the water to keep the baby’s skin soft.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Tshould shampoo the head after washing the rest of the body.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “TI‘ll wash from the feet upward and change the washcloth for the face.”

questions.rationale: The shampoo is done last, because the large surface area of the head predisposes the infant to heat loss.

questions.chapter_title: The Term Newborn
questions.stem: The nurse is measuring the vital signs of a calm, full-term newborn. Which finding is abnormal?

choices.label: B
choices.text: An apical pulse rate of 178 beats/minute

questions.rationale: The normal range for a newborn‘s pulse rate is 110 to 160 beats/minute. A pulse rate outside of this range should be reported.

questions.chapter_title: The Term Newborn
questions.stem: The nurse is caring for a newborn who is being breastfed. What will the nurse expect the stool color to be 2 days after birth?
questions.rationale: The stool of a breastfed infant is bright yellow, soft, and pasty.

questions.chapter_title: The Term Newborn
questions.stem: The mother of a 2-week-old infant tells the nurse, “I think the baby is constipated. I‘ve noticed she strains when she has a bowel movement.” What is nurse‘s most helpful response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Give the baby one serving of fruit per day.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Increase the amount and frequency of her feedings.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Ttsounds like the baby is uncomfortable because she is constipated.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Newborns might strain with bowel movements because their muscles aren‘t fully developed.”

questions.rationale: Straining in the newborn period is normal. It results from underdeveloped abdominal musculature. No treatment is required.

questions.chapter_title: The Term Newborn
questions.stem: A full-term newborn weighs 3600 grams at birth. What would the nurse expect the newborn to weigh in grams 3 days later?
questions.rationale: In the first 3 to 4 days of life, a newborn generally loses 5% to 10% of his or her birth weight.

questions.chapter_title: The Term Newborn
questions.stem: The parents of a newborn girl express concern about the infant‘s vaginal discharge, which appears to be bloody mucus. What does the nurse explain as the cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Premature stimulation of the ovarian hormones by the pituitary system

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cessation of female sex hormones transferred in utero from mother to infant

choices.label: C
choices.text: The increased amount of circulating blood from the mother throughout pregnancy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Trauma to the genitalia during the birth process

questions.rationale: Blood-tinged mucus discharged from the vagina is caused by hormonal withdrawal from the mother at birth.

questions.chapter_title: The Term Newborn
questions.stem: The mother of a 2-week-old infant tells the nurse that she thinks he is sleeping too much. What is the most appropriate nursing response to this mother?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Tell me how many hours per day your baby sleeps.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “It is normal for newborns to sleep most of the day.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Newborns generally sleep 12 to 15 hours per day.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “You will find as the baby gets older, he sleeps less.”

questions.rationale: Although it is true that newborns sleep a great deal of any 24-hour period, the nurse must find out what the mother means by “too much” before giving any information.

questions.chapter_title: The Term Newborn
questions.stem: Which statement indicates the parents understand when to contact the pediatrician or nurse practitioner?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Infant has an axillary temperature of 97°F.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Infant has three pasty, yellow-brown stools in 24 hours.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Infant‘s diaper is not wet after 8 hours.

questions.rationale: Decreased or lack of voiding by the newborn should be reported to the pediatrician or nurse practitioner to prevent dehydration.

questions.chapter_title: The Term Newborn
questions.stem: A mother asks the nurse, “Do you think my baby recognized my voice?” The nurse should consider which correct information when responding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Voice recognition is delayed because the ears are not well developed at birth.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Infants respond to voice by increasing movements and sucking.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Infants initially respond to low-pitched voices.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neonates can distinguish a mother‘s voice from other sounds in the first days of life.

questions.rationale: The ability to discriminate between a mother‘s voice and other voices may occur as early as in the first 3 days of life.

questions.chapter_title: The Term Newborn
questions.stem: The nurse compared the birth weight of a 3-day-old with her current weight and determined the infant had lost weight. What is the most appropriate intervention by the nurse?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Do nothing because this is a normal occurrence.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Report the discrepancy to the pediatrician immediately.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Decrease the interval between the infant‘s feedings.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Try feeding the infant a different type of formula.

questions.rationale: It is typical for the newborn to lose 5% to 10% of his or her birth weight in the first 3 to 4 days of life. No change in the plan of care is needed.

questions.chapter_title: The Term Newborn
questions.stem: Parents express concern about the milia on the face and nose of their infant. What is the nurse‘s most helpful response when instructing the parents?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Contact a pediatric dermatologist for topical medication.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Squeeze out the white material after cleansing the face.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Wash the infant‘s face with a mild astringent several times a day.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Leave the milia alone; it will disappear spontaneously. No treatment is needed.

questions.rationale: Milia require no treatment. This skin manifestation will disappear spontaneously.

questions.chapter_title: The Term Newborn
questions.stem: The nurse is going to use a bulb syringe to clear mucus from a newborn‘s nose and mouth. What is the nurse‘s first action?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Place the tip in the nose and squeeze the bulb gently.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Suction secretions from the nose before the mouth.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Depress the bulb before inserting the syringe tip into the mouth.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Insert the tip into the back of the mouth to reach mucus.

questions.rationale: The bulb is depressed, and then the tip is inserted into the mouth and then the nose. The depression is slowly released, creating the suction.

questions.chapter_title: The Term Newborn
questions.stem: The mother of a 4-day-old calls the pediatrician‘s office because she is concerned about her infant‘s skin. Which finding needs to be reported promptly to the child‘s pediatrician?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The hands and feet feel cooler than the rest of the body.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Skin is peeling on several parts of the infants body.

choices.label: C
choices.text: There is a small pink patch on the left eyelid and one on the neck.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Today, the infant‘s skin has a yellowish tinge.

questions.rationale: Physiological jaundice becomes evident between the second and third days of life and lasts for about 1 week. Evidence of jaundice is reported and the newborn is evaluated.

questions.chapter_title: The Term Newborn
questions.stem: What action does the nurse implement to protect newborns from infection while in the nursery?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Wash hands before touching each infant.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Wear a disposable gown when giving infant care.

questions.rationale: Hand washing is the most reliable precaution available to prevent infection. The nurse washes his or her hands between handling different babies.

questions.chapter_title: The Term Newborn
questions.stem: Which assessment of the newborn should be reported?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Head circumference is 5 cm greater than the chest circumference.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hands and feet are warm with a blue color.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Head has a longer than normal shape to it.

questions.rationale: The circumference of the head should be less than 2 cm greater than that of the chest. All other listed assessments are within the norm.

questions.chapter_title: The Term Newborn
questions.stem: Parents of a newborn are worried about dark areas over the sacrum of the newborn. What does the nurse explain this transitory skin discoloration is called?
questions.rationale: Bluish skin discoloration over the sacral area of a newborn is a transitory condition called Mongolian spots.

questions.chapter_title: The Term Newborn
questions.stem: The pediatric clinic nurse receives lab results on several newborn patients. Which of the following should be brought to the physician‘s attention first?
questions.rationale: A bilirubin of 15 is elevated and requires further immediate investigation.

questions.chapter_title: The Term Newborn
questions.stem: The nurse is assessing Apgar score on a newborn. What will be evaluated? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: The Apgar score is a standardized method of evaluating the newborn‘s condition immediately after delivery. Five objective signs are measured: heart rate, respiration, muscle tone, reflexes, and color. The score is obtained | minute after birth and again after 5 minutes.

questions.chapter_title: The Term Newborn
questions.stem: What noninvasive forms of pain relief might a nurse implement with a newborn? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Swaddling, rocking, nonnutritive sucking, quiet environment, and cuddling are all effective, noninvasive pain remedies. Distraction is not a dependable method of pain reduction with infants.

questions.chapter_title: The Term Newborn
questions.stem: The nurse reminds new parents that newborns must be protected from environments that are too cold or too hot because of which aspects of the newborn‘s physiology? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Newborns have very little subcutaneous fat, which offers little insulation against cold. Newborns have ineffective sweat glands and cannot cool themselves through evaporation.

questions.chapter_title: The Term Newborn
questions.stem: Which interventions would be included in the nursing care of the newly circumcised infant? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gently remove the yellow crust formation.

questions.rationale: Postcircumcision care includes washing with warm water, avoiding alcohol wipes, leaving the yellow crust in place, and diapering loosely.

questions.chapter_title: The Term Newborn
questions.stem: The nurse is aware that a full-term infant is born with which reflexes? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Blinking, sneezing, gagging, and sucking reflexes are present in the full-term newborn. Pincer grasp does not occur until between 8 and 12 months.

questions.chapter_title: The Term Newborn
questions.stem: The nurse takes into consideration that newborns are especially prone to dehydration because of which aspects of their physiology? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: D
choices.text: Excessive fluid loss from the sweat glands

choices.label: E
choices.text: Immature renal tubules that do not concentrate urine

questions.rationale: The newborn‘s glomeruli are small and have only one-third of the blood circulation of an adult, and they are unable to effectively concentrate urine. The GI tract is active. The infant‘s sweat glands do not work effectively and allow very little fluid loss through sweat.

questions.chapter_title: Preterm and Postterm Newborns
questions.stem: The nurse is assessing a preterm infant. To what does the infant‘s level of maturation refer?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Actual time the fetus remained in the uterus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Age on the Dubowitz scoring system

choices.label: C
choices.text: Infant‘s weight as compared to the gestational age

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ability of the organs to function outside of the uterus

questions.rationale: Level of maturation refers to how well developed the infant is at birth and the ability of the organs to function outside of the uterus.

questions.chapter_title: Preterm and Postterm Newborns
questions.stem: A preterm infant has a yellow skin color and a rising bilirubin level. The nurse knows that this infant is at risk for what?
questions.rationale: The higher the bilirubin level and the deeper the jaundice, the greater is the risk for neurological damage.

questions.chapter_title: Preterm and Postterm Newborns
questions.stem: Why does a 4-day-old infant born at 33 weeks of gestation possibly need to be fed by gavage during the first few days of life?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Weak or absent sucking or swallowing reflex

choices.label: C
choices.text: Refusal to take formula by mouth

choices.label: D
choices.text: Need for a larger quantity of formula at each feeding

questions.rationale: When the preterm infant‘s sucking and swallowing reflexes are immature, gavage feedings can be used to promote nutrition.

questions.chapter_title: Preterm and Postterm Newborns
questions.stem: What deficiency causes a preterm infant respiratory distress syndrome?
questions.rationale: The production of surfactant, necessary for the absorption of oxygen by the lungs, is deficient in the preterm infant.

questions.chapter_title: Preterm and Postterm Newborns
questions.stem: How will the nurse safely ensure tube placement when preparing to initiate a gavage feeding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Check tube placement by injecting air into the stomach.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Weigh the infant before the feeding.

questions.rationale: When the preterm infant is gavage fed, the contents of the stomach should be aspirated before the feeding is started. Aspiration of the stomach contents ensures tube placement and also allows the nurse to assess the amount of feeding in the stomach.

questions.chapter_title: Preterm and Postterm Newborns
questions.stem: The nurse explains to a patient in preterm labor that what may be ordered by the physician to accelerate fetal lung maturity?
questions.rationale: Surfactant production can be increased by administering corticosteroids to the mother before delivery.

questions.chapter_title: Preterm and Postterm Newborns
questions.stem: The apnea monitor indicates that a preterm infant is having an apneic episode. What is the most appropriate nursing action in this situation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Administer oxygen via a nasal cannula.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gently rub the infant‘s feet or back.

questions.rationale: Gently rubbing the infant‘s back, ankles, or feet may stimulate the infant to breathe.

questions.chapter_title: Preterm and Postterm Newborns
questions.stem: What would the nurse assess for in a preterm infant receiving an intravenous infusion containing calcium gluconate?
questions.rationale: The infant receiving intravenous calcium gluconate should be monitored for bradycardia.

questions.chapter_title: Preterm and Postterm Newborns
questions.stem: What is the rationale for placing a preterm infant born at 34 weeks of gestation in an incubator?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The infant has a small body surface-to-weight ratio.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Heat increases the flow of oxygen to the extremities.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The infant‘s temperature control mechanism is immature.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Heat within the incubator facilitates drainage of mucus.

questions.rationale: The preterm infant is at risk for heat loss for several reasons, one of which is that the heat regulating center in the brain is immature.

questions.chapter_title: Preterm and Postterm Newborns
questions.stem: What nursing action is appropriate to prevent possible retinopathy in a preterm infant requiring oxygen therapy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Monitor arterial oxygen levels with a pulse oximeter.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Position the head slightly lower than the body.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Keep the infant‘s eyes covered at all times.

questions.rationale: Use of a pulse oximeter to carefully monitor arterial blood gases in high-risk infants continues to be a priority in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU).

questions.chapter_title: Preterm and Postterm Newborns
questions.stem: When assessing a preterm infant, the nurse observes nasal flaring, sternal retractions, and expiratory grunting. What do these findings indicate?
questions.rationale: Insufficient amounts of surfactant predispose the preterm infant to respiratory distress. The signs manifested by the infant are indicative of respiratory distress.

questions.chapter_title: Preterm and Postterm Newborns
questions.stem: What nursing action will the nurse implement for a preterm infant who is being gavage fed and has a bloody stool?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decrease the amount of the next feeding.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Get a culture of the next stool.

questions.rationale: Bloody stools, abdominal distention, diarrhea, and bilious vomitus are signs of necrotizing enterocolitis. Specific nursing responsibilities include measuring the abdomen and listening to bowel sounds.

questions.chapter_title: Preterm and Postterm Newborns
questions.stem: Parents of a preterm infant come to the NICU every day to see their infant, who is being gavage fed. What will the nurse teaching about stimulating the infant tell the parents?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To bring in colorful pictures and toys to place in the incubator

choices.label: B
choices.text: That stimulating the infant during feedings increases intake

choices.label: C
choices.text: To stroke the infant during feeding to increase intake

choices.label: D
choices.text: Not to disturb the infant between feedings

questions.rationale: During gavage feedings, stroking the infant gently can provide stimulation.

questions.chapter_title: Preterm and Postterm Newborns
questions.stem: The nurse caring for an infant born at 36 weeks of gestation assesses tremors and a weak cry. The nurse is aware that these symptoms indicate what?
questions.rationale: The preterm infant, before 38 weeks, should be assessed for hypoglycemia because the infant‘s glycogen stores are not adequate.

questions.chapter_title: Preterm and Postterm Newborns
questions.stem: The mother of a 4-month-old infant, born prematurely, asks the nurse if her daughter will always be small for her age. What is the most appropriate nursing response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Preterm infants usually remain smaller than term infants throughout childhood.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Your daughter will be the same size as other children by the time she is 1 year old.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Prematurity is associated with short stature but does not affect weight gain.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Tt takes about two years for the preterm infant to catch up to a full-term infant.”

questions.rationale: In the absence of severe birth defects and complications, the growth rate of the preterm newborn nears that of the term infant by about the second year.

questions.chapter_title: Preterm and Postterm Newborns
questions.stem: The nurse caring for a preterm infant will record the intake and output. The nurse is aware that what is the optimum output for this infant?
questions.rationale: The optimum output for a preterm infant is 1 to 3 mL/kg/hr.

questions.chapter_title: Preterm and Postterm Newborns
questions.stem: The nurse is caring for an infant born at 35 weeks of gestation. What physical characteristic might the nurse expect this infant to exhibit?
questions.rationale: The growth and development of the fetus are abruptly halted by a preterm birth. One of the characteristics of the preterm infant is skin that is loose and transparent.

questions.chapter_title: Preterm and Postterm Newborns
questions.stem: The nurse in a pediatrician‘s office is preparing to do a developmental assessment ona 3-month-old infant who was born at 36 weeks. The nurse knows that the infant should be evaluated in what month of achievement to adjust for the preterm birth?
questions.rationale: The growth and development of a preterm infant are based on the current age minus the number of weeks before term that the infant was born.

questions.chapter_title: Preterm and Postterm Newborns
questions.stem: The mother of a postterm infant asks the nurse why the infant is being watched so closely. What is the nurse‘s most appropriate response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “The placenta does not function adequately as it ages.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Delivery of the postterm infant is more difficult.”

questions.rationale: Fetal distress may occur in the postterm infant because placental functioning becomes inadequate with maturity.

questions.chapter_title: Preterm and Postterm Newborns
questions.stem: What symptoms of cold stress might the nurse recognize in a preterm infant?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Warm skin with low core temperature

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased respiratory rate and periods of apnea

questions.rationale: Signs of cold stress include increased respiratory rate with periods of apnea, decreased skin temperature, bradycardia, mottling of skin, and lethargy.

questions.chapter_title: Preterm and Postterm Newborns
questions.stem: The nurse is caring for an infant born at 42 weeks. What would the physical assessment reveal?
questions.rationale: Loss of vernix caseosa leaves the skin dry, causing peeling.

questions.chapter_title: Preterm and Postterm Newborns
questions.stem: What term describes the age of a neonate that is based on the actual time in utero?
questions.rationale: The gestational age is the age based on the actual time in the uterus.

questions.chapter_title: Preterm and Postterm Newborns
questions.stem: How often will the nurse caring for a preterm infant in an incubator record the temperature of the infant and the incubator?
questions.rationale: The temperature of the incubator is adjusted to a level that will maintain an optimal body temperature in the infant. Smaller infants may require higher incubator temperatures. The nurse records the temperature of the infant and the incubator every 2 hours. The infant‘s temperature is monitored with a heat-sensitive probe that is taped to the abdomen.

questions.chapter_title: Preterm and Postterm Newborns
questions.stem: Why is the postterm neonate at risk for cold stress?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fat stores have been used in utero for nourishment

questions.rationale: Fat stores have been used in utero for nourishment during the extended pregnancy.

questions.chapter_title: Preterm and Postterm Newborns
questions.stem: When assessing a neonate born at 38 weeks of gestation, the nurse records his weight as 8 pounds, 10 ounces. What will the nurse consider this newborn?
questions.rationale: Term infants over 4000 g (8.8 Ib) may be classified as large for gestational age (LGA). For the preterm infant this is less than 38 weeks, for the term infant it is 38 to 42 weeks, and for the postterm infant it is beyond 42 weeks. A late preterm infant, also known as a near-term infant, is born between 34 and 36 weeks.

questions.chapter_title: Preterm and Postterm Newborns
questions.stem: An infant receives surfactant via endotracheal (ET) tube at birth for symptoms of respiratory distress syndrome (RDS). When will the nurse anticipate seeing improvement of lung function?
questions.rationale: In preterm newborns, surfactant can be administered via ET tube at birth or when symptoms of RDS occur, with improvement of lung function seen within 72 hours.

questions.chapter_title: Preterm and Postterm Newborns
questions.stem: The nurse knows that a postterm infant may experience which potential problems? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: The postterm infant should be assessed closely for indication of asphyxia, seizures, and polycythemia.

questions.chapter_title: Preterm and Postterm Newborns
questions.stem: The nurse is caring for a woman who gave birth to a preterm infant. The nurse is aware that what are possible causes of preterm delivery? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: The predisposing causes of preterm birth are numerous; in many instances, the cause is unknown. Prematurity may be caused by multiple births, illness of the mother (e.g., malnutrition, heart disease, diabetes mellitus, or infectious conditions), or the hazards of pregnancy itself, such as gestational hypertension, placental abnormalities that may result in premature rupture of the membranes, placenta previa (in which the placenta lies over the cervix instead of higher in the uterus), and premature separation of the placenta. Studies also indicate the relationships between prematurity and poverty, smoking, alcohol consumption, and abuse of cocaine and other drugs. Hyperemesis gravidarum and chloasma are not risk factors for preterm birth.

questions.chapter_title: Preterm and Postterm Newborns
questions.stem: The nurse assesses a preterm infant in the NICU. What signs should be reported to the physician? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Paleness, vomiting, and bulging fontanelles can indicate complications in the preterm newborn. Transparent skin and superficial scalp veins are expected findings.

questions.chapter_title: Preterm and Postterm Newborns
questions.stem: The nurse clarifies that a fetus has enough surfactant to breathe on its own at the age of weeks.
questions.rationale: Surfactant begins to appear at the age of 24 weeks and is adequate to support life at the age of 34 weeks.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: What occurrence results from obstruction within the ventricles of the brain or inadequate reabsorption of cerebrospinal fluid?
questions.rationale: Hydrocephalus is characterized by an increase in cerebrospinal fluid in the ventricles of the brain.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: The nurse is caring for an infant with hydrocephalus. What nursing action is most important for this nurse to implement?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Keep the head lower than the hip.

questions.rationale: The child with hydrocephalus has a heavy head on a small body with poor muscle tone; the head must be supported when feeding and moving the child to prevent injury to the neck.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: The nurse observes that the infant‘s anterior fontanelle is bulging after placement ofa ventriculoperitoneal shunt. How should the nurse position this infant?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Prone, with the head of the bed elevated

questions.rationale: If the fontanelles are bulging, the child will be positioned in a semi-Fowler‘s position to promote drainage from the ventricles through the shunt.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: What nursing action will the nurse implement after feeding an infant with hydrocephalus?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Position the infant sitting upright in an infant seat.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Place the infant over the shoulder to burp.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Leave the infant in a side-lying position.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stimulate the infant by rubbing its feet.

questions.rationale: Because children with hydrocephalus are prone to vomiting, the child is fed and then positioned in the side-lying position in a quiet atmosphere to reduce the incidence of vomiting.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: A newborn was just admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit with a meningomyelocele. What is the priority preoperative nursing care of this newborn?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Move from side to side every hour.

questions.rationale: The infant is placed prone in a humidified incubator, and the sac is covered with dressings of sterile saline. The infant‘s hips are kept lower than the lesion, and the infant is usually not in diapers.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: The nurse is caring for a child who has had a ventriculoperitoneal shunt (VP) for hydrocephalus and observes an increasing abdominal girth. What is the most appropriate response?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Notify the charge nurse of possible malabsorption.

questions.rationale: An increasing abdominal girth in a child with a VP shunt may be indicative of malabsorption of the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) that is being shunted to the peritoneum.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: The nurse is providing education to parents of a child with cleft palate. What will the nurse instruct the parents to report immediately?
questions.rationale: Children with cleft palate are at risk of ear infections and dental disorders. Parents should be instructed to take the child to the health care provider at the first sign of earache.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: Postoperative nursing care of the infant following surgical repair of a cleft lip would include:

choices.label: A
choices.text: Feeding the infant with a spoon to avoid sucking

choices.label: B
choices.text: Positioning the infant on the abdomen to facilitate drainage

choices.label: C
choices.text: Applying elbow restraints to protect the surgical area

choices.label: D
choices.text: Providing minimal stimulation to prevent injury to the incision

questions.rationale: Elbow restraints are used postoperatively to prevent the infant from damaging the operative area.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: Which statement indicates that parents understand how to feed their infant who had a surgical repair for a cleft lip?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Weare feeding the baby with a dropper for 2 weeks.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “We started the baby on solid food yesterday.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “The baby is drinking well from a straw.”

questions.rationale: The infant is fed with a dropper until the incision is completely healed about | to 2 weeks after surgery.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: An 18-month-old child had a surgical repair of a cleft palate and is now allowed to eat a regular diet. What nursing action is the most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Feed solid foods with the spoon at the side of the mouth.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Puree foods and offer them through a straw.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Place small bites of food in the mouth with a tongue blade.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Offer small, frequent meals of finger foods.

questions.rationale: The primary concern with feeding is to protect the operative site. The child can be fed with a spoon, but only the side of the spoon is placed into the mouth at the side of the mouth. The spoon must not touch the roof of the mouth.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: When bathing an infant, what sign does the nurse recognize as a sign of developmental hip dysplasia?

choices.label: B
choices.text: One leg is shorter than the other

choices.label: C
choices.text: Broadening and flattening of the buttocks

choices.label: D
choices.text: Two skinfolds on the back of each thigh

questions.rationale: When developmental hip dysplasia is present, the leg on the affected side will appear shorter than the leg on the unaffected side.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: A 3-month-old infant is diagnosed with developmental hip dysplasia. The nurse knows that what is the usual treatment for an infant with this diagnosis?
questions.rationale: In infants who are more than 2 months of age, longer-term immobilization with a Pavlik harness is required.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: After delivery, a mother asks the nurse about newborn screening tests. The nurse explains that what is the optimal time for testing for phenylketonuria?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In the first 24 hours of life

questions.rationale: Blood tests for phenylketonuria should be obtained 48 to 72 hours after birth. The newborn will have had enough time to ingest protein through feedings, and the chance of false-negative results will be reduced.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: The nurse is advising parents about feeding their infant with phenylketonuria. What formula and/or diet should the nurse suggest?

choices.label: B
choices.text: A formula that is low in the amino acid leucine

choices.label: D
choices.text: Substitute Lofenalac for some protein foods

questions.rationale: A synthetic food providing enough protein for growth and tissue repair, but little phenylalanine, is substituted for natural protein foods.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: Parents of a 2-month-old infant with Down syndrome are attending a well visit at the pediatric clinic. What should they be instructed to provide special attention to in regard to the generalized hypotonicity of the child?
questions.rationale: The child with Down syndrome has generalized hypotonicity, which caused mucus accumulation and respiratory problems.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: What would the nurse include when instructing parents about positioning their toddler who has just had a body spica cast applied?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Prop the child upright with pillows for meals.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use the bar between the legs to turn the child.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Put the child on her abdomen to sleep.

questions.rationale: The child‘s position must be changed frequently to relieve pressure and promote circulation.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: The nurse is caring for an Rh-negative mother on the labor and birth unit. What scenario indicates this patient will require RaoGAM administration?

choices.label: A
choices.text: She has had one Rh-negative child and is pregnant with an Rh-negative child.

choices.label: B
choices.text: She has had an Rh-positive infant and is pregnant with an Rh-positive fetus.

choices.label: C
choices.text: She has had an O-negative child and is pregnant with a B-negative child.

choices.label: D
choices.text: She is a primipara with an O-negative child.

questions.rationale: The only woman with antibodies against the Rh-positive infant is the Rh-negative woman who has had one Rh-positive child and is now pregnant with another.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: Parents ask the nursery staff what the light does for their jaundiced infant. What is the nurse‘s best response?
questions.rationale: Severe jaundice can cause kernicterus, an accumulation of bilirubin in the brain tissue, which can lead to serious brain damage. The light breaks down excess bilirubin so that it can be excreted.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: Parents of a newborn with a unilateral cleft lip are concerned about having the defect repaired. The nurse explains that a child with a cleft lip usually undergoes surgical repair at which time?
questions.rationale: A cleft lip is repaired by 3 months of age when weight gain is established and the infant is free of infection.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: Phototherapy is instituted for an infant. What is the most appropriate nursing action for the infant having phototherapy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cover the infant‘s head with a hat.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dress the infant lightly in a T-shirt.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reposition the infant at least every 4 to 8 hours.

questions.rationale: The infant‘s eyes are protected with patches to prevent damage from the high-intensity lights.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: The nurse is caring for a macrosomic newborn whose mother has diabetes. What should the nurse assess for with this neonate?
questions.rationale: The newborn of a mother with diabetes is prone to hypoglycemia.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: What assessment made by the nurse would lead the nurse to suspect hip dysplasia?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Limited adduction of the affected side

questions.rationale: The gluteal folds are asymmetrical because the head of the femur has slipped out of the acetabulum. There is also limited abduction of the affected side, and when the legs are flexed the affected leg seems to be shorter.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: The nurse is providing care to a child with Down syndrome. What body system has the highest risk of congenital anomaly in a child with Down syndrome?
questions.rationale: Down syndrome children are prone to deformities of the cardiovascular system.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: The parents of a child diagnosed with cystic fibrosis ask the nurse what caused this disorder. What is the most appropriate response?

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Cystic fibrosis is a malformation present at birth.”

questions.rationale: Inborn errors of metabolism include a number of inherited diseases that affect body chemistry. There may be an absence or a deficiency of a substance necessary for cell metabolism. The deficient substance is usually an enzyme. Almost any organ of the body may be damaged. Examples of inborn errors of metabolism include cystic fibrosis and phenylketonuria (PKU). In disorders of the blood, there is a reduced or missing blood component or an inability of a component to function adequately. Sickle cell disease, thalassemia, and hemophilia fall into this category. Chromosomal abnormalities number in the thousands. Most involve some type of mental retardation, and others are incompatible with life. The newborn with Turner‘s syndrome or Klinefelter‘s syndrome may have impaired physical growth and sexual development. Malformations at birth include several types of structural defects.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: What characteristics are typical in a child diagnosed with Down syndrome? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Children with Down syndrome have close-set upturned eyes, simian creases in palms of hands, protruding tongue, and curved, small fingers. They also have a wide space between their first and second toe and a high incidence of heart defects.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: What will the nurse include in the plan of care when caring for an infant with an intracranial hemorrhage? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Feed slowly to reduce possibility of vomiting.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Stimulate often to maintain level of consciousness.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hold and coddle frequently to stimulate.

questions.rationale: These children should be kept positioned with the head elevated, fed slowly, and monitored for increased intracranial pressure. Children with intracranial hemorrhages are not stimulated and are kept in a quiet environment.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: What would be included in the plan of care for a child just returned to the floor from surgery in which a clubfoot was repaired? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Keep cast uncovered to allow drying.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Circle with a pen any area of bleeding on the cast.

questions.rationale: The casted leg should be kept elevated. All the other options are necessary nursing interventions for a child who is freshly casted.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: The nurse in the newborn nursery is watchful for neonatal abstinence syndrome in the newborn of a mother who took opioids during pregnancy. What would be the manifestations of this syndrome? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: The neonate with abstinence syndrome will have tremors, be hyperirritable and wakeful, have excessive sneezing or yawning, and have no appetite.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: What manifestations of increasing ICP in the hydrocephalic child should the nurse be aware of? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Increased ICP is manifested by high-pitched cry, inequality of pupils, and bulging fontanelles.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: The nurse is obtaining intake information on a new patient being seen for preconception care and notes a family history of neural tube defects. What interventions can the nurse suggest to this woman to help prevent neural tube anomalies in a developing fetus? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: C
choices.text: Take a folic acid supplement every day.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Maintain bed rest during the first trimester.

questions.rationale: The use of drugs during early pregnancy and poor nutrition may contribute to the development of a neural tube defect. The American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) recommends that all women of childbearing age take a daily multivitamin that contains 0.4 mg of folic acid and continue the intake of folic acid until the 12th week of pregnancy, when basic neural tube development is completed. Studies have shown that the intake of folic acid before conception dramatically decreases the occurrence of neural tube defects such as spina bifida. Daily exercise and bed rest do not decrease the risk of neural tube anomalies.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: The nurse is caring for a macrosomic newborn of a woman diagnosed with gestational diabetes immediately after birth. What assessment findings can the nurse anticipate? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Many newborn infants of diabetic mothers have serious complications. When the mother is hyperglycemic, large amounts of glucose are transferred to the fetus. After delivery the infant often has low blood glucose levels because of the abrupt loss of maternal glucose and hypertrophy of the pancreatic islet cells, which results in a temporary overproduction of insulin. Hyperinsulinism, along with excess production of protein and fatty acids, often results in a newborn infant who weighs more than 4082 g (9 lb). These infants suffer from hypoglycemia, hypocalcemia, and hyperbilirubinemia.

questions.chapter_title: The Newborn with a Perinatal Injury or Congenital Malformation
questions.stem: The home health nurse is educating parents on home phototherapy. What will the nurse include when providing information to these parents? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cover the infant‘s eyes when under the light.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Place the light source on an absorbent surface.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Expose as much skin as possible.

questions.rationale: Parents should be instructed to use a three-prong plug for safety, keep a diaper in place, and expose as much skin as possible. The light source should be placed on a nonabsorbent surface, not on carpet or in a crib. It is not necessary to cover the infant‘s eyes when under the light.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
questions.stem: What type of development is the nurse assessing when an infant can lift his or her head before he or she can sit?
questions.rationale: Cephalocaudal development proceeds from head to toe.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
questions.stem: What is a unique organization of characteristics that determines an individual‘s pattern of behavior?
questions.rationale: One definition of personality states that it is a unique organization of characteristics that determines the individual‘s typical or recurrent pattern of behavior.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
questions.stem: An infant's birth weight is 7 pounds, 8 ounces. What can the nurse project the weight to be at 6 months?
questions.rationale: An infant usually doubles his or her birth weight by 5 to 6 months.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
questions.stem: What would the nurse further investigate when assessing patterns of growth in a child?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Previous weight was in the 75th percentile, and present weight is in the 25th percentile.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Height is in the 90th percentile, and weight is in the 75th percentile.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Last weight was in the Sth percentile, and present weight is in the 10th percentile.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Weight is in the 50th percentile, and sibling‘s weight at the same age was in the 75th percentile.

questions.rationale: The child showing a difference of two or more percentile levels from an established growth pattern should undergo further evaluation.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
questions.stem: A mother reports that she and her husband have had one child together, but both have children from previous marriages living in their home. The nurse will base the care planning on what type of family?
questions.rationale: A blended family involves the remarriage of persons with children.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
questions.stem: The mother of a 7-month-old infant reports that the first lower central incisor has erupted. She asks the nurse, “How many teeth will he have by his first birthday?” The nurse explains that the infant will have how many teeth by | year of age?
questions.rationale: The 1-year-old infant usually has about 6 teeth, 4 above and 2 below.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
questions.stem: Ata well-baby visit, parents of a 6-month-old infant ask when to take the infant for the first dental visit. What is the nurse‘s best response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Tf the teeth are brushed regularly, the child should see a dentist by 3 years of age.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “The first dental visit should be arranged after the first tooth erupts.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “The child should have a dental examination when all deciduous teeth have erupted.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “A dental visit by 1 year of age is recommended by the American Academy of Pediatric Dentistry.”

questions.rationale: The Academy of Pediatric Dentistry recommends that the first dental visit occur by | year of age.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
questions.stem: The nurse is planning anticipatory guidance for a caregiver of a preschool-age child. The nurse will explain that permanent teeth begin erupting at what age?
questions.rationale: Permanent teeth do not erupt through the gums until the sixth year.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
questions.stem: A mother asks the nurse how much food should be offered to her 2-year-old child. What is a good rule of thumb for serving size (in tablespoons) per year of age?
questions.rationale: The rule of thumb for serving sizes is to offer 1 tablespoon of each food group per year of age.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
questions.stem: An assessment of a child‘s nutritional status reveals the child is alert, with shiny hair, firm gums, firm mucous membranes, and regular elimination. How would this child‘s nutritional status be described?
questions.rationale: Well-nourished children show steady gains in height and weight and have shiny hair, firm gums and mucous membranes, and regular elimination.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
questions.stem: The nurse encourages a Puerto Rican family to bring food to a child because he is not eating the food served on his hospital tray. What can the nurse expect the child to eat?
questions.rationale: A common food choice of Americans of Puerto Rican descent is dried beans mixed with rice.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
questions.stem: The nurse observes that a 2-year-old toddler is able to use a spoon steadily at mealtime. What does self-feeding help to develop in the toddler?
questions.rationale: By the end of the second year, toddlers can feed themselves. This helps them to develop a sense of independence.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
questions.stem: What activity would the nurse choose to meet Erikson‘s developmental task of industry when caring for a 7-year-old child?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Playing a game of “I Spy” with the nurse

choices.label: D
choices.text: Coloring a picture in a coloring book

questions.rationale: In the developmental period of late childhood, children are striving to develop a sense of industry. The completion of a jigsaw puzzle is industrious play.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
questions.stem: What does the nurse recognize as an example of Piaget‘s concrete operational thinking?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A 2-year-old child says, “It‘s nighttime” when his room is darkened.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A 4-year-old child refers to the hospital as “my house.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: A 5-year-old child coloring a picture of a puppy says, “This is my puppy.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: A 7-year-old child says, “I am sick because I have germs in my chest.”

questions.rationale: The 7-year-old child‘s remark reflecting the cause and effect of germs and illness is an example of operational thinking. All other options are examples of preoperational thought, which is egocentric and symbolic.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
questions.stem: The nurse has discussed with a mother the process of introducing solid foods to her 6-month-old infant. What statement by the mother leads the nurse to determine that learning has taken place?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Twill give my infant rice cereal first.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “I will give my infant yellow vegetables first.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Twill give my infant egg yolks first.”

questions.rationale: Solid foods are usually introduced at about 6 months of age, starting with rice cereal, which is the least allergenic.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
questions.stem: What is the best nursing action when an 8-year-old child comes to the school nurse with his central incisor in his hand and reports he knocked his tooth out on the water fountain?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Give him an ice cube to suck on.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Have him wash his mouth out with peroxide and water.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Wrap the tooth in a clean tissue.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Wash off the tooth and place it in a container of milk.

questions.rationale: The tooth should be washed off and put in a container of milk to preserve it for possible reimplantation.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
