questions.stem: The mother of a 7-month-old infant states, “The baby is eating food now. Should I give him regular milk, too?” What is the nurse‘s best response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “You should give the baby low-fat milk.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Try the milk. See if he has any digestive problems.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Continue breast milk or iron-fortified formula until 1 year of age.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “At this age, infants can tolerate lactose-free or soy-based milk.”

questions.rationale: Whole milk should not be introduced before 1 year of age. Low-fat milk should not be introduced before 2 years of age.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
questions.stem: When a small group of preschool-age children were playing house, each child was pretending to be a particular family member. What type of play does the nurse recognize these children are participating in?
questions.rationale: In cooperative play, children play with each other, each taking a specific role.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
questions.stem: When the nurse asks a 10-year-old Native American if he is ready to go to therapy, he does not answer immediately. How does the nurse interpret this response?
questions.rationale: Native Americans value silence. They need to sit and consider matters before replying to questions.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
questions.stem: A mother tells the nurse, “My 11-month-old son is not as active as my other children were at this age. He is the youngest of four and the older children love to dote on him.” Which factor is influencing this child‘s language development?
questions.rationale: Motor development of the youngest child may be prolonged if the child is babied by others in the family.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
questions.stem: A mother tells her 4-year-old child that balls should be played with outside and not inside the house. Why is the child likely to obey the rule?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The child does not want to be punished.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The child wants to please her mother.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The child believes that following the rules is right.

questions.rationale: According to Kohlberg, children in the preconventional stage (4 to 7 years) are obedient to their parents for fear of punishment.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
questions.stem: What should the nurse avoid when demonstrating a bath procedure to parents of Vietnamese origin?
questions.rationale: The Vietnamese are very sensitive about anyone touching a child‘s head because that is where consciousness lies.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
questions.stem: What does the nurse calculate the basal metabolic index (BMI) of an 8-year-old child who is 48 inches tall (1.2 meters) and weighs 100 pounds (45.4 kg) to be?
questions.rationale: The formula for BMI calculation is weight in kg divided by height in meters (squared): 45.4 (weight in kg) divided by 1.4 (1.2 squared) = 32.4. A BMI of over 30 is classified as obese.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
questions.stem: What toy is developmentally appropriate for the nurse to suggest to entertain a 5-year-old child?
questions.rationale: At this age children are into creative play. The model airport with toy planes is the most developmentally appropriate.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
questions.stem: The nurse caring for a 4-year-old postoperative patient instructs him to blow bubbles. What nursing intervention is the nurse most likely implementing by using this form of therapeutic play?
questions.rationale: Play can also be therapeutic and aid in the recovery process. An example of therapeutic play is the game of having the child blow bubbles to promote deep breathing.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
questions.stem: The mother of a 7-year-old pediatric patient asks the nurse about her child‘s sleep requirement. What is the most accurate response by the nurse?

choices.label: B
choices.text: “5 to 7 hours a night with one daytime nap”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “4 to 6 hours a night with two daytime naps”

questions.rationale: Sleep patterns vary with age. The neonate sleeps 8 to 9 hours per night and naps an equal amount of time during the day. The 2-year-old child may sleep 10 hours during the night and have only one short daytime nap. The 7-year-old child usually requires 11 to 13 hours of sleep and rarely has a daytime nap. These patterns may be altered by cultural practices.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
questions.stem: How do children differ from adults? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Greater surface area in relation to their weight

choices.label: E
choices.text: Continuously changing growth and development pattern

questions.rationale: Children are in a continuous growth and development pattern. Children have a greater surface area and a higher metabolic rate. All of their organ systems are not mature.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
questions.stem: What approaches should the nurse suggest for introducing a toddler to new foods? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Serve one food at a time.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Avoid showing personal likes or dislikes.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Offer foods in small amounts, less than a teaspoon.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Entice the toddler to eat with sweets.

questions.rationale: Foods should be introduced in small, warm servings, one food at a time. Sweets and milk should not be offered until after solid food.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
questions.stem: Which healthy snack foods would the school nurse suggest to a group of adolescents? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Cheese and raw vegetables are acceptable healthy snacks. Bubble gum, chocolate-covered peanuts, and dried fruits all contain high amounts of sugar.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
questions.stem: The nurse suggests to the parents of an obese 10-year-old child that they use the Portion Plate for Kids place mat. How does this tool help with selection of portion sizes? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: C
choices.text: Portion measurement in tablespoons for common food

choices.label: D
choices.text: Calorie values for cup-size portions of common foods

choices.label: E
choices.text: Familiar objects such as a deck of cards to measure servings

questions.rationale: The Portion Plate for Kids is a place mat that uses common objects such as a deck of playing cards or a baseball to measure serving portions.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
questions.stem: An educational program is being presented to pediatric nurses on the relationship of play to childhood development. What information should be included in this presentation? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Art play should be used sparingly.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use of computer/video games is detrimental.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Understanding of child—parent relationships can be gained by observing play.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Play provides a sense of accomplishment.

questions.rationale: Art is an appropriate play activity at almost any age and provides an avenue for experimentation as well as for creative expression and a feeling of accomplishment in the child. Observing the child at play can aid in assessing growth and development and understanding the child‘s relationships with family members. Any plan of care for a hospitalized child of any age should include a play activity that either encourages growth and development or encourages the expression of thoughts and feelings. Computer programs are popular with all age groups, providing problem-solving skills, manipulative skills, and opportunities for new learning.

questions.chapter_title: An Overview of Growth, Development, and Nutrition
questions.stem: Parents attending a well visit for their 11-year-old son verbalize concern over his computer use. When asked about it, the boy states, “I play games on my computer for | hour a day.” The nurse knows that computer games can provide what opportunities to childhood development? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Computer programs are popular with all age groups, providing problem-solving skills, manipulative skills, and opportunities for new learning.

questions.chapter_title: The Infant
questions.stem: A mother calls the pediatrician‘s office because her infant is “colicky.” What is the most helpful measure the nurse can suggest to the mother?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sing songs to the infant in a soft voice.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Place the infant in a well-lit room.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Walk around and massage the infant‘s back.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rock the fussy infant slowly and gently.

questions.rationale: One technique the nurse can offer parents of a fussy infant is to rock the infant gently and slowly while being careful to avoid sudden movements.

questions.chapter_title: The Infant
questions.stem: When does the posterior fontanelle close?
questions.rationale: The posterior fontanelle closes between 2 and 3 months of age.

questions.chapter_title: The Infant
questions.stem: At what age does an infant‘s birth weight triple?
questions.rationale: The infant usually triples his or her birth weight by about 12 months of age.

questions.chapter_title: The Infant
questions.stem: What is the earliest age at which an infant is able to sit steadily alone?
questions.rationale: The infant can sit alone without support at about 8 months of age.

questions.chapter_title: The Infant
questions.stem: What is the earliest age at which the infant should be able to walk independently?
questions.rationale: For the majority of children, the milestone of walking alone is achieved between 12 and 15 months.

questions.chapter_title: The Infant
questions.stem: The parent of a 3-month-old infant asks the nurse, “At what age do infants usually begin drinking from a cup?” What is the nurse‘s most accurate response?
questions.rationale: The infant can usually drink from a cup when it is offered at about 9 months.

questions.chapter_title: The Infant
questions.stem: What would the nurse expect a 4-month-old infant to be able to accomplish?
questions.rationale: Because development is cephalocaudal, of these choices, lifting the head and shoulders is the one that the infant learns to do first. The infant can usually sit with support at about 5 months of age and can sit alone at about 8 months.

questions.chapter_title: The Infant
questions.stem: What is an abnormal finding in an evaluation of growth and development for a 6-month-old infant?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Weight gain of 4 to 7 ounces per week

choices.label: B
choices.text: Length increase of | inch in 2 months

choices.label: D
choices.text: Can sit alone for a few seconds

questions.rationale: The infant should be holding the head up well by 5 months of age. If head lag is present at 6 months, the child should undergo further evaluation.

questions.chapter_title: The Infant
questions.stem: A parent brings a 6-month-old infant to the pediatric clinic for her well-baby examination. Her birth weight was 8 pounds, 2 ounces. What will the nurse weighing the infant today expect her weight to be?
questions.rationale: Birth weight is usually doubled by 6 months of age.

questions.chapter_title: The Infant
questions.stem: What will the nurse advise a parent to do when introducing solid foods?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Begin with one tablespoon of food.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Eliminate a refused food from the diet.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Introduce each new food 4 to 7 days apart.

questions.rationale: Only one new food is offered in a 4- to 7-day period to determine tolerance.

questions.chapter_title: The Infant
questions.stem: The nurse is talking with a parent about tooth eruption. What teeth will the nurse explain are the first deciduous teeth to erupt?
questions.rationale: The first teeth to erupt, usually at about 7 months, are the lower central incisors.

questions.chapter_title: The Infant
questions.stem: The nurse is assessing development in a 9-month-old infant. What would the nurse expect to observe?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Beginning to use a spoon rather sloppily

questions.rationale: The 9-month-old infant tries to creep, has developed pincer movement, and can grasp a spoon without keeping food on it.

questions.chapter_title: The Infant
questions.stem: What statement made by a parent indicates correct understanding of infant feeding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “T‘ve been mixing rice cereal and formula in the baby‘s bottle.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “I switched the baby to low-fat milk at 9 months.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “The baby really likes little pieces of chocolate.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “TI give the baby new foods before he takes his bottle.”

questions.rationale: New solid foods should be introduced before formula or breast milk to encourage the infant to try new foods.

questions.chapter_title: The Infant
questions.stem: A mother is concerned because her 10-month-old infant is lethargic. What is the best action the nurse can advise this mother to implement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Keep the infant‘s room well lit.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Handle the infant slowly and gently.

questions.rationale: Some infants respond to stimulating environments by shutting down. Move and handle infants slowly and gently.

questions.chapter_title: The Infant
questions.stem: The nurse discusses child-proofing the home for safety with the mother of a 9-month-old infant. Which statement made by the mother would indicate an unsafe behavior?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “T put covers on all of the electrical outlets.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “In the car, she rides in a front-facing car seat.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “There are locks on all of the cabinets in the house.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Ihave a gate at the top and bottom of the stairs.”

questions.rationale: A rear-facing infant car seat should be used for infants younger than | year of age.

questions.chapter_title: The Infant
questions.stem: The nurse observes a 10-month-old infant using her index finger and thumb to pick up pieces of cereal. What does this behavior indicate the infant has developed?
questions.rationale: By | year, the pincer-grasp coordination of index finger and thumb is well established.

questions.chapter_title: The Infant
questions.stem: A parent is concerned because her infant has a diaper rash. What is the best action the nurse would advise the parent to implement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use commercial diaper wipes to clean the area.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Apply a protective ointment on the area.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Change the infant‘s diaper less frequently.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Keep the diaper area covered all of the time.

questions.rationale: A protective ointment can be applied when the skin in the diaper area appears pink and irritated.

questions.chapter_title: The Infant
questions.stem: The mother of an infant born prematurely tells the nurse, “The baby is irritable. She cries during diaper changes and feedings. Can you make some suggestions about what I should do to soothe her?” What is the most appropriate recommendation to help this parent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Play the radio or TV while you feed the infant.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Put the infant in a room with sunlight.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Wrap the infant snugly when you hold them.

questions.rationale: A strategy that may be helpful is to swaddle the infant snugly in a light blanket with extremities flexed and hands near the face.

questions.chapter_title: The Infant
questions.stem: What is the most appropriate activity to recommend to parents to promote sensorimotor stimulation for a 1-year-old infant?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Spend time in an infant swing.

questions.rationale: Push-pull toys are appropriate to promote sensorimotor stimulation for a 1-year-old infant.

questions.chapter_title: The Infant
questions.stem: Which statement indicates the mother of an 8-month-old infant understands infant sleep patterns?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “T put the baby in my bed until she falls asleep, then I put her in her crib.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “I let the baby skip an afternoon nap so that she will fall asleep earlier.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “T put the pacifier in the crib so that she can find it when she wakes up.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Trock the baby back to sleep if she wakes up at night.”

questions.rationale: The parent should assist the infant to develop self-soothing behaviors so that the infant can get back to sleep on her own.

questions.chapter_title: The Infant
questions.stem: How might the nurse demonstrate the parachute reflex with an infant?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lifting the infant high in the air above her head

choices.label: B
choices.text: Holding the infant in a football hold, cradling the head

choices.label: C
choices.text: Seating the infant in a stroller in an upright position

choices.label: D
choices.text: Placing the infant downward into the crib

questions.rationale: The infant, when placed downward in a prone position, will protectively extend the arms.

questions.chapter_title: The Infant
questions.stem: Parents of a 6-month-old infant ask the nurse why it is necessary to offer iron-rich formula to their child. What is the correct response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “The infant has limited ability to produce red blood cells.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “The infant has exhausted maternal iron stores.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “The infant has need of the iron to support dentition.”

questions.rationale: It is necessary to offer iron-rich formula to the children when they exhausted maternal iron stores.

questions.chapter_title: The Infant
questions.stem: The nurse is assessing a 1-year-old infant in the pediatric office. What finding should the nurse report to the physician immediately?
questions.rationale: Respirations of a 1-year-old infant should be 20 to 40 breaths/minute. Increased respiratory rate can lead to distress and should be reported immediately. Pulse rate of 100 to 140 beats/minute is normal. Minimal verbalization and fussy behavior are not emergency situations or abnormal for this age.

questions.chapter_title: The Infant
questions.stem: Anew mother is voicing concern she is breastfeeding her newborn too frequently. How often does the nurse instruct this mother she should expect her newborn to feed?
questions.rationale: Breastfed infants may require feedings at 2- to 3-hour intervals because breast milk is more easily digested. A flexible but regular schedule that provides a rest period between feedings is best for the parent and infant.

questions.chapter_title: The Infant
questions.stem: The nurse cautions that children who have unmet hunger needs will likely display which characteristic(s)? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Children who experience frequent hunger do not have effective parental bonding. All other options are probable outcomes for a child who has unmet hunger needs.

questions.chapter_title: The Infant
questions.stem: The nurse is preparing to outline principles of discipline for parents of an infant. What information should the nurse include? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Distract the child to another activity.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bribe the child with a sweet treat.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ignore the child until behavior improves.

questions.rationale: Parental approval is important to the infant, and setting limits early is essential. Principles of discipline at this age include the following: lowering the voice to say no firmly, removing the child from the situation, distraction, and consistency.

questions.chapter_title: The Infant
questions.stem: What should the teaching plan include about infant fall precautions? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Keep crib rails up and in locked position.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Steady infant with hand when on changing table.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use tray attachment on high chair as restraint.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Keep infant seat on the floor while indoors.

questions.rationale: The tray attachment to a high chair is an inadequate restraint. All other options are good precautions to prevent an infant from a fall.

questions.chapter_title: The Infant
questions.stem: The nurse is aware that the 7-month-old infant can signal feeding readiness bywhich action(s)? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Biting at spoon with upper and lower incisors

choices.label: D
choices.text: Bouncing up and down with excitement at sight of food

questions.rationale: The 7-month-old infant pulls the spoon toward his or her mouth and can manipulate finger foods. The 7-month-old infant does not have upper incisors and has not developed adequately to recognize the food container or exhibit excitement related to the sight of food.

questions.chapter_title: The Infant
questions.stem: The nurse is educating parents of a 2-month-old infant about immunizations. What immunizations against illness should their child receive? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: The first DPT, polio, and flu immunizations are given at the age of 2 months.

questions.chapter_title: The Infant
questions.stem: What will the nurse take into consideration when educating parents regarding infant nutrition? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Parents have many concerns about feeding their infant during the first year of life. This is a period when readiness to receive nutrition education is usually high; therefore, the nurse looks for opportunities to provide accurate information. Assessment of parental knowledge; infant development, behavior, and readiness; parent-child interaction; and cultural and ethnic practices is important. Sex of the infant does not enter into nutritional education.

questions.chapter_title: The Infant
questions.stem: Parents of an infant inform the nurse they are planning home preparation of solid foods. What directions should the nurse provide? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Boil foods in a large amount of water.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Add 1 teaspoon of salt per cup.

questions.rationale: Home-prepared infant food can be strained and pureed in an electric blender. Sugar should be added sparingly. Food should be boiled in small amounts of water and not over cooked to avoid destroying nutrients. Foods may be frozen in ice cube trays and defrosted for use.

questions.chapter_title: The Toddler
questions.stem: Which behavior reported by a parent of an 18-month-old toddler would the nurse report to the pediatrician as a cause for concern?
questions.rationale: By 18 months, a toddler should have been walking alone for several months. The toddler who walks holding onto furniture should be evaluated by a developmental specialist.

questions.chapter_title: The Toddler
questions.stem: What would the nurse assessing growth and development of a 2-year-old child expect to find?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The child jumps with both feet.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The child can hop on one foot.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The child has a vocabulary of 900 words.

questions.rationale: The 2-year-old child can jump with both feet. The remaining achievements occur after 2 years of age.

questions.chapter_title: The Toddler
questions.stem: A parent remarks, “My 18-month-old daughter carries her blanket around everywhere. Is this normal?” What is the best explanation a nurse who has an understanding of toddler development might give?

choices.label: A
choices.text: She carries her blanket because she is ritualistic.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Carrying her favorite blanket is self-consoling behavior.

choices.label: C
choices.text: This behavior can be discouraged by offering new toys to the child.

choices.label: D
choices.text: This could be indicative of emotional distress.

questions.rationale: Favorite possessions and repetitive rituals are self-consoling behaviors for the toddler.

questions.chapter_title: The Toddler
questions.stem: The nurse observed three toddlers playing side by side with dolls. Closer observation revealed that the children were not interacting with one another. What type of play is this?
questions.rationale: Toddlers engage in parallel play. Children play next to, but not with, each other.

questions.chapter_title: The Toddler
questions.stem: What instruction would the nurse include when planning anticipatory guidance for parents of a toddler?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adhere to a rigid schedule because the toddler is ritualistic.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Shoes should fit snugly at the toe and arch.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Dress the toddler in pants with a zipper so that he or she can learn to zip and unzip clothes.

questions.rationale: Limit-setting should include praise as well as disapproval for undesired behavior.

questions.chapter_title: The Toddler
questions.stem: What is the best advice the nurse can offer a parent concerned because her 2-year-old child is very active and does not eat much?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Insist that the child eat one food on the plate.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Help the child wind down with a quiet activity before mealtime.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Maintain a consistent eating schedule for the family.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Serve the meal with a variety of interesting plates, cups, and utensils.

questions.rationale: Quiet time before meals provides an opportunity for the active toddler to wind down.

questions.chapter_title: The Toddler
questions.stem: How would the nurse advise a parent who states, “I never know how much food to feed my child”?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Serving sizes should not exceed 1 teaspoon of each type of food.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Food quantities must be carefully measured to avoid overfeeding.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use | tablespoon of each food for each year of age as a guideline.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A toddler should eat three balanced meals. Snacks are not necessary.

questions.rationale: A tablespoon of each type of food for each year of age is a good guideline to follow when determining serving sizes.

questions.chapter_title: The Toddler
questions.stem: The nurse is discussing toilet training with parents. What behavior by the child would identify toilet training readiness?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Willing to sit on the potty for 15 to 20 minutes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dry in the daytime for 4-hour periods

choices.label: C
choices.text: Able to communicate that he or she is wet

questions.rationale: Children are ready for toilet training when they can communicate in some fashion that they are wet or need to urinate or defecate.

questions.chapter_title: The Toddler
questions.stem: What is the most appropriate toy for the nurse to select for a normal 2-year-old child?
questions.rationale: The 2-year-old child enjoys playing with objects that can be pushed or pulled.

questions.chapter_title: The Toddler
questions.stem: What could the nurse recommend to a child‘s mother to encourage a toddler to practice independence?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Offer a variety of items to choose from to stimulate his mind.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Allow the child to determine his own daily routine.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Offer him a choice between two items.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Set the routine herself, but discuss with her toddler how he or she would have done it differently.

questions.rationale: The toddler can be allowed to make choices as the situation warrants, but the number of choices should be limited because too many confuse the toddler.

questions.chapter_title: The Toddler
questions.stem: Ona home visit, the nurse notes that the parents require teaching intervention to protect the 15-month-old child who lives there. What observation would lead the nurse to this conclusion?

choices.label: B
choices.text: The dining room table has a tablecloth on it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: There are paintings on the wall.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The kitchen floor is clean but not shiny.

questions.rationale: A tablecloth presents a safety hazard because the curious toddler will reach up and pull on it. The toddler could be injured if items on the table are moved when the tablecloth is pulled.

questions.chapter_title: The Toddler
questions.stem: What does the nurse consider as an appropriate snack for a 2-year-old child?
questions.rationale: Applesauce is a healthy and safe snack food for the toddler. The toddler is at risk for choking on foods such as grapes, hot dogs, and popcorn.

questions.chapter_title: The Toddler
questions.stem: Which finding would concern the nurse assessing vital signs on a 2-year-old child?
questions.rationale: In the toddler period, the respiratory rate decreases to 25 breaths/minute.

questions.chapter_title: The Toddler
questions.stem: What would be an expected finding when assessing language development in a 2-year-old child?
questions.rationale: The 2-year-old child should be using two-word sentences.

questions.chapter_title: The Toddler
questions.stem: The nurse is planning to explain the use of time-outs to the parent of a 3-year-old child. How many minutes will the nurse indicate is appropriate for a child of this age?
questions.rationale: Timing for time-out is usually based on 1 minute per year of age.

questions.chapter_title: The Toddler
questions.stem: The parent of a toddler tells the nurse, “My daughter‘s appetite has decreased. Thank goodness she loves to drink milk.” What is the most appropriate response by the nurse?

choices.label: B
choices.text: “How much milk does she drink in a day?”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Has she become a fussy eater, too?”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Have you tried offering her finger foods?”

questions.rationale: Milk should be limited to 24 ounces a day. Too few solid foods can lead to dietary deficiencies of iron.

questions.chapter_title: The Toddler
questions.stem: How many hours should toddlers be able to stay dry for the nurse to suggest they are ready to begin bladder training?
questions.rationale: If the toddler is mature enough to retain urine for 2 hours, bladder training can be effective.

questions.chapter_title: The Toddler
questions.stem: Parents tell the nurse they are frustrated with their toddler‘s recent behavior and refusal to agree with anything they ask of them. What does the nurse explain as the term for when a toddler tests their own power?
questions.rationale: By refusing to eat, dress, sleep, or anything else by saying “No,” toddlers test their own power to control. Because toddlers are also egocentric, they come to believe that their negativism is absolute. This is especially true if the adults give into it.

questions.chapter_title: The Toddler
questions.stem: The nurse is assessing a 3-year-old toddler. What is the expected weight gain for this age child?
questions.rationale: The expected weight of a 2 YA-year-old toddler is four times the birth weight.

questions.chapter_title: The Toddler
questions.stem: What guideline should an adult follow when speaking to a toddler?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Beat eye level with the child.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hold by the shoulders to keep the child‘s attention.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Seat the child to focus on conversation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Speak in a firm strong voice.

questions.rationale: Being at eye level is helpful to hold the child‘s attention and is especially important when the child is frightened.

questions.chapter_title: The Toddler
questions.stem: Why does day care for the toddler differ from that of the preschooler?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Toddlers have a shorter attention span.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Toddlers are less prone to environmental dangers.

questions.rationale: Toddlers have a shorter attention span than preschoolers and are prone to investigate other opportunities in the environment that may put them in harm‘s way. Toddlers are more interested in parallel play.

questions.chapter_title: The Toddler
questions.stem: A 16-month-old child is attending a well-child visit at a pediatric clinic. Which assessment would indicate the biggest cause for concern?
questions.rationale: A child should be walking independently by 16 months. It is normal for a child this age to prefer finger feeding and to be limited to single words. Many children do not climb steps until 24 months of age.

questions.chapter_title: The Toddler
questions.stem: When selecting a potty chair, the parents are encouraged to select one that has which characteristic(s)? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Small enough for the child‘s feet to touch floor

choices.label: C
choices.text: Supportive of child‘s back and arms

choices.label: E
choices.text: Capable of being taken apart easily

questions.rationale: Potty chairs should be small and sturdy and supportive of the child‘s back and arms. The composition is not important as long as it is stable.

questions.chapter_title: The Toddler
questions.stem: The nurse suggests offering which food(s) to support the toddler‘s desire to self-feed? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: E
choices.text: Foods that are varied and colorful

questions.rationale: Finger foods that are varied and colorful and served in colorful dishes at a moderate temperature are all attractive. Foods can be chopped into small pieces but not pureed.

questions.chapter_title: The Toddler
questions.stem: The nurse points out which physiological change(s) in the toddler that serve(s) as protection against disease? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: D
choices.text: Elevation in white blood cell count

questions.rationale: With the exception of an increased white blood cell (WBC) count, which is always pathological, the other options are all maturing changes that equip the toddler to better fight disease.

questions.chapter_title: The Toddler
questions.stem: Parents of a toddler are discussing the emotion of fear with the pediatric nurse. What information can the nurse offer regarding fear and the toddler? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: C
choices.text: Teasing the child can decrease fear.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Once fear is learned it is difficult to eliminate.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Adults should openly share their fears.

questions.rationale: Once a fear has been learned, it is more difficult to eliminate. Clinging to favorite possessions and repetitive rituals are self-consoling behaviors for the toddler, particularly at bedtime and during separation from parents. Stress increases fear of separation. Adults should attempt to control their own fears in the presence of young children. Respect and understanding should always be accorded to children who are afraid. Making fun of the fear or shaming the child in front of others is detrimental to self-esteem.

questions.chapter_title: The Toddler
questions.stem: The nurse assessing a 2-year-old is satisfied to see that the present weight of the child is times their birth weight.
questions.rationale: The birth weight has usually tripled by the time the child is 2 years of age.

questions.chapter_title: The Preschool Child
questions.stem: Which statement best describes the 3-year-old child?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Helpful, wants to assist with chores

questions.rationale: Three-year-old children are helpful and can assist in simple household chores.

questions.chapter_title: The Preschool Child
questions.stem: The parents of a 4-year-old boy are concerned because they have noticed him frequently touching his penis. What knowledge would act as the basis for the nurse‘s response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: This behavior indicates a normal curiosity about sexuality.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Masturbation suggests the boy has an excessive fear of castration.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is usually a result of discomfort from a penile rash or irritation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The behavior is abnormal and the child should be referred for counseling.

questions.rationale: Masturbation at this age is common and indicates that the preschooler has a normal curiosity about sexuality.

questions.chapter_title: The Preschool Child
questions.stem: A preschool child is asked, “Why do trees have leaves?” Which response would be an example of animism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “So Ican have shade over my sandbox.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “To hide behind when they are scared.”

questions.rationale: Animism describes the tendency of preschool children to attribute human characteristics to nonhuman objects.

questions.chapter_title: The Preschool Child
questions.stem: What tasks would be appropriate to expect of a 5-year-old child?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Setting the table with paper plates

choices.label: C
choices.text: Carrying glasses from the table to the sink

choices.label: D
choices.text: Scrubbing out the sink with cleanser

questions.rationale: Parents must consider developmental level and safety when asking the 5-year-old child to help with chores.

questions.chapter_title: The Preschool Child
questions.stem: A 3-year-old child, while playing with his favorite toy in the playroom of the pediatric unit, is approached by another child who also wants to play with the same toy. What behavior will the nurse anticipate from this child?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Will play well with the other child.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Will give the toy up and then not play anymore.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Will become angry and a physical response might ensue.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Will ignore the toy and go on to something else.

questions.rationale: The 3-year-old child is egocentric and likely will become angry when others attempt to take his or her possessions.

questions.chapter_title: The Preschool Child
questions.stem: A parent is concerned about her children‘s reaction should their grandmother die. What understanding will guide the nurse‘s response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Children are unlikely to notice their grandmother‘s absence if no one reminds them.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Young children often understand that other people die, but do not equate it with themselves.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The children‘s response will depend entirely on whether they have beenacquainted with death before this.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Children can understand the concept of a higher being much like adults can.

questions.rationale: Between 3 and 4 years of age, the children become curious about death and dying. They may realize that others die, but they do not relate death to themselves.

questions.chapter_title: The Preschool Child
questions.stem: What is the most appropriate intervention when dealing with occasional aggression in a 4-year-old child?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Have the child take a time-out in the corner for 4 minutes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Spank the child at the time of the incident.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Take away television privileges for the day.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Send the child to his room for 30 minutes.

questions.rationale: Time-out periods, usually lasting 1 minute per year of age, with the child sitting in a chair or corner, are considered an effective disciplinary technique.

questions.chapter_title: The Preschool Child
questions.stem: A father is concerned about how long his preschool-age child will continue sucking his thumb. What is the most helpful response from the nurse?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Most children will stop thumb-sucking naturally by school age.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Over-the-counter treatments that give a bad taste can be placed on the thumb to discourage the practice.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Consistently touching the child‘s fingers whenever he sucks his thumb is most effective.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Thumb-sucking is detrimental to the eruption of the child‘s teeth and must be stopped as soon as possible.”

questions.rationale: Most children give up the habit of thumb-sucking by the time they reach school.

questions.chapter_title: The Preschool Child
questions.stem: How does the nurse characterize the play of 5-year-old children?
questions.rationale: The 5-year-old child wants to play by the rules but cannot accept losing. The rules may be very strict or change as the game progresses.

questions.chapter_title: The Preschool Child
questions.stem: The nurse is discussing preschoolers‘ sexual curiosity with the parent. What statement bythe mother leads the nurse to determine that the mother understands the information?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Make up funny words for body parts.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Distract the child with a toy if they ask about sex.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Tell them to ask you again when they are 6 years old.”

questions.rationale: Parents should provide sex education at the time the child asks about sex.

questions.chapter_title: The Preschool Child
questions.stem: What type of play is most appropriate when planning care for a child with moderate intellectual deficiency?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Be educationally oriented to make up for lost time.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Be adjusted to mental age rather than chronological age.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Involve contact sports and aggressive physical activity with other children.

questions.rationale: The nurse must consider the child‘s mental age rather than her chronological age when selecting toys for play.

questions.chapter_title: The Preschool Child
questions.stem: What is the nurse‘s best advice to a parent about a preschooler‘s “imaginaryfriend”?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Having imaginary friends is a sign that the child has low self-esteem.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is common for preschoolers to have imaginary friends.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Preschoolers invent an imaginary friend when they feel overwhelmed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The best approach to dealing with an imaginary friend is to ignore them.

questions.rationale: Imaginary friends are common and normal during the preschool period and serve many purposes, such as relief from loneliness, mastery of fears, and acting as a scapegoat.

questions.chapter_title: The Preschool Child
questions.stem: What intervention might the nurse suggest as helpful for the child with enuresis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Applying an electric pad that gently shocks the child

choices.label: B
choices.text: Waking the child several times during the night to urinate

choices.label: C
choices.text: Decreasing fluid intake after the evening meal

questions.rationale: Ifa child is experiencing enuresis, liquids after dinner should be limited and the child should routinely void before going to bed.

questions.chapter_title: The Preschool Child
questions.stem: What should the nurse suggest as the most appropriate toy choice for a 3-year-old?

choices.label: B
choices.text: A small pet, such as a goldfish

questions.rationale: Large construction sets are suitable toys for the preschool-age child.

questions.chapter_title: The Preschool Child
questions.stem: The parent of a 3 vA -year-old child tells the nurse, “My daughter points instead of speaking whenever she wants me to get something for her, but she understands me when I ask her to do something.” Based on the parent‘s comment, what does the nurse suspect?
questions.rationale: An expressive language delay is suspected when the child understands spoken language but is not talking.

questions.chapter_title: The Preschool Child
questions.stem: The parent of a 4 WA -year-old child tells the nurse, “Bedtime is difficult. I can‘t get my son to go to bed at night.” The nurse and the child‘s mother discuss options. What intervention is the most appropriate choice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Allow the child to put himself to bed when he is tired.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Let the child read in his room until he falls asleep.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Establish a bedtime routine and use it consistently.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tire him out with physical activity before bedtime.

questions.rationale: Parents should engage the child in quiet activities before bedtime and establish a ritual that signals readiness for bedtime.

questions.chapter_title: The Preschool Child
questions.stem: What fear is unique to the preschool period?
questions.rationale: The fear of bodily harm, particularly the loss of body parts, is unique to this stage.

questions.chapter_title: The Preschool Child
questions.stem: A 4-year-old child tells the nurse she will not eat peas because they are green. Of what is this an example?
questions.rationale: The tendency to concentrate on a single outstanding characteristic of an object while excluding other features is known as centering.

questions.chapter_title: The Preschool Child
questions.stem: A 4-year-old child insists he has more money with a nickel than his father has with a dime. What is this perception, as described in Piaget‘s theory?
questions.rationale: The intuitive stage, as described by Piaget, is prelogical thinking that is based on the outside appearance of objects. A nickel is larger than a dime and therefore more valuable.

questions.chapter_title: The Preschool Child
questions.stem: What will children who are unable to express themselves with words often do?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Develop other methods of verbal communication.

questions.rationale: Children with delayed communication skills will frequently have tantrums and act out when they are unable to make their needs known.

questions.chapter_title: The Preschool Child
questions.stem: Which is an example of associative play?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Two children playing in house, one playing the role of the dad and the other playing the role of the mom

choices.label: B
choices.text: Two children playing in a sand box, one building a wall and the other digging a hole

choices.label: C
choices.text: Two children playing with sports-associated items, one with a football and the other with a bat

choices.label: D
choices.text: Two children playing with a coloring book, one coloring pictures and the other looking at pictures

questions.rationale: Associative play allows the preschoolers to use their enlarged vocabulary in play with other children to carry on conversations and describe scenarios for each to play.

questions.chapter_title: The Preschool Child
questions.stem: The nurse is educating a group of preschool parents about the importance of safety. Which statement by a parent indicates the need for further education?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Tcontinue to provide a great deal of indirect supervision for my child.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “My stairway is always free of clutter.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Tonly leave my child in the car for brief moments.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Medications are kept in a locked cabinet.”

questions.rationale: Children must not play in or around the car or be left alone, even for a brief moment, in the car. Preschool children still require a good deal of indirect supervision to protect them from dangers that arise from their immature judgment or social environment. Stairways should be free of clutter and medications kept out of reach.

questions.chapter_title: The Preschool Child
questions.stem: Parents of a 5-year-old child tell the nurse they are concerned about their child‘s speech development by stating, “No one can understand him but us.” What clinical classification of speech disorder does the nurse suspect?
questions.rationale: When parents are the only people to understand their preschool child, an articulation disorder is suspected (see Table 18-3).

questions.chapter_title: The Preschool Child
questions.stem: What does including play in the plan of care for a 5-year-old allow the child to do? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Assume a role and act it out.

questions.rationale: Benefits of play for the preschooler include exercising imagination, assuming a role and acting it out, offering an emotional outlet, and interacting with other children. Play employs the use of magical thinking.

questions.chapter_title: The Preschool Child
questions.stem: What developmental milestone(s) assist the 5-year-old boy toward developing his sexual identity? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Begins to be less focused on his mother.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Regresses to a more infantile level.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Forms a romantic attachment to the mother.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Identifies with the parent of the same sex.

questions.rationale: Children of this age become less focused on the mother as the central person and begin to identify with the parent of the same sex, forming a romantic attachment to the parent of the opposite sex. This little boy might say, “I‘m going to marry my mother.” A little girl might say, “I‘m going to marry my daddy.”

questions.chapter_title: The Preschool Child
questions.stem: Which bedtime preparation rituals are the most appropriate for the nurse to suggest? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Placing a favorite toy in bed

choices.label: C
choices.text: Placing a glass of water at the bedside

questions.rationale: All options are soothing bedtime rituals except energetic playing, which would be stimulating and counterproductive to sleep.

questions.chapter_title: The Preschool Child
questions.stem: The nurse points out what advantage(s) of a nursery school or preschool experience? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Nursery school increases self-confidence, group cooperation, social skills, and cooperative play. Objective observations by a nursery school instructor can detect early adjustment problems. The child is usually toilet trained prior to the start of preschool.

questions.chapter_title: The Preschool Child
questions.stem: Which major developmental tasks will the nurse expect a child to accomplish by the end of the preschool years? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: The major tasks of the preschool child include preparation to enter school, development of a cooperative type of play, control of body functions, acceptance of separation, and increase in communication skills, memory, and attention span. Appetite remains inconsistent.

questions.chapter_title: The Preschool Child
questions.stem: When planning an activity for a 3-year-old child, the nurse bases the plan on the average attention span of____ minutes.
questions.rationale: The average attention span of the preschooler is about 15 minutes.

questions.chapter_title: The School-Age Child
questions.stem: The nurse is assessing a school-age child. What will the nurse expect in regard to physical development of this child?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Growth of 3 to 6 inches per year

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gain of 5 to 7 pounds per year

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increase of head circumference by | inch per year

choices.label: D
choices.text: A visual acuity of 20/20 by 9 years of age

questions.rationale: During the school-age period, the average weight gain per year is generally 5.5 to 7 pounds.

questions.chapter_title: The School-Age Child
questions.stem: What should the nurse keep in mind when planning to teach a class on nutrition to fourth-grade students?

choices.label: A
choices.text: School-age children can concentrate on only one aspect of a situation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: School-age children are egocentric in their thinking.

choices.label: D
choices.text: School-age children think logically and concretely.

questions.rationale: Piaget refers to the thought process of this period as concrete operations, which involves logical thinking and an understanding of cause and effect.

questions.chapter_title: The School-Age Child
questions.stem: What type of relationships are the preferred social interactions for the school-age child?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Rigidly organized groups with complex rules

questions.rationale: The preferred social interaction of the school-age child is in same-sex peer groups or cliques.

questions.chapter_title: The School-Age Child
questions.stem: The nurse is advising parents of a 10-year-old boy about the most developmentally supportive experiences for their son. What is the best experience for this child according to Erikson‘s theory?
questions.rationale: The child who is successful in.activities will, feel pesitively,about himself or herself, cain si.236 SSS Distribution of this document is illegal extra per year iat

questions.chapter_title: The School-Age Child
questions.stem: The parents of an 8-year-old child tell the nurse the child wakes the household crying out during his frequent nightmares. What is the nurse‘s most helpful response to explain nightmares?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They are a normal extension of the child‘s fear of mutilation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: They are an abnormal response to repressed feelings.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They are a common result of latent sexuality.

choices.label: D
choices.text: They are a side effect of overactivity and stimulation.

questions.rationale: The nightmares experienced by an 8-year-old child are an extension of their characteristic fear of mutilation.

questions.chapter_title: The School-Age Child
questions.stem: What is the best suggestion by the nurse for an appropriate toy for a hospitalized 6-year-old boy?
questions.rationale: The 6-year-old child can perform numerous feats that require muscle coordination. At this age, the handheld video game will offer competition without overexertion.

questions.chapter_title: The School-Age Child
questions.stem: The nurse discusses preparation for school with the parents of a 6-year-old girl who will soon be starting first grade. What statement by the girl‘s father leads the nurse to determine that the parents understood the information?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “We should puta stop to her thumb-sucking.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “We'll have a talk about what school is like.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “We will let her walk to the bus stop by herself.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “We'll have her meet some children who will be in her class.”

questions.rationale: To prepare a child for school, parents can arrange for the child to meet other children who will be entering school with her.

questions.chapter_title: The School-Age Child
questions.stem: A 9-year-old boy is often cranky and irritable, and his school performance has declined. What is the most probable factor causing this behavior?

choices.label: A
choices.text: He sleeps only 6 to 7 hours a night.

choices.label: D
choices.text: He plays about 1 to 3 hours each evening.

questions.rationale: The 9-year-old child requires about 10 hours of sleep per night.

questions.chapter_title: The School-Age Child
questions.stem: A parent asked the nurse, “At what age are children capable of assuming more responsibility for personal belongings?” What is the nurse‘s best response based on knowledge of growth and development?
questions.rationale: The 9-year-old child is dependable and assumes more responsibility for personal belongings.

questions.chapter_title: The School-Age Child
questions.stem: The school nurse is preserving a tooth that was knocked out on the school playground. What will the nurse be especially careful to do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Wrap the tooth loosely in a clean cloth.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Handle the tooth only by the crown.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Place the tooth in a warm environment.

questions.rationale: When a permanent tooth is avulsed, the tooth should be picked up by the crown to prevent any further damage to the root and placed in milk until the child can be examined by a dentist.

questions.chapter_title: The School-Age Child
questions.stem: A parent states, “My 7-year-old really wants a dog. His 10-year-old brother has allergies to animal dander. I don‘t know what to do.” What type of pet should the nurse suggest as the best choice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A small breed of dog because the large dogs produce more allergens.

choices.label: B
choices.text: An older unneutered dog that produces fewer allergens than a younger one.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A cat because it requires less care and is less allergenic.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A poodle, which does not shed, making it a good choice for people with allergies.

questions.rationale: The poodle does not have a shed cycle and so it may be the least offensive pet for the allergic child.

questions.chapter_title: The School-Age Child
questions.stem: When asked about her activities, a 10-year-old girl responded, “I like school. I play the flute in the school band, and I take tennis lessons.” What does the nurse know these activities will help this child develop?
questions.rationale: The school-age period is referred to by Erikson as the stage of industry. Successful participation in activities facilitates the child‘s sense of industry.

questions.chapter_title: The School-Age Child
questions.stem: A mother reports that she has a new job and her 12-year-old child is home alone for a time after school. Which statement made by the parent alerts the nurse to a potentially unsafe situation for this child?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Ttold him that he could invite a few friends after school.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “I puta list of emergency numbers next to the telephone.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Last week we made a first aid kit together.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “There is a neighbor available in case of an emergency.”

questions.rationale: Latchkey children are subject to a higher rate of accidents. Permitting school-age children and their friends to be home alone in an unsupervised environment is an unsafe situation.

questions.chapter_title: The School-Age Child
questions.stem: A mother is concerned because her 9-year-old boy has developed the habit of twitching his eyes and flipping his hair while communicating with anyone. What is the best nursing response to this parent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “This may indicate that he needs eyeglasses.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Children sometimes do these things for attention.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Tics appear when a child is under stress.”

questions.rationale: The child cannot help such actions and should not be scolded for them because they are mainly a result of tension.

questions.chapter_title: The School-Age Child
questions.stem: A seventh-grade girl tells the school nurse that her art teacher, a woman, is her hero. What is the most appropriate interpretation of the girl‘s comment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The student may be exploring her career options.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The comment is cause for concern about sexual abuse.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The child may have difficulty interacting with her peers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hero worship is a normal phenomenon.

questions.rationale: School-age children tend to admire their teachers and adult companions. For the 11- to 12-year-old, hero worship is a normal phenomenon.

questions.chapter_title: The School-Age Child
questions.stem: Which stage of cognitive development is a 9-year-old child in according to Piaget?
questions.rationale: School-age children are in the concrete operations stage of cognitive development.

questions.chapter_title: The School-Age Child
questions.stem: What statement by an 11-year-old child leads the nurse to determine he has moved from the mind-set of egocentrism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Tama member of the best Cub Scout group in the world.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “I must do my homework before I can play.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “I‘m sorry. I bet that hurt your feelings.”

questions.rationale: The ability to see another‘s point of view indicates moving away from egocentrism into a more altruistic mind-set.

questions.chapter_title: The School-Age Child
questions.stem: A school-age child becomes frustrated with a school assignment and says, “I can‘t do this!” What is the most developmentally supportive response from the parent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ask, “What is it that is so difficult?”

choices.label: B
choices.text: Allow the child to quit the effort.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Call in older siblings to help.

questions.rationale: Helping the child focus on the problem that is keeping him from mastery can limit frustration. Quitting or having someone else finish is detrimental to the development of industry.

questions.chapter_title: The School-Age Child
questions.stem: What is best for the nurse to suggest to the parents of an overweight 9-year-old child to help prevent obesity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use whole milk as a between-meal snack because it is more filling than skim milk.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Feed the child before family meal times to monitor intake more closely.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Encourage the child to engage in physical activity for at least an hour a day.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Remove all sweets and junk food from the house.

questions.rationale: Regular physical activity reduces weight.

questions.chapter_title: The School-Age Child
questions.stem: A parent confides in the school nurse that her 8-year-old twins argue and bicker constantly. What is the best response by the nurse?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Express alarm at the constant aggression.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Voice concern and investigate referral for counseling.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inquire about what punitive action the parents have taken to stop it.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Offer reassurance that such behavior is normal for 8-year-olds.

questions.rationale: Argumentative and competitive behavior is normal in 8-year-olds.

questions.chapter_title: The School-Age Child
questions.stem: The school nurse is planning sex education classes for school-age children. What should the nurse be sure to do?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Avoid slang or “street” words and concepts.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Keep topics on biological aspects of sexual development.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Limit questions to keep content clear.

questions.rationale: Using simple terms is essential but slang and street terms need to be clarified. Apply age-specific information across broad aspects of biological, social, and current attitudes.

questions.chapter_title: The School-Age Child
questions.stem: Parents ask the pediatric nurse how school life might influence their growing child. What area of development will the nurse indicate that school affects the /east?
questions.rationale: Physical development is the least affected by school life. Moral development occurs as they have experience with, and understand, rules and fairness in the school setting. Schools have a profound influence on the socialization of children, who bring to school what they have learned and experienced in the home. Success in school requires an integration of cognitive, receptive, and expressive (language) skills.

questions.chapter_title: The School-Age Child
questions.stem: What basic “feeling” words should the nurse use in attempting to help a 7-year-old girl express her feelings about being in a new school? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: The words “mad,” “glad,” “sad,” and “scared” are basic feeling words that can prompt a young child to better express his or her feelings.

questions.chapter_title: The School-Age Child
questions.stem: The school nurse is preparing an educational program for new teachers regarding school-age children. What information is accurate for the nurse to include? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Piaget refers to the thought processes of the school-age period as concrete operations. Concrete operations involve logical thinking and an understanding of cause and effect. The egocentric view of the preschool child is replaced by the ability to understand the point of view of another person. Between 6 and 12 years of age, children prefer friends of their own sex and usually prefer the company of their friends to that of their brothers and sisters.

questions.chapter_title: The School-Age Child
questions.stem: The pediatric nurse is presenting school-age children with information on safety issues to follow when going home alone. What guidelines should they be educated to follow? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ask for identification before letting someone in the house.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Do not enter house if door is ajar.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Walk to and from school with friends.

questions.rationale: Strangers should never be allowed in the house. Children should be instructed never to accept rides with strangers, to keep doors locked, not to enter the house if the door is ajar, and to walk to and from school with friends.

questions.chapter_title: The School-Age Child
questions.stem: A 10-year-old child with disabilities is begging her parents for a dog. When at the pediatric clinic, the parents inquire about possible benefits pet ownership may provide to their child. What benefits of pet ownership should the nurse indicate? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decrease the need for physical therapy

questions.rationale: Studies have documented the positive influence of pet ownership on improving the medical and psychological outcome after illness or surgery. Disabled children especially benefit from interacting with pets. The interaction with animals can lower blood pressure and heart rate, reduce loneliness and feelings of isolation, improve communication, foster trust, and motivate participation in physical therapy. Pets allow the ill child who feels separated from other people to feel companionship and acceptance. Shy children often find pet ownership eases the path to socialization with others who initiate contact because of the pet.

questions.chapter_title: The School-Age Child
questions.stem: The nurse advises the parents of a 6-year-old child to try and ensure at least hours of sleep daily for the child.
questions.rationale: The 6-year-old school-age child needs at least 11 hours of sleep.

questions.chapter_title: The School-Age Child
questions.stem: The nurse is aware that by the age of. , the first permanent teeth erupt.
questions.rationale: At the age of 6, the first permanent teeth erupt: the 6-year molars.

questions.chapter_title: The Adolescent
questions.stem: The nurse is assessing a 13-year-old boy. Which physical change indicates that male puberty has begun?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Development of axillary and facial hair

questions.rationale: In boys, pubertal changes begin with enlargement of the testicles and internal structures.

questions.chapter_title: The Adolescent
questions.stem: A 13-year-old boy states, “The girls in my class tower over me.” What would be the nurse‘s most informative response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “It may seem that way because girls have a growth spurt 2 years earlier than boys.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Perhaps your parents are not exceptionally tall.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Boys usually experience a growth spurt | year earlier than girls.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “You may feel short, but you are actually average height for your age.”

questions.rationale: Although the age for growth spurts during puberty varies, growth spurts occur 2 years earlier for girls than for boys.

questions.chapter_title: The Adolescent
questions.stem: A parent comments that her adolescent daughter seems to be daydreaming a lot. What does the nurse understand this behavior to indicate regarding their daughter?

choices.label: B
choices.text: She is not getting enough rest.

choices.label: C
choices.text: She is trying to block out stress and anxiety.

choices.label: D
choices.text: She is mentally preparing for real situations.

questions.rationale: Daydreaming allows adolescents to act out in their imaginations what will be said or done in certain situations. This helps them to prepare for and cope with interactions with others.

questions.chapter_title: The Adolescent
questions.stem: The nurse is planning a safety program for high school students. Which is the top cause of accidental deaths during adolescence?
questions.rationale: The chief safety hazard for the adolescent is automobiles.

questions.chapter_title: The Adolescent
questions.stem: A 16-year-old boy excitedly tells his parents that he was offered a part-time job. Which response represents an effective problem-solving approach for his parents?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Your studies are too important for you to have a part-time job.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “When we went to high school, academics were the adolescent's priority.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “We want you to put your earnings in a savings account.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “How do you think you will manage your school work and a job?”

questions.rationale: An effective approach to help adolescents learn to solve problems is for parents to guide them in exploring alternatives.

questions.chapter_title: The Adolescent
questions.stem: The nurse is planning care of an adolescent. What psychosocial task does the nurse understand is important for the adolescent to develop?
questions.rationale: Psychosocial milestones that must be accomplished during adolescence include the five Is—image of self, identity, independence, interpersonal relationships, and intellectual maturity.

questions.chapter_title: The Adolescent
questions.stem: A 13-year-old girl tells the school nurse that she is getting fat, especially in her hips and legs. What understanding by the nurse would best guide the response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Many adolescents are unaware of proper nutrition.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Adolescents of this age become less active and should eat fewer calories.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Puberty is often preceded by fat deposits in these areas.

choices.label: D
choices.text: As soon as menarche occurs, she will lose this excess weight.

questions.rationale: Secondary sexual characteristics become apparent before menarche. Fat is deposited in the hips, thighs, and breasts, causing them to enlarge.

questions.chapter_title: The Adolescent
questions.stem: The school nurse is planning a program for girls about the physical changes of puberty. What is the target age the nurse should choose for this program?
questions.rationale: Because puberty can occur in girls as early as age 10 years, instruction must be given by that age.

questions.chapter_title: The Adolescent
questions.stem: What statement made by a parent indicates an understanding about helping a 13-year-old adult manage his allowance?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “TI set amounts he can earn for particular chores.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “I give him a certain amount of money for each day.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “T put money into his bank account each month.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “TI told him to ask me when he needs money.”

questions.rationale: If money is simply handed out as requested, it is difficult to develop responsibility for finances and money management. The older adolescent is able to get a job. The younger adolescent can earn money by doing particular chores.

questions.chapter_title: The Adolescent
questions.stem: What can the nurse suggests as a good dietary source of zinc for an adolescent who is a vegetarian?
questions.rationale: Zinc is essential for growth and sexual maturation in adolescence. Good vegetable sources include nuts, legumes, and wheat germ.

questions.chapter_title: The Adolescent
questions.stem: Anadolescent‘s parent comments, “My son seems so preoccupied with his appearance these days. Is this normal?” What is the nurse‘s best response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Tt is his attempt to express his individualism.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “His preoccupation with his looks is quite normal.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “He is probably troubled with his physical changes.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “This shows that he has a positive self-image.”

questions.rationale: Preoccupation with self-image is normal and accounts for the constant primping of adolescents.

questions.chapter_title: The Adolescent
questions.stem: What foods would be a healthy choice for an adolescent who just finished playing in a strenuous sports game?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Two sausage and egg breakfast sandwiches and orange juice

questions.rationale: A bagel provides a rapid supply of carbohydrates to the muscles, and skim milk provides a slow release of carbohydrates to the muscles.

questions.chapter_title: The Adolescent
questions.stem: When planning to answer a 16-year-old girl‘s questions about menstruation, the nurse must consider cognitive development. What is developed during adolescence according to Piaget?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The ability to view a situation from multiple perspectives

choices.label: B
choices.text: The ability to focus more on the past than present situations

choices.label: C
choices.text: The ability to exercise concrete reasoning

choices.label: D
choices.text: The ability to consider hypothetical situations

questions.rationale: According to Piaget, in the formal operations stage adolescents have the ability to think abstractly.

questions.chapter_title: The Adolescent
questions.stem: A girl tells the nurse that she and her best friend belong to the popular clique. She states, “I love Katy Perry, and I want to be a singer.” The nurse recognizes the girl‘s statement as characteristic of what time period?
questions.rationale: Cliques of unisex friends, having a best friend, and hero worship are characteristics of the early adolescent.

questions.chapter_title: The Adolescent
questions.stem: The nurse is leading a discussion group with parents of adolescents. One parent comments, “My son can‘t do anything without checking with his friends first. My opinion doesn‘t count anymore.” What knowledge in regard to this behavior would the nurse formulate as a response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is unusual for adolescent boys.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is often more apparent in boys than girls.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is suggestive of feelings of low self-worth.

questions.rationale: Parents may need help understanding that the adolescent‘s exaggerated conformity is necessary for moving away from dependence and obtaining approval from persons outside the nuclear family.

questions.chapter_title: The Adolescent
questions.stem: What does an adolescent‘s peer group serve as related to development?
questions.rationale: Being a member of a peer group and communicating with and seeking approval from this group are hallmarks of the first separation from the family.

questions.chapter_title: The Adolescent
questions.stem: At what stage is the adolescent considered to be, according to Freud‘s theory?
questions.rationale: Freud describes the adolescent period as genital.

questions.chapter_title: The Adolescent
questions.stem: The nurse using the PACE interview guide for persons at risk for substance abuse arrives at a score of 2 for an adolescent patient. How would the nurse interpret this score?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Need to schedule another PACE interview in 3 months

questions.rationale: The PACE guide recommends that a score of 2 or higher would suggest the need for a referral for counseling about substance abuse.

questions.chapter_title: The Adolescent
questions.stem: What does adolescent acne result from?
questions.rationale: Adolescent acne is the result of overactive sweat glands and oily skin.

questions.chapter_title: The Adolescent
questions.stem: The nurse suggests the use of “I” messages to communicate a parent‘s feeling to an adolescent. What is the most appropriate example of an “I” message?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “T feel frightened when you stay out past your curfew.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Iam your mother, and I insist that you observe your curfew.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Tam sick and tired of your staying out late.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “TI expect you to show me proper respect.”

questions.rationale: This is the only statement that associates the parent‘s feelings about the adolescent behavior that is not aggressive or accusatory.

questions.chapter_title: The Adolescent
questions.stem: A 13-year-old girl tells the nurse she is concerned because she has not had her first menstrual period. What is the best initial response from the nurse?
questions.rationale: Puberty is easily recognized in girls by the onset of menstruation. The first menstrual period is called the menarche. It commonly occurs about age 12 or 13 years, but this varies. It may occur as early as age 10 years or as late as age 15 years.

questions.chapter_title: The Adolescent
questions.stem: The nurse is documenting the pediatrician‘s assessment of a female patient. When assessing Tanner‘s stages of breast development there is elevation of papilla only. What stage of development will the nurse document?
questions.rationale: According to Tanner‘s Stages of Sexual Maturity, Stage 1 (preadolescent) is elevation of papilla only.

questions.chapter_title: The Adolescent
questions.stem: The school nurse is educating high school students about guidelines to be followed when participating in sports. Which statement by a student alerts the nurse of the need for further information?

choices.label: B
choices.text: “I drink large amounts of fluid when working out.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “TI wear protective gear every time I play sports.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “I avoid caffeine when participating in sports.”

questions.rationale: Fluids lost by sweat must be replaced by drinking sma// amounts of fluid during a workout. Thirst is one guide for intake. Caffeine and alcohol deplete body water and are to be avoided. Carbohydrates that provide both energy and other nutrients are best for athletes.
