Protective gear should be worn by all team players in any contact sport.

questions.chapter_title: The Adolescent
questions.stem: Restlessness in adolescence is most likely attributed to which changes? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Drive to be accepted by society as an individual

questions.rationale: All the options listed are sources of stress to the adolescent and are stimulants to restlessness except option E body changes are rapid.

questions.chapter_title: The Adolescent
questions.stem: What are the best breakfast choices for the nurse to point out prior to a big exam, to provide high levels of alertness and increased memory? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Meals high in protein will break down into norepinephrine and increase alertness. Meals with a high sugar content result in a soothing sleepy response. Meals high in fats digest slowly and draw blood from the brain during the lengthy digestive process.

questions.chapter_title: The Adolescent
questions.stem: The nurse considers what “rites of passage” valued by the adolescent in American society? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Rites of passage are socially recognized milestones that signify adulthood. Legal drinking age, driver‘s license, and matriculation through high school are such signals. Religious affiliation and selection of a career path do not necessarily signal adulthood.

questions.chapter_title: The Adolescent
questions.stem: A mother confides in the school nurse that she witnessed her son kissing another boy. Which concepts should guide the nurse to base a reply? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Homosexual behavior in adolescents is not uncommon.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Adolescents often desire to explore alternative lifestyles.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Homosexual tendencies should be addressed with counseling.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Parents should immediately seek a support group for parents of gays.

questions.rationale: Adolescents may experiment with an alternate sexual expression as part of their self-discovery. Homosexual activities are not uncommon in adolescence.

questions.chapter_title: The Adolescent
questions.stem: The school nurse is discussing challenges of the adolescent years with a group of high school students in health class. What challenges toward adolescent development will the nurse include? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Adolescents face the challenges of developing intimacy, searching for identity, adjusting to body changes, and establishing goals for the future. Adolescents are striving for independence from parents.

questions.chapter_title: The Adolescent
questions.stem: The nurse stresses the need for using a sunscreen with a sun protection factor (SPF) of at least
questions.rationale: A sunscreen with an SPF of at least 30 is recommended to block sun rays that cause cancer.

questions.chapter_title: The Child’s Experience of Hospitalization
questions.stem: Which child would have the most difficulty in coping with separation from parents because of hospitalization?
questions.rationale: Separation anxiety occurs after age 6 months and is most pronounced in the toddler.

questions.chapter_title: The Child’s Experience of Hospitalization
questions.stem: A 2-year-old child has been crying constantly for his mother since he was hospitalized 3 days ago. What does this behavior suggest?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The toddler feels abandoned by his mother.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The child still has not adjusted to his hospitalization.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The child is not separated from his mother often.

choices.label: D
choices.text: There is a poor mother-child bond.

questions.rationale: Unless toddlers are extremely ill, their grief and sense of abandonment during hospitalization are obvious.

questions.chapter_title: The Child’s Experience of Hospitalization
questions.stem: Which statement best corresponds to a preschooler‘s understanding of hospitalization?

choices.label: B
choices.text: “I got sick because I was mad at my brother.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “My tonsils are sick and they have to come out.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Ihave a cast because I broke my leg.”

questions.rationale: The preschooler may feel guilty, particularly if an accident happens as a result of mischief on his or her part.

questions.chapter_title: The Child’s Experience of Hospitalization
questions.stem: The parents of a hospitalized toddler are upset because she seems more interested in her toys when they come to visit her. In which stage of separation anxiety is the toddler?
questions.rationale: In the stage of denial or detachment, the child appears to deny the need for the parents and becomes uninterested in their visits.

questions.chapter_title: The Child’s Experience of Hospitalization
questions.stem: The nurse must make a room assignment for a 16-year-old adolescent with cystic fibrosis. Which roommate would be the most appropriate for this patient?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A 4-year-old child who had an appendectomy

choices.label: B
choices.text: A 10-year-old child with sickle cell disease in vaso-occlusive crisis

choices.label: C
choices.text: A 15-year-old adolescent with type 1 diabetes mellitus

choices.label: D
choices.text: To assign the adolescent to a private room

questions.rationale: Adolescents usually do better in rooms with one or more roommates than in single rooms. The adolescent would do best with a roommate who is closest to his or her age and also lives with a chronic illness.

questions.chapter_title: The Child’s Experience of Hospitalization
questions.stem: The parents of a hospitalized 9-month-old infant ask if their preschool child may visit his younger sibling. What understanding would assist the nurse most in formulating a response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Preschool children can be disruptive in the hospital environment.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Seeing his younger sibling would probably frighten the preschooler and thus should be avoided.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The sibling could view the infant from the doorway but not enter the room to prevent the spread of microorganisms.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The preschooler needs to visit his infant sister to reassure himself that she is all right.

questions.rationale: Siblings are affected by a child‘s hospitalization. Their ability to cope is influenced by their age, experience, and intactness of the family.

questions.chapter_title: The Child’s Experience of Hospitalization
questions.stem: A hospitalized toddler was drinking from a cup at home but now refuses to drink from anything except his favorite bottle. What is the most likely reason for this behavior?

choices.label: A
choices.text: He is dealing with the anxiety of hospitalization byregressing.

choices.label: B
choices.text: He is demonstrating attention-seeking behaviors because of an overabundance of attention in the hospital.

choices.label: C
choices.text: He is attempting to refocus the attention of the adults around him to avoid further painful procedures.

choices.label: D
choices.text: He is exhibiting normal behavior for his age, as children often stop new behaviors after they believe they have mastered them.

questions.rationale: Hospitalization is frustrating for toddlers. They show their displeasure when illness restricts satisfaction of their desires. It is not unusual for a toddler who was drinking from a cup to refuse it in the hospital.

questions.chapter_title: The Child’s Experience of Hospitalization
questions.stem: A nurse encourages a school-age child to draw a picture after a painful procedure. What is the best rationale for this nursing intervention?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Providing a way for the child to express his feelings

choices.label: D
choices.text: Distracting the child from thinking about the pain

questions.rationale: After treatments, the nurse should encourage children to draw and talk about their drawings or to act out their feelings through puppet play.

questions.chapter_title: The Child’s Experience of Hospitalization
questions.stem: What is the best suggestion by the nurse when parents ask, “When is the best time to begin to prepare a 5-year-old child for surgery and hospitalization?”

choices.label: A
choices.text: “As soon as the surgery is scheduled”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “On the night before admission to the hospital”

questions.rationale: Parents should prepare children for procedures and hospitalization a few days in advance. Nursing Process Step: Implementation

questions.chapter_title: The Child’s Experience of Hospitalization
questions.stem: The mother of a 3-year-old child tells the nurse that she will be in to visit tomorrow around 12:00 PM. The next morning, the child asks the nurse, “When is my mommy coming?” What is the nurse‘s best response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Your mommy will be here around noon.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Your mommy will be here when you have lunch.”

questions.rationale: The toddler and preschooler do not understand time yet. They understand time relationships through activities in their experience, such as naptime and mealtimes.

questions.chapter_title: The Child’s Experience of Hospitalization
questions.stem: A 13-year-old girl has been hospitalized for the past week. When discussing the girl‘s feelings about her illness, what would the nurse expect the girl to express as her biggest concern?
questions.rationale: Illness during early adolescence (12 to 15 years) is seen mainly as a threat to body image.

questions.chapter_title: The Child’s Experience of Hospitalization
questions.stem: The nurse notices that the mother of a child with cerebral palsy corrects and redoes many of the things the nurse does for her child. What is the nurse‘s most appropriate response to this mother?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Would you like to do all of your child‘s care?”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “I‘m doing the very best job that I can with your child.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Why don‘t you go have a cup of coffee? You are going to be exhausted if you don‘t take a break.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “I‘d love for you to share with me some of the special things you do for your child.”

questions.rationale: The person who cares daily for the child with a chronic illness can provide information that will best guarantee continuity of care between the home and the hospital.

questions.chapter_title: The Child’s Experience of Hospitalization
questions.stem: The mother of a hospitalized toddler states, “He cries when I visit. Maybe I should just stay away.” What is the nurse‘s best response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Perhaps you are right. He only gets upset when you have to leave.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “It is important that you are here. This is a common reaction in children when they are separated from their parents.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “It might be easier for your child if you would stay with him, but this decision is up to you.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “We take good care of him and he seems fine when you are not here.”

questions.rationale: During the second stage of separation anxiety (despair), the child is quiet, is not crying, and is sad and depressed. The child will revert to protest when the parent arrives for a visit.

questions.chapter_title: The Child’s Experience of Hospitalization
questions.stem: What should the nurse, preparing to collect an admission history from parents who have recently emigrated from Russia, keep in mind?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Touching the child‘s head means the nurse is superior.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Smiling is inappropriate in a serious situation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Staring is a sign of the nurse‘s rudeness.

questions.rationale: In Russia, a smile indicates happiness and is inappropriate in a serious or sad situation.

questions.chapter_title: The Child’s Experience of Hospitalization
questions.stem: Which nursing action would facilitate rapport with a child and the child‘s parents duringthe admission process?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Direct the parents to undress the child.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Answer questions in a calm and matter-of-fact way.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Perform assessments and ask questions as quickly as possible.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Express concern about the seriousness of the child‘s condition.

questions.rationale: The nurse tries not to appear rushed. A matter-of-fact attitude must be maintained regardless of the child‘s condition.

questions.chapter_title: The Child’s Experience of Hospitalization
questions.stem: When a 2-year-old child returns to her hospital room following a diagnostic procedure, her parents are not available, and the child is crying loudly. Which technique is most appropriate to alleviate the child‘s distress?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rock the child gently to sleep.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Play with the child using pop-up toys.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Role-play with the child to act out her feelings.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ask the child to draw a picture about her feelings.

questions.rationale: Distractions such as blowing bubbles, looking through a kaleidoscope, and playing with pop-up toys may help reduce anxiety and pain.

questions.chapter_title: The Child’s Experience of Hospitalization
questions.stem: A 4-year-old child begins to cry when his mother tells him it is time for his operation. The nurse understands this is an expected reaction. On which particular fear of the preschooler does the nurse base this understanding?
questions.rationale: The preschool child is afraid of bodily harm, particularly invasive procedures.

questions.chapter_title: The Child’s Experience of Hospitalization
questions.stem: What statement by the parent of a hospitalized toddler leads the nurse to determine the parent understands a hospitalized toddler‘s need for transitional objects?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “This stuffed animal makes him feel secure.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “He insisted on bringing this dirty old blanket with him.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “TI‘m going to buy him a big stuffed animal from the gift shop.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “TI‘d like to get him some toys from the playroom.”

questions.rationale: The use of a transitional object such as a blanket or a favorite toy promotes security.

questions.chapter_title: The Child’s Experience of Hospitalization
questions.stem: An 8-year-old child will be hospitalized for several weeks in skeletal traction to treat a fractured femur. What does the nurse realize immobilization in this age group cangenerate feelings of in planning care of this child?
questions.rationale: Forced dependency in the hospital, such as immobilization, can result in a feeling of loss of control and loss of security.

questions.chapter_title: The Child’s Experience of Hospitalization
questions.stem: The nurse explains to the parents of a hospitalized child that their child will receive fentanyl for an upcoming procedure. What advantage of fentanyl will the nurse explain?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is specifically designed for children.

questions.rationale: Fentanyl is a drug useful for all ages because of its rapid onset and brief duration.

questions.chapter_title: The Child’s Experience of Hospitalization
questions.stem: The nurse shares the information and timelines recorded on the interdisciplinary outline of care for a child. What is this document?
questions.rationale: This document is the clinical pathway, which is a broad outline of interdisciplinary plan of care with specific timelines.

questions.chapter_title: The Child’s Experience of Hospitalization
questions.stem: The anxious parent asks if there is a danger of her 2-year-old child becoming addicted to the opioid pain reliever. What is the nurse‘s most helpful response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Although this drug is addictive, the doctor monitors the dose very carefully.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Don‘t worry. Addicted children are very easy to wean off the drug.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Addiction is rare in children when opiates are given for pain.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Addictive behaviors are easy to assess. The drug will be stopped if that happens.”

questions.rationale: Addiction is rare in children.

questions.chapter_title: The Child’s Experience of Hospitalization
questions.stem: The nurse is preparing to start an IV on an infant admitted to the pediatric unit. What intervention is appropriate for the nurse to implement?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Provide a simple explanation to the child.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Let the child examine the equipment.

questions.rationale: It is appropriate to involve the parents when performing a procedure on an infant. Providing a simple explanation, letting the child examine the equipment, and suggesting coping techniques are not appropriate interventions for an infant.

questions.chapter_title: The Child’s Experience of Hospitalization
questions.stem: The pediatric nurse is caring for a child that weighs 15 kg and calls the physician for an order for acetaminophen for pain control. What is the maximum amount of medication per dose the nurse anticipates ordering?
questions.rationale: Acetaminophen is commonly used for the relief of mild to moderate pain in infants and children. The maximum dose is 15 mg/kg/dose for infants and children, with a maximum of 5 doses in 24 hours.

questions.chapter_title: The Child’s Experience of Hospitalization
questions.stem: What will the nurse include when documenting the discharge of a pediatric patient? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Adult(s) accompanying the child and the relationship to the child

choices.label: E
choices.text: Instructions that were given to physician

questions.rationale: Information that should be included in the discharge note include time of discharge, adults accompanying the child and relationship to the child, condition of the child, and method of transportation. It should also be documented that instructions were given to parents.

questions.chapter_title: The Child’s Experience of Hospitalization
questions.stem: The nurse suggests to parents that they use the outpatient surgical center for their child‘s upcoming surgery. What advantage(s) does this type of facility have to offer? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Less incidence of health care—associated infections

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ample time for recuperation at the facility

questions.rationale: All options listed are advantages of outpatient services with the exception of recuperating at the facility.

questions.chapter_title: The Child’s Experience of Hospitalization
questions.stem: What are the basic fears of a young child being hospitalized? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Small children all share the same basic fears relative to hospitalization, which are separation from family, pain, and body intrusion or mutilation.

questions.chapter_title: The Child’s Experience of Hospitalization
questions.stem: What information will the nurse include when taking a developmental history? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: The developmental history has information about the child and the child‘s developmental and cultural needs and personal preferences. The information relative to history of illness or allergies would be covered in the medical history.

questions.chapter_title: The Child’s Experience of Hospitalization
questions.stem: The nurse is preparing to obtain a throat culture on a toddler patient. What interventions are appropriate for the nurse to implement? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: E
choices.text: Encourage the child to ask questions.

questions.rationale: Whenever possible the parent should be involved in the preparation for and initiation of a treatment or procedure, and the child should be prepared according to his or her developmental level. For a toddler, model the behavior desired (i.e., opening the mouth), tell the child it is okay to yell if the treatment or procedure is uncomfortable, and use distractions. Explaining the procedure in detail and encouraging questions are appropriate interventions for an older child.

questions.chapter_title: The Child’s Experience of Hospitalization
questions.stem: Parents are preparing their child for admission to the pediatric unit for minor surgery. What should they expect to see when visiting the pediatric unit? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: The children‘s hospital unit differs in many respects from adult divisions. The pediatric unit or hospital is designed to meet the needs of children and their parents. A cheerful, casual atmosphere helps to bridge the gap between home and hospital and is in keeping with the child‘s emotional, developmental, and physical needs. Nurses wear colorful uniforms, and colored bedspreads and wagons or strollers for transportation provide a more homelike atmosphere. The physical structure of the unit includes furniture of the proper height for the child, soundproof ceilings, and color schemes with eye appeal. Most pediatric departments include a playroom.

questions.chapter_title: Health Care Adaptations for the Child and Family
questions.stem: What is the best pulse location for the nurse to use when assessing the pulse rate on a 12-month-old infant?
questions.rationale: Apical pulses are advised for children under age 5 years.

questions.chapter_title: Health Care Adaptations for the Child and Family
questions.stem: The nurse preparing to administer medication to a 2-month-old infant discovers there is no ID bracelet on the child. What should be the next action by the nurse?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Give the medication after confirming the child‘s name from the foot of the crib.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ask the charge nurse to give the medicine.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Confirm the identity with the charge nurse, make a new bracelet, and give the medicine.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Delay the medication until the admissions office can supply a new ID bracelet.

questions.rationale: After confirmation of the child‘s identity with the charge nurse and making a new bracelet, the medication can be safely given. All patients should be identified before treatment.

questions.chapter_title: Health Care Adaptations for the Child and Family
questions.stem: The nurse instructed an adolescent female about collecting a clean-catch urine specimen. What statement made by the adolescent led the nurse to determine she understood the instructions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Tshould wash my perineum with soap and water, then begin to urinate.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Iclean the perineum from front to back with an antiseptic wipe before I urinate.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Tl collect the first stream of urine in a sterile container.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Twill discard the first void and collect a freshly voided specimen 30 minutes later.”

questions.rationale: To obtain a clean-catch specimen, the perineum is cleansed with an antiseptic wipe from front to back.

questions.chapter_title: Health Care Adaptations for the Child and Family
questions.stem: Which strategy might the nurse use when administering oral medications to a young child who is reluctant?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Mix the medication with chocolate milk.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tell the child that the medication is candy.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Give the medication quickly if the child is crying.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Offer the child fruit juice after the medication is swallowed.

questions.rationale: The nurse can offer a chaser of water, fruit juice, or a carbonated beverage after the medication has been swallowed. Medications should not be mixed with food or drinks with important nutrients such as milk because the child may develop distaste for it.

questions.chapter_title: Health Care Adaptations for the Child and Family
questions.stem: A parent tells the nurse, “I‘m not sure how to give this medicine to my infant.” How would the nurse teach the parent to best administer an oral suspension?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Pour the medication into a small cup and allowing the infant to drink it.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Place the medication in a nipple and having the infant suck the nipple.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use an oral syringe and placing the medication in the side of the infant‘s mouth.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Administer the medication with a dropper onto the back of the infant‘s tongue.

questions.rationale: An oral syringe is a useful device for measuring small quantities of medications for infants. The syringe is placed midway back, at the side of the mouth.

questions.chapter_title: Health Care Adaptations for the Child and Family
questions.stem: Gentamicin ear drops are prescribed for a 4-year-old child. How would the nurse position the auricle when administering the ear drops?
questions.rationale: For children 3 years of age and older, the auricle is gently pulled upward and backward to straighten the canal.

questions.chapter_title: Health Care Adaptations for the Child and Family
questions.stem: Why is a tympanic thermometer considered more accurate than other types of thermometers?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The thermometer probe is blunt and wide.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It takes a brief time to register.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The tympanic membrane shares circulation with the hypothalamus.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The tympanic membrane and the brain have the same temperature.

questions.rationale: The accuracy of the tympanic thermometer is attributable to the fact that the tympanic membrane and the hypothalamus share the same circulation.

questions.chapter_title: Health Care Adaptations for the Child and Family
questions.stem: Which intervention is correct when a nurse is administering a gastrostomy feeding by gravity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Discard the residual and increase the volume of feeding by the amount of residual.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Flush the gastrostomy tube with 2 to 4 ounces of water before the feeding.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Refill the syringe with formula after it has completely emptied.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Position the child on the right side after a feeding.

questions.rationale: To prevent regurgitation and aspiration, the child is placed in the Fowler‘s position or on the right side to promote gastric emptying after a gastrostomy tube feeding.

questions.chapter_title: Health Care Adaptations for the Child and Family
questions.stem: Which restraint is most appropriate for the insertion of an intravenous line in a scalp vein of an infant?
questions.rationale: A mummy restraint would be used to restrain an infant for insertion of an intravenous line in a scalp vein.

questions.chapter_title: Health Care Adaptations for the Child and Family
questions.stem: How often should a child who has a continuous intravenous infusion should be assessed?
questions.rationale: The nurse must assess hourly an intravenous infusion for complications, such as inflammation and infiltration.

questions.chapter_title: Health Care Adaptations for the Child and Family
questions.stem: The prescription for a 4-month-old is penicillin G 150,000 units intramuscularly bid. The drug is supplied as a unit dose of 600,000 units in a 5-mL vial. How many milliliters (mL) should the nurse provide?
questions.rationale: 600,000 mL Sm x 150000 ~ 2m This dose would have to be given in divided doses as only 0.5 to 1 mL should be injected in one site on an infant.

questions.chapter_title: Health Care Adaptations for the Child and Family
questions.stem: Which intervention will the nurse implement when suctioning a tracheostomy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Suction for two to three breaths.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clear the catheter with water after suctioning for reuse.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Apply suction for no more than 15 seconds.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Establish a regular schedule for suctioning.

questions.rationale: Suctioning should be limited to 15 seconds.

questions.chapter_title: Health Care Adaptations for the Child and Family
questions.stem: What emergency action should be implemented for airway obstruction in the infant?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Five back blows followed by five chest thrusts

choices.label: C
choices.text: Five chest thrusts followed by five back blows

choices.label: D
choices.text: Abdominal thrusts until the object is expelled

questions.rationale: Five back blows followed by five chest thrusts is the appropriate intervention for airway obstruction in the infant.

questions.chapter_title: Health Care Adaptations for the Child and Family
questions.stem: A 4-year-old child asks tearfully if the IM injection will hurt. What is the nurse‘s most effective response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “No. It is over before you know it.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “No. Would you like to see the syringe?”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Yes. Your mom and [are going to hold you to help you be still.”

questions.rationale: Truthful answers will give a child a realistic expectation and help establish trust in the nurse.

questions.chapter_title: Health Care Adaptations for the Child and Family
questions.stem: Where is the best site for giving an IM injection to a 15-month-old child?
questions.rationale: The vastus lateralis muscle is free of major blood vessels and nerves and can be used in children of any age.

questions.chapter_title: Health Care Adaptations for the Child and Family
questions.stem: What factor does the nurse explain affects the infant‘s physiological response to medications?
questions.rationale: Immature kidney function prevents effective excretion of drugs from the body in infants less than | year of age.

questions.chapter_title: Health Care Adaptations for the Child and Family
questions.stem: What intervention should the nurse implement after topical administration of hydrocortisone cream to the buttocks and abdomen of an infant?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Diaper the infant snugly with a disposable diaper.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cover the area with a transparent dressing.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Place the infant on a plastic pad, undiapered.

questions.rationale: Plastic coverings increase the absorption of drugs. The diaper should be cloth, or the infant should be left undiapered on a cloth pad.

questions.chapter_title: Health Care Adaptations for the Child and Family
questions.stem: Which observation on entering the hospital room lets the nurse know that there is a need for the parents to receive safety education to prevent unintentional injury?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The blanket is not tucked into the mattress.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Diapers and wipes are stacked at the foot of the crib.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The crib side is locked in the up position.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pillows are stacked on the bedside table.

questions.rationale: Disposable diapers and supplies must be kept out of the infant‘s reach to prevent accidental suffocation.

questions.chapter_title: Health Care Adaptations for the Child and Family
questions.stem: A 9-year-old child is preparing for a lumbar puncture. What position will the nurse explain the child will assume for this procedure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “On your stomach with your head turned to the side.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “On your side, keeping the legs bent and the head arched back.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “On your back with your legs extended straight out.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “On your side with the knees bent and the head close to the knees.”

questions.rationale: The child is positioned on his or her side with the knees flexed, and the head is brought down close to the flexed knees.

questions.chapter_title: Health Care Adaptations for the Child and Family
questions.stem: The nurse is caring for a 4-year-old child. What will the nurse expect the child‘s dailyurinary output to be?
questions.rationale: The average daily excretion of urine for a 4-year-old child is 600 to 720 mL.

questions.chapter_title: Health Care Adaptations for the Child and Family
questions.stem: An infant‘s dry diaper weighs 2.5 g. The wet diaper weighs 47 g. How would the nurse record the infant‘s urine output?
questions.rationale: Urine output is determined by calculating the difference in weight between the wet diaper and a dry diaper. One gram is equivalent to one milliliter of output. 47 — 2.5 = 44.5 g = 44.5 mL of urine.

questions.chapter_title: Health Care Adaptations for the Child and Family
questions.stem: The nurse instructs the mother of a 2-year-old child who is taking iron supplements for anemia that some foods reduce the absorption of iron. What would be the best example provided by the nurse?
questions.rationale: Egg yolks and starches reduce the absorption of iron in the digestive tract and should be limited for persons taking an iron supplement.

questions.chapter_title: Health Care Adaptations for the Child and Family
questions.stem: The pediatric nurse completes an assessment on all patients assigned during evening shift at the hospital. Which patient assessment requires immediate intervention?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Toddler with an axillary temperature of 99°F

choices.label: B
choices.text: School-age child with widening pulse pressure

choices.label: D
choices.text: Adolescent with a respiratory rate of 28 breaths/minute

questions.rationale: A widening pulse pressure can indicate increased ICP; therefore, it is the priority. An axillary temperature of 99°F, infant pulse of 100 bpm, and adolescent respiratory rate of 28 are expected assessments.

questions.chapter_title: Health Care Adaptations for the Child and Family
questions.stem: A 15-year-old patient returns to the pediatric unit following a lumbar puncture. What initial position will the nurse maintain for this patient?
questions.rationale: The adolescent may avoid post—lumbar puncture headache by lying flat for some time.

questions.chapter_title: Health Care Adaptations for the Child and Family
questions.stem: Informed consent for a minor guarantees that the parent or legal guardian understands what aspect(s) of a procedure? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: C
choices.text: That no suit can be brought for damages

choices.label: D
choices.text: That the document must be signed and witnessed

questions.rationale: The informed consent establishes that the patient, parent, or legal guardian understands the purpose and risks of the procedure. It also establishes that the patient, parent, or legal guardian understands what they have been told; the document should be signed and witnessed.

questions.chapter_title: Health Care Adaptations for the Child and Family
questions.stem: Which specific drug(s) should be checked with a second licensed nurse prior to administration? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Insulin, hypoglycemics, narcotics, digoxin, inotropic drugs, anticoagulants, potassium, and calcium salts all must be checked by a licensed nurse prior to administration.

questions.chapter_title: Health Care Adaptations for the Child and Family
questions.stem: A 3-year-old patient is admitted to the pediatric unit with a fever of 103°F. Which actions will the nurse implement? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: When evaluating the degree of illness in a febrile child, the nurse should assess and record response of the child to cuddling, alertness, hydration, sociability, and quality of cry. A quiet, lethargic child who does not respond readily to the environment may be acutely ill. Because dehydration is a common problem in infants and children, skin turgor should be assessed. Antipyretics also provide comfort and may aid in enabling the child to consume fluids, lessening the risk of dehydration. Rectal temperatures are not recommended for pediatric patients.

questions.chapter_title: Health Care Adaptations for the Child and Family
questions.stem: What should the nurse assess to determine the method of transportation for a pediatric patient? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: The means by which the child is transported within the unit and to other parts of the hospital depends on age, level of consciousness, and how far the child must travel.

questions.chapter_title: Health Care Adaptations for the Child and Family
questions.stem: The order reads, “Give ampicillin oral suspension 400 mg PO every day.” The vial reads, “Ampicillin 125 mg/5 mL.” The nurse will give a dose of mL.
questions.rationale: Per the safe drug dose calculation, 16 mL is the correct dose to give.

questions.chapter_title: Health Care Adaptations for the Child and Family
questions.stem: After instilling nose drops, the nurse will keep the infant in the head down position for at least seconds.
questions.rationale: The retained position for 30 seconds to 1 minute allows the nose drops to enter deeply into the nostril.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: A parent comments that her infant has had several ear infections in the past few months. Why are infants more susceptible to otitis media?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Infants are in a supine or prone position most of the time.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sucking on a nipple creates middle ear pressure.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They have increased susceptibility to upper respiratory tract infections.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Eustachian tube is short, straight, and wide.

questions.rationale: An infant‘s Eustachian tubes are short, wide, and straight, allowing microorganisms easy access to the middle ear.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: What statement by a patient‘s mother leads the nurse to determine she understands instructions about administering an oral antibiotic for otitis media?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Twill continue using the medication until symptoms are relieved.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “I will share the medicine with siblings if their symptoms are the same.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Twill give the medication with a glass of milk.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Twill administer prescribed doses until all the medication is used.”

questions.rationale: Antibiotic therapy for otitis media is continued until the prescribed amount has been completed, even if symptoms are alleviated.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: Which situation would cause the nurse to suspect a hearing impairment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 3-month-old infant with a positive Moro (startle reaction) reflex

choices.label: C
choices.text: 18-month-old toddler who is speaking one-syllable words

questions.rationale: The child who is not making verbal attempts by 24 months should undergo a complete physical examination.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: What is the best way for the nurse to communicate with a 10-year-old child who has a hearing impairment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use gestures and signs as much as possible.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Let the child‘s parents communicate for her.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Face the child and speak clearly in short sentences.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Recognize that the child‘s ability to communicate will be on a 6-year-old child‘s level.

questions.rationale: The nurse who faces the child and speaks clearly will help the hearing-impaired child in the hospital to develop a healthy personality.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: What would the nurse include when planning postoperative teaching for a child who has had a tympanostomy with insertion of tubes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Keeping the infant flat after feeding

choices.label: C
choices.text: Avoiding getting water in the ears

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cleaning the ear canal with cotton-tipped applicators

questions.rationale: After a tympanostomy, care should be taken to avoid getting water in the ears.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: What assessment made by the school nurse would lead to the suspicion of strabismus?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Child covers one eye to read the chalkboard

questions.rationale: Indicators of strabismus include covering one eye to see, tilting the head to see, and missing objects in attempts to pick them up. Although headaches may be associated with amblyopia, this symptom is too vague to point suspicion to any disorder.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: What might the nurse explain as a common treatment for amblyopia?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Patching the good eye to force the brain to use the affected eye

choices.label: B
choices.text: Patching the affected eye to allow the refractory muscles to rest

choices.label: C
choices.text: Using glasses that will slightly blur the image for the good eye

choices.label: D
choices.text: Using corticosteroids to treat inflammation of the optic nerve

questions.rationale: Early detection and treatment are essential for the child with amblyopia. Treatment includes patching the good eye and using glasses to correct refractive errors.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: What assessment does the school nurse recognize as the cardinal sign of a hyphema?

choices.label: B
choices.text: A yellow-white reflex on the pupil

choices.label: C
choices.text: A dark-red spot in front of the iris

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inflamed mucous membranes of the eyelids

questions.rationale: A dark red spot in front of the iris is blood that has drained into the anterior chamber as the result of an injury.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: The nurse is planning to teach parents about prevention of Reye‘s syndrome. What information would the nurse include in this teaching?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use aspirin instead of acetaminophen for children with viral illness.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Advise parents to have their children immunized against Reye‘s syndrome.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Avoid giving salicylate-containing medications to a child who has viral symptoms.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Get the child tested for Reye‘s syndrome if the child exhibits fever, vomiting, and lethargy.

questions.rationale: Prevention of Reye‘s syndrome includes educating parents not to give aspirin-containing medication to children with viral symptoms.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: What symptom leads the nurse caring for a 5-month-old child with viral influenza to suspect the development of Reye‘s syndrome?
questions.rationale: A child with a viral infection is at risk for Reye‘s syndrome, the onset of which is effortless vomiting, lethargy, and a change in level of consciousness. A 5-month-old child who sleeps after eating is normal.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: What does the nurse explain to parents of a child with febrile seizures?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They occur when the body temperature exceeds 38.3°C (101°F).

choices.label: B
choices.text: They can be prevented by anticonvulsant medication.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They usually lead to the development of epilepsy.

choices.label: D
choices.text: They occur when the temperature rises quickly.

questions.rationale: Febrile seizures occur in response to a rapid rise in temperature, often above 38.8°C (102°F).

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: A parent reports that her child has begun to do poorly at school and experiences episodes where he appears to be staring into space. Of which type of seizure is this behavior a characteristic?
questions.rationale: Absence seizures are characterized by transient loss of consciousness where the child appears to stare blankly, and may last only a few seconds.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: An adolescent has just had a generalized seizure and collapsed in the school nurse‘s office. When should the nurse should call 911?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The seizure lasts more than 5 minutes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The child is sleepy and lethargic after the seizure.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The child vomited at the onset of the seizure.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The child is confused and has slurred speech after the seizure.

questions.rationale: If there are multiple seizures or if seizures last more than 5 minutes, call 911 because these are indicators of possible status epilepticus, a medical emergency.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: What is an appropriate nursing action when a child is experiencing a generalized tonic-clonic seizure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Assist the child to bed and then go for help.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Move objects out of the child‘s immediate area.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Stick a padded tongue blade between the child‘s teeth.

questions.rationale: During a generalized tonic-clonic seizure, the immediate area is cleared to protect the child from injury.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: A child diagnosed with epilepsy had a generalized tonic-clonic seizure that lasted 90 seconds. What would the nurse expect to assess after a generalized tonic-clonic seizure?
questions.rationale: Following a generalized tonic-clonic seizure, the child may have some confusion and may sleep for a time (postictal lethargy) and then return to full consciousness.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: What would the nurse include when creating a teaching plan that includes the long-term administration of phenytoin (Dilantin)?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The medication should be given on an empty stomach.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Insomnia can be a significant side effect.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gums should be massaged regularly to prevent hyperplasia.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Blood pressure should be closely monitored.

questions.rationale: Dilantin can cause gum overgrowth, which can be minimized by regular massaging. Dilantin frequently causes drowsiness and should be given with meals at the same time each day. 13

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: The nurse observes that the legs of a child with cerebral palsy cross involuntarily, and the child exhibits jerky movements with his arms as he tries to eat. The nurse recognizes that he has which type of cerebral palsy?
questions.rationale: Spasticity is characterized by tension in certain muscle groups, which makes voluntary movements of muscles jerky and uncoordinated.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: Which assessment finding in a child with meningitis should be reported immediately?
questions.rationale: Irregular respirations in conjunction with slowing heart rate and increasing blood pressure are reported immediately, because they could indicate increased intracranial pressure.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: The nurse observes a child‘s position is supine with his arms and legs rigidly extended and the hands pronated. How does the nurse identify this posture?
questions.rationale: In decerebrate posturing, arms are extended along the side of the body and hands are pronated. This posture indicates brainstem function only.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: What will the nurse teach parents when giving instructions for acute conjunctivitis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Apply cool compresses to the affected eye several times a day.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Instill topical steroid eyedrops for 1 week.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Clear drainage from the inner to the outer aspect of the eye.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Keep the eye patched until the inflammation resolves.

questions.rationale: Eye secretions are always cleared from the inner canthus downward and away from the opposite eye (inner to outer direction).

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: A child is brought to the emergency department after he fell and hit his head on the ground. Which nursing assessment suggests the child has a concussion?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cannot remember what happened to him

questions.rationale: A concussion is a temporary disturbance of the brain that is immediately followed by a period of unconsciousness. It is accompanied often by a loss of memory of the events that occurred immediately before, during, or after the injury.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: A child is admitted to the hospital because she had a seizure. Her parents report that for the past few weeks she has had headaches, with vomiting, that are worse in the morning. What does the nurse suspect?
questions.rationale: The signs and symptoms of a brain tumor are related to its size and location. Most tumors create increased intracranial pressure (ICP) with the hallmark symptoms of headache, vomiting, drowsiness, and seizures.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: The nurse urges the mother of a 6-month-old child to get her child inoculated with Haemophilus influenzae type B. What does this immunization protect against?
questions.rationale: H. influenzae type B and conjugated pneumococcal vaccines have decreased the incidence of bacterial meningitis.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: The nurse is caring for a 3-year-old child with a head injury. Which assessment would lead the nurse to report the probability of increasing intracranial pressure (ICP)?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increase in blood pressure with an attendant decrease in pulse

questions.rationale: Increasing blood pressure, accompanied by decreasing pulse, and accompanied by unequal pupils are indicators of ICP.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: Acchild is diagnosed with nonparalytic strabismus. How will this disorder most likely be corrected?
questions.rationale: In nonparalytic strabismus, the refractory error is usually corrected with eyeglasses.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: Parents of a 10-year-old child diagnosed with an intellectual deficit are sharing multiple approaches they implement in dealing with various challenges. Which statement by the parents alerts the nurse they need further instruction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “We dress our son every morning for school.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Our son participates in the Special Olympics every year.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Our son attends play therapy at a center close to home.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “We attend a support group once a week.”

questions.rationale: The mentally handicapped child needs to develop a sense of accomplishment. Caregivers should not “take over” projects because of their own need to assist or speed up the process.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: What would the nurse include in teaching when preparing to teach parents about air travel instructions to prevent barotrauma in infants?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Omitting the meal just before takeoff

choices.label: C
choices.text: Letting the infant nurse during descent

questions.rationale: Encouraging an infant to swallow reduces the pressure in the ears during descent.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: Which assessments would cause the pediatric nurse to suspect the probability of an ear infection in a 6-month-old child? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rolls head from side to side

questions.rationale: Infants signal ear infections by being irritable, rolling their heads from side to side, spiking a temperature, and pulling at or rubbing their ears.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: Which aspect(s) of a child‘s development does the nurse caution parents that hearing impairment can affect? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: All the options, except immunity to disease, are areas in which a hearing impairment could interfere with normal development.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: What intervention(s) would the nurse caring for a child with infectious meningitis include? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: All elements of nursing care listed in the options, except a brightly lit room, would be part of comprehensive care of a child with meningitis.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: What will the nurse include when documenting a grand mal seizure? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: C
choices.text: Activity level prior to and following seizure

questions.rationale: Documentation on a seizure should include LOC following episode, activity prior to and following seizure, change in color, respiration, muscle tone, and length of seizure. Reporting of medication regimen is not necessary.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: The nurse is educating parents on prevention of eyestrain in their 5-year-old child. What information will the nurse include? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Words in books should be closely spaced.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Be sure desks and chairs are adequate height.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Instruct child to squint when reading.

questions.rationale: Children who are beginning to read need books with large type in which the letters are spaced far apart. The lighting must be adequate and without glare. Chairs and desks must be of the proper height.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Sensory or Neurological Condition
questions.stem: An 8-year-old near-drowning victim is rushed into the ED. What priorities of care will be implemented? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Respiratory and cardiovascular support, controlled rewarming, and maintenance of adequate cerebral oxygenation are priorities of care. The parents should be offered support, explanations of the therapy, and referral to social services, religious, or community agencies for follow-up.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.stem: What would the nurse include in planning teaching to parents of a child with Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease about the long-term effects of this disease?

choices.label: B
choices.text: The disease is self-limited and requires no long-term treatment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Degenerative arthritis may develop later in life.

choices.label: D
choices.text: There is risk of osteogenic sarcoma in adulthood.

questions.rationale: Marked distortion of the head of the femur may lead to an imperfect joint or to degenerative arthritis of the hip later in life.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.stem: What intervention will the nurse caring for a child in Buck skin traction implement?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Assist the child to be pulled up in bed.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Keep child‘s heel on the bed surface.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Maintain child‘s feet against the foot of the bed.

questions.rationale: Buck traction is a type of skin traction that relies on the child‘s weight as counterbalance. The child must be kept with head elevated no more than 20 degrees and pulled up in bed, and the feet should not touch the bed surface or the foot of the bed.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.stem: What will the nurse include when caring for a child in Buck‘s extension?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Positioning the child with hips flexed 90 degrees at all times

choices.label: B
choices.text: Keeping the weights in contact with the floor

choices.label: C
choices.text: Checking for skin irritation from traction equipment

choices.label: D
choices.text: Releasing the weights on a schedule

questions.rationale: The skin exposed to frequent friction may break down.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.stem: The nurse is reviewing the characteristics of Ewing‘s sarcoma. Which statement if made by the nurse indicates correct understanding of this disease?

choices.label: B
choices.text: “The disease is sensitive to radiation and chemotherapy.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “The disease is more prevalent among toddlers and preschoolers.”

questions.rationale: Ewing‘s sarcoma is sensitive to radiation therapy and chemotherapy. Amputation of the affected extremity is not recommended. This cancer occurs in school-age children and does metastasize.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.stem: What characteristic manifestation does the nurse caring for a child with Duchenne‘smuscular dystrophy document?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Exhibits atrophy of the calf muscles.

questions.rationale: Frequent falling and clumsiness are clinical manifestations of Duchenne‘s muscular dystrophy.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.stem: The nurse assessing a child with juvenile rheumatoid arthritis notes the child‘s right knee and ankle are swollen, warm, and tender. The child has a temperature of 38.8°C (102°F) and abdominal pain. What type of juvenile rheumatoid arthritis do these findings suggest?
questions.rationale: The systemic form of juvenile rheumatoid arthritis is associated with an elevated temperature, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), and C-reactive protein; abdominal pain; and a macular rash.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.stem: The nurse is providing instructions about how to treat a sprained ankle. What statement by the mother does the nurse recognize as indicative of a need for additional teaching?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Apply warm compresses to the ankle for the first 24 hours.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Put an ice pack on the ankle, alternating 30 minutes on with 30 minutes off.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Wrap the ankle in an Ace bandage for support.”

questions.rationale: Heat is not a treatment for soft tissue injuries. The principles of managing soft tissue injuries are rest, ice, compression, and elevation.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.stem: How does Russell traction provide adequate skin traction?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Does not interfere with range of motion.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Supplies continuous pull in two directions.

questions.rationale: Russell traction is skin traction, similar to Buck, with a sling positioned under the knee, which prevents subluxation of the tibia. Although the traction interferes with full ROM, the patient can change position without disrupting the continuous pull in two directions.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.stem: The nurse is checking for capillary refill on a child in Bryant‘s traction. How long does it take for the toe to regain color if adequate perfusion is assessed?
questions.rationale: Capillary refill in 3 seconds or less is determined to be indicative of adequate perfusion.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.stem: The parent of a child with osteomyelitis asks why his child is in so much pain. What will the nurse respond causes the pain experienced with osteomyelitis?
questions.rationale: Osteomyelitis is an infection of the bone. Inflammation produces an exudate that collects under the marrow and cortex of the bone. The vessels are compressed and thrombosis occurs, producing ischemia and pain.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.stem: A child hospitalized for treatment of osteomyelitis complains that he is tired of being sick and wants to know when the antibiotic protocol will end. How long will the nurse indicate that antibiotic therapy will probably last?
questions.rationale: Because osteomyelitis is an infection in the bone, antibiotics are given intravenously for 4 to 6 weeks.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.stem: What finding would the nurse assessing the neurovascular status of a child in Russell traction report immediately?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Skin that‘s warm to the touch

questions.rationale: Cyanosis or pallor noted in an extremity is an indication of circulatory impairment.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.stem: A 13-year-old girl is diagnosed with functional scoliosis. What does the nurse explain as the cause of this spinal curvature defect?
questions.rationale: Functional scoliosis usually is caused by poor posture, and it is not a spinal disease.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.stem: What intervention is appropriate for a nurse assessing a preadolescent child for scoliosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ask the child to bend forward at the waist and observe the child‘s back for asymmetry.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Observe the gait while the child is walking forward heel to toe.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Have the child flex the knees and look for uneven knee height.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Look at the child‘s shoulders and hips while fully clothed.

questions.rationale: The nurse looks at the back as the child bends forward for general body alignment and asymmetry.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.stem: What nursing action will significantly decrease the risk of serious complications for a child in Bryant‘s traction?

choices.label: C
choices.text: The child is restrained from rolling over.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The child‘s buttocks are resting on the bed.

questions.rationale: The nurse caring for a child in traction must be alert for Volkmann‘s ischemia, which occurs when circulation is obstructed.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.stem: Which intervention would be helpful in relieving morning discomfort associated with juvenile rheumatoid arthritis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Wearing splints at night to prevent extension contractures

choices.label: B
choices.text: Applying moist heat packs upon awakening

choices.label: C
choices.text: Taking a warm tub bath the evening before

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sleeping with two pillows under the head

questions.rationale: Application of moist heat, with a compress or by tub bath upon awakening in the morning, will help to lessen stiffness.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.stem: What instruction would the nurse provide to an adolescent who has been fitted with a Milwaukee brace?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Wear the brace directly against the skin.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Wear the brace over regular clothing.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Wear the brace over a T-shirt 23 hours a day.

questions.rationale: A Milwaukee brace is worn approximately 23 hours a day over a T-shirt, which protects the skin.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.stem: Which observation is most likely to cause the nurse to consider the possibility of child abuse when a mother says that her young child fell down the basement stairs?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Red, green, and yellow bruises on his body.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bruises are dispersed on his head, arms, and legs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A broken arm last year, and the child being described as accident-prone.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The mother is very anxious for her son to get medical attention.

questions.rationale: As bruises heal, they change color in stages. Different colors of bruises indicate that injuries have not all occurred at the same time. The nurse must consider whether the bruises match the caretaker‘s explanation of what happened.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.stem: A 6-year-old sustained a fractured femur and was put in Russell traction 2 days ago. She screams in pain when she raises herself onto the bedpan. Which nursing diagnosis takes highest priority for this child?

choices.label: B
choices.text: High risk for impaired skin integrity resulting from immobility

choices.label: C
choices.text: Altered growth and development related to separation from family

choices.label: D
choices.text: Altered urinary elimination related to immobility and traction

questions.rationale: Although all of these nursing diagnoses are relevant to the child in traction, pain resulting from muscle spasm and tissue trauma is the highest priority.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.stem: What would the nurse consider an abnormal finding on a musculoskeletal assessment of a 4-year-old child?
questions.rationale: Toe walking after 3 years of age may indicate a muscle problem.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.stem: Why does a child‘s fracture heal more rapidly than theadult‘s?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A child‘s bones are less porous than adult bone.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A child‘s bones are covered by a thicker periosteum.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A child‘s bones are not affected by bone overgrowth.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A child‘s bones have faster callus formation.

questions.rationale: Callus forms more rapidly in the child than the adult.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.stem: On entering the room of a child in Buck traction, the nurse makes all of the following observations. Which observation requires a nursing intervention?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Child‘s heels are placed firmly against the foot of the bed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Head of bed is elevated 20 degrees.

questions.rationale: Buck traction is dependent on the child as a counterweight. The heels should be elevated above the level of the foot of the bed.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.stem: Approximately how old does the nurse assess a large green bruise on the thigh of a 4-year-old to be?
questions.rationale: Bruises heal in various stages that are indicated according to color; after 5 to 7 days bruise are green.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.stem: A pediatric nurse is assisting with the care of a child diagnosed with a fractured femur. What type of fracture would be the most likely to alert the nurse to the possibility of physical abuse?
questions.rationale: A spiral fracture of the femur is caused by a forceful twisting motion. When the history of an injury does not correlate with x-ray findings, child abuse should be suspected because spiral fractures can be the result of manual twisting of the extremity.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.stem: A child is sent to the school nurse for assessment because she comes to school every day disheveled, unbathed, and hungry. The assessment does not indicate any bruises or marks on the body. What do these finding indicate?
questions.rationale: Physical neglect is the failure to provide for the basic physical needs of the child, including food, clothing, shelter, and basic cleanliness.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.stem: Which assessment performed by a nursing student performing a neurovascular check alerts the instructor that further education is necessary?
questions.rationale: Neurovascular checks include assessment of pain, pulse, sensation, color, capillary refill, and movement. Pupils are assessed with a neurological check.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.stem: What factor(s) may trigger abuse in a parent? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: E
choices.text: Knowledge deficit relative to child care

questions.rationale: All options except high self-esteem are possible triggers for a parent to become abusive.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.stem: The nurse demonstrates which similarities among all traction devices? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Tractions are designed to immobilize and pull limbs into extension. Traction can also align broken bones and decrease muscle spasm. Although some traction devices may relieve pain, many may actually cause pain.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.stem: The nurse performing a neurovascular check on a limb in traction would report and document which finding(s) as indicative of altered circulation? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Pulse is equal to uncasted limb.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Patient is aware of touch and warm and cold application.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Limb is cool to the touch.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Distal limb can flex and extend.

questions.rationale: The limb should be warm, and capillary refill should be less than 3 seconds.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.stem: How does the pediatric skeletal system differ from that of the adult? (Se/ect all that apply.)
questions.rationale: The child‘s skeletal system has lower mineral content, greater porosity, open epiphyses, greater bone strength, and a thicker periosteum.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Musculoskeletal Condition
questions.stem: The nurse explains that Bryant‘s traction is reserved for children who weigh less than pounds.
questions.rationale: Bryant‘s traction is a skin traction used in the treatment of orthopedic disorders of young children who weigh less than 30 pounds. Greater weight would cause excessive counterbalance and injury to soft tissues.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Respiratory Disorder
questions.stem: What will the nurse tell parents of a child with a positive throat culture for group A hemolytic streptococcus that the treatment is most likely to be?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Penicillin until his sore throat is gone

questions.rationale: When a throat culture is positive for group A beta-hemolytic streptococcus, penicillin is administered for 10 days even if symptoms are alleviated before the medication is finished.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Respiratory Disorder
questions.stem: Which initial intervention will the nurse suggest to the parents of a child experiencing laryngeal spasm?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Take the child outside in the cool air.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bring the child directly to the emergency department.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Take the child to the bathroom and turn on a hot shower.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Have the child drink plenty of fluids.

questions.rationale: The child experiencing laryngeal spasm should be placed in a high-humidity environment, such as the bathroom with a hot shower running. The humidity liquefies secretions and reduces spasm.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Respiratory Disorder
questions.stem: The nurse would observe a child for frequent swallowing after a tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy (T&A). What might this indicate?
questions.rationale: Hemorrhage is the most common postoperative complication. Blood trickling down the back of the child‘s throat could cause frequent swallowing.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Respiratory Disorder
questions.stem: What is the best choice for fluid replacement that the nurse can offer a child who has just had a tonsillectomy?
questions.rationale: Small amounts of clear liquids can be offered to the child. Synthetic fruit juices are not as irritating as natural juices. A popsicle is usually well-tolerated.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Respiratory Disorder
questions.stem: When auscultating breath sounds of an infant with respiratory syncytial virus, which assessment would the nurse immediately report?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Respiration rate decreases from 40 to 32 breaths/minute

choices.label: B
choices.text: Heart rate decreases from 110 to 100 beats/minute

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Quiet chest” from previous assessment of wheezing

questions.rationale: A “quiet chest” after assessment of wheezing indicates occlusion of air pathways and impending respiratory arrest. All other options are within normal range for infants undergoing oxygen administration.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Respiratory Disorder
questions.stem: What classic sign would the nurse, auscultating the breath sounds of a child hospitalized for an acute asthma attack, expect to find?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Decreased breath sounds at lung bases

questions.rationale: The child experiencing an acute asthma attack wheezes as air moves in and out of the narrowed airways. The expiratory wheeze is most pronounced.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Respiratory Disorder
questions.stem: What is the best intervention for the nurse caring for a child experiencing an acute asthma attack?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Offer plenty of fluids, particularly carbonated beverages.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Place the child in a humidified cool mist tent with oxygen.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Administer sedatives as ordered to decrease anxiety.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Position the child with arms resting on the overbed table.

questions.rationale: This position is comfortable and allows maximum use of the accessory muscles for breathing. Sedatives would mask symptoms of increasing air hunger. Carbonated beverages are contraindicated in persons with dyspnea.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Respiratory Disorder
questions.stem: What should the nurse explain to the parent of a child with exercise-induced asthma about when to inhale Cromolyn?

choices.label: B
choices.text: At the initial onset of the attack

choices.label: C
choices.text: During the attack to relieve symptoms

choices.label: D
choices.text: As often as 4 times a day

questions.rationale: Anti-inflammatory inhalants are taken before exercise to prevent attacks. These drugs can do nothing for the attack in progress. They are meant to be used as prophylactic therapies.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Respiratory Disorder
questions.stem: The parents of a 3-month-old infant with cystic fibrosis (CF) want to know how their child got this disease, because no one in either of their families has CF. What is the nurse‘s best response based on the understanding of CF?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Only one parent carries the CF gene.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Both parents are carriers of the CF gene.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The result is probably a genetic mutation.

questions.rationale: Cystic fibrosis is an inherited disease. Both parents must be carriers of the CF gene for the child to have the disease.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Respiratory Disorder
questions.stem: Which statement indicates that the child‘s parents understand how to perform respiratory therapy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “We do her postural drainage before the aerosol therapy.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “We give her respiratory treatments when she is coughing a lot.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “We give the aerosol followed by postural drainage before meals.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “She needs respiratory therapy every day when she has an infection.”

questions.rationale: Postural drainage for the child with CF is done following nebulization. Therapy is best scheduled before meals or at least 1 hour after eating to prevent vomiting.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Respiratory Disorder
questions.stem: What will the nurse teach the child with cystic fibrosis to take in order to facilitate digestion and absorption of nutrients?
questions.rationale: An oral pancreatic enzyme is given to the child with every meal and with snacks to replace the pancreatic enzymes that the child‘s body cannot produce.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Respiratory Disorder
questions.stem: How would the nurse advise a mother to clear the nostrils when her infant has a cold?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Clear the nasal passages after the infant has a feeding.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use over-the-counter nose drops to clear passages.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Remove nasal secretions with a bulb syringe.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Instill saline nose drops after clearing away secretions.

questions.rationale: The nasal passages can be cleared by instilling a few drops of saline into the nose and then suctioning the secretions with a bulb syringe.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Respiratory Disorder
questions.stem: The nurse offers a variety of fluids to a 5-year-old asthmatic child to compensate for the fluid loss through dyspnea. Which fluids are most appropriate?
questions.rationale: Room temperature fluids are the best. Carbonated and iced beverages increase spasm. Milk stimulates mucus production.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Respiratory Disorder
questions.stem: The asthmatic child who has been taking theophylline complains of stomachache and tachycardia and is sweating profusely. What does the nurse recognize as the cause of these symptoms?
questions.rationale: The symptoms described are the signs of theophylline toxicity.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Respiratory Disorder
questions.stem: The nurse is planning to teach parents about preventing sudden infant death syndrome (SIDS). What significant information would the nurse include?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Wrapping the infant snugly for rest periods

choices.label: B
