choices.text: Positioning the infant prone for sleep

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sitting the infant up in an infant seat

choices.label: D
choices.text: Placing infants on their backs or sides for sleep

questions.rationale: The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends that all healthy infants be placed in the supine or side-lying position on a firm mattress to prevent SIDS.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Respiratory Disorder
questions.stem: The nurse is caring for a toddler with acute laryngotracheobronchitis. Which assessment finding would indicate the child is experiencing increased respiratory obstruction?
questions.rationale: Restlessness is a primary sign of increased respiratory obstruction.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Respiratory Disorder
questions.stem: The teaching plan for the use of a dry powder inhaler for the treatment of asthma should include the warning to rinse the mouth after inhaling the powder. What does this prevent?
questions.rationale: Inhalant powders can cause candidiasis (yeast) infection of the mouth.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Respiratory Disorder
questions.stem: The nurse is caring for a 3-year-old child who suffered a smoke inhalation injury. How long is this patient at the highest risk for pulmonary edema after exposure?
questions.rationale: Pulmonary edema appears in a child with smoke inhalation injury 6 to 72 hours after exposure.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Respiratory Disorder
questions.stem: Which is the most appropriate nursing action when planning care for a child with cystic fibrosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Provide chest physiotherapy before meals every day.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Administer pancreas with protein food at mealtime.

questions.rationale: The maintenance of adequate nutrition is essential. The diet is high in protein and calories. Chest physiotherapy should be done between meals. Pancreatic enzyme powder should be given with applesauce or other nonstarch, nonfat, nonprotein food. Children with cystic fibrosis should be weighed daily.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Respiratory Disorder
questions.stem: The first child of a couple is being treated for bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD). They ask how to prevent this from happening with the child they are currently expecting. What will the nurse explain as the best way to prevent BPD?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Provision of oxygen therapy to the newborn

questions.rationale: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) is a fibrosis, or thickening, of the alveolar walls and the bronchiolar epithelium. It occurs in premature infants (less than 32 weeks) who have abnormal or arrested lung development and receive ventilation and oxygen for more than 28 days to survive. Respiratory distress in the newborn is the major reason why oxygen and ventilators are used for prolonged periods. The main cause of respiratory distress in the newborn is prematurity. Therefore, the prevention of preterm birth is the best way to prevent BPD.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Respiratory Disorder
questions.stem: The nurse describes the “allergic salute” as a cluster of what signs related to chronic allergy? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: The allergic salute does not include a productive cough.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Respiratory Disorder
questions.stem: The nurse would suggest the parents of an asthmatic child to encourage participation in which sport(s)? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Sports that require bursts of energy rather than long-term output of energy are suitable pursuits for asthmatics. Swimming, gymnastics, and baseball fit this criterion.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Respiratory Disorder
questions.stem: The nurse reports which assessments that suggest a meconium ileus in a newborn? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Distended abdomen, vomiting, and absence of stool are the signs indicating meconium ileus in the newborn.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Respiratory Disorder
questions.stem: What would the nurse teaching an asthmatic child the technique of pursed-lip breathing include? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Inhale deeply through nose with mouth closed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Make exhalation twice as long as inhalation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use medicated inhaler prior to perform breathing exercise.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Exhale through mouth as if whistling.

questions.rationale: The technique requires that breath be inhaled through the nose and exhaled through pursed lips in a nonforceful manner. The exhalation should be twice as long as the inhalation.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Respiratory Disorder
questions.stem: A toddler must maintain bed rest for the diagnosis of pneumonia. What actions will the nurse implement? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Confinement to bed for a child does not always result in physical rest. In pediatrics, “bed rest” means providing play therapy that promotes minimal activity. The nurse should consider the age and developmental level of the child and the activity level involved in the play when designing appropriate activities and guiding parents in the home care of their child.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Respiratory Disorder
questions.stem: The school nurse suspects a first-grade student has sinusitis. Which symptoms might lead the nurse to this suspicion? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Severe wheezing is auscultated on inspiration.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Child reports, “I have had a cold for 2 weeks.”

questions.rationale: Child reports, “I have had a cold for 2 weeks.” d. Nurse observes periorbital swelling. e. Halitosis is present. The proximity of the sinus to the tooth roots often results in tooth pain when the sinus is infected. The maxillary and ethmoid sinuses are most often involved in childhood sinusitis. Therefore, the signs and symptoms of sinusitis in children are different from those in adults, depending on the age of the child and which sinus is fully developed. An acute sinusitis is suspected when an upper respiratory infection lasts longer than 10 days, with a daytime cough. Halitosis is often present. Untreated sinusitis can lead to periorbital cellulitis. Severe wheezing is not indicative of sinusitis.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Respiratory Disorder
questions.stem: The nurse is caring for a 4-year-old child diagnosed with H. influenzae type B. Which signs and symptoms exhibited by the child would alert the nurse to suspect epiglottitis? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: H. influenzae type B and most often occurs in children 3 to 6 years of age. It can occur in any season. The course is rapid and progressive. The onset of epiglottitis is abrupt, and the child presents with classic symptoms. The child insists on sitting up, leans forward with the mouth open, and drools saliva because of the difficulty in swallowing. The child appears wide-eyed, anxious, and restless, and he or she may emit a froglike croaking sound on inspiration. Cough is absent. Inspection of the throat shows an enlarged, reddened edematous epiglottis much like a “beefy-red thumb.” However, the examining tongue blade may trigger a laryngospasm and result in sudden respiratory arrest.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Respiratory Disorder
questions.stem: What will the nurse discourage when providing education to parents of a child with asthma? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Use of stuffed toys is discouraged due to potential allergens. Basketball might not be well tolerated because of the constant physical exertion. Certain pets are encouraged, gymnastics is usually well tolerated, and cotton blankets are recommended for children with asthma.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Respiratory Disorder
questions.stem: After the 3-month-old child with respiratory syncytial virus is given a protocol of antiviral medications, the nurse explains that routine immunizations will need to be delayed for months.
questions.rationale: After a protocol of antiviral medications, the routine immunizations should be delayed because the antiviral medications affect the integrity of the immunizations.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Cardiovascular Disorder
questions.stem: What does the nurse explain that a ventricular septal defect will allow?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blood to shunt left to right, causing increased pulmonary flow and no cyanosis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blood to shunt right to left, causing decreased pulmonary flow and cyanosis

choices.label: C
choices.text: No shunting because of high pressure in the left ventricle

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased pressure in the left atrium, impeding circulation of oxygenated blood in the circulating volume

questions.rationale: Pulmonary blood flow is increased when a ventricular septal defect exists. The blood shifts from left to right because of the higher pressure in the left ventricle. This particular shift does not cause cyanosis.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Cardiovascular Disorder
questions.stem: Which assessment would lead the nurse to suspect that a newborn infant has a ventricular septal defect?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A loud, harsh murmur with a systolic thrill

choices.label: C
choices.text: Blood pressure higher in the arms than in the legs OREO) = &: 2

questions.rationale: A loud, harsh murmur combined with a systolic thrill is characteristic of a ventricular septal defect.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Cardiovascular Disorder
questions.stem: What finding would the nurse expect when measuring blood pressure on all four extremities of a child with coarctation of the aorta?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blood pressure higher on the right side

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blood pressure higher on the left side

choices.label: C
choices.text: Blood pressure lower in the arms than in the legs

choices.label: D
choices.text: Blood pressure lower in the legs than in the arms

questions.rationale: The characteristic symptoms of coarctation of the aorta are a marked difference in blood pressure and pulses between the upper and lower extremities. Pressure is increased proximal to the defect and decreased distal to the coarctation.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Cardiovascular Disorder
questions.stem: A father asks why his child with tetralogy of Fallot seems to favor a squatting position. What is the nurse‘s best response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Squatting increases the return of venous blood back to the heart.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Squatting decreases arterial blood flow away from the heart.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Squatting is a common resting position when a child is tachycardic.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Squatting increases the workload of the heart.

questions.rationale: The squatting position allows the child to breathe more easily because systemic venous return is increased.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Cardiovascular Disorder
questions.stem: An infant is experiencing dyspnea related to patent ductus arteriosus (PDA). What does the nurse understand regarding why dyspnea occurs?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blood is circulated through the lungs again, causing pulmonary circulatory congestion.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blood is shunted past the pulmonary circulation, causing pulmonary hypoxia.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Blood is shunted past cardiac arteries, causing myocardial hypoxia.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Blood is circulated through the ductus from the pulmonary artery to the aorta, bypassing the left side of the heart.

questions.rationale: When PDA is present, oxygenated blood recycles through the lungs, overburdening the pulmonary circulation.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Cardiovascular Disorder
questions.stem: Which is the most appropriate nursing action related to the administration of digoxin (Lanoxin) to an infant?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Counting the apical rate for 30 seconds before administering the medication

choices.label: B
choices.text: Withholding a dose if the apical heart rate is less than 100 beats/minute

choices.label: C
choices.text: Repeating a dose if the child vomits within 30 minutes of the previous dose

choices.label: D
choices.text: Checking respiratory rate and blood pressure before each dose

questions.rationale: As a tule, if the pulse rate of an infant is less than 100 beats/minute, the medication is withheld and the physician is notified.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Cardiovascular Disorder
questions.stem: Achild develops carditis from rheumatic fever. Which areas of the heart are affected by carditis?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Heart muscle and the mitral valve

questions.rationale: The tissues that cover the heart and heart valves are affected. The heart muscle may be involved and the mitral valve is frequently involved.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Cardiovascular Disorder
questions.stem: Which comment made by a parent of a 1-month-old infant would alert the nurse about the presence of a congenital heart defect?

choices.label: C
choices.text: “He is fussy for several hours every day.”

questions.rationale: Fatigue during feeding or activity is common to most infants with congenital cardiac problems.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Cardiovascular Disorder
questions.stem: The nurse is caring for a child with a diagnosis of Kawasaki disease. The child‘s parent asks the nurse, “How does Kawasaki disease affect my child‘s heart and blood vessels?” On what understanding is the nurse‘s response based?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Inflammation weakens blood vessels, leading to aneurysm.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increased lipid levels lead to the development of atherosclerosis.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Untreated disease causes mitral valve stenosis.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Altered blood flow increases cardiac workload with resulting heart failure.

questions.rationale: Inflammation of vessels weakens the walls of the vessels and often results in aneurysm.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Cardiovascular Disorder
questions.stem: The nurse explained how to position an infant with tetralogy of Fallot if the infant suddenly becomes cyanotic. Which statement by the father leads the nurse to determine he understood the instructions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Ifthe baby turns blue, I will hold him against my shoulder with his knees bent up toward his chest.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Ifthe baby turns blue, I will lay him down on a firm surface with his head lower than the rest of his body.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Ifthe baby turns blue, I will immediately put the baby upright in an infant seat.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Ifthe baby turns blue, I will put the baby in supine position with his head elevated.”

questions.rationale: In the event of a paroxysmal hypercyanotic or “tet” spell, the infant should be placed in a knee-chest position.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Cardiovascular Disorder
questions.stem: The parent ofa 1-year-old child with tetralogy of Fallot asks the nurse, “Why do my child‘s fingertips look like that?” On what understanding does the nurse base a response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Clubbing occurs as a result of untreated congestive heart failure.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clubbing occurs as a result of a left-to-right shunting of blood.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Clubbing occurs as a result of decreased cardiac output.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Clubbing occurs as a result of chronic hypoxia.

questions.rationale: Clubbing of the fingers develops in response to chronic hypoxia.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Cardiovascular Disorder
questions.stem: A child has an elevated antistreptolysin O (ASO) titer. Which combination of symptoms, in conjunction with this finding, would confirm a diagnosis of rheumatic fever?
questions.rationale: The presence of two major Jones criteria would indicate a high probability of rheumatic fever.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Cardiovascular Disorder
questions.stem: An infant with congestive heart failure is receiving digoxin (Lanoxin). What does the nurse recognize as a sign of digoxin toxicity?
questions.rationale: Symptoms of digoxin toxicity include nausea, vomiting, anorexia, irregularity in pulse rate and rhythm, and a sudden change in pulse.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Cardiovascular Disorder
questions.stem: Through what does the infant born with hypoplastic left heart syndrome acquire oxygenated blood?

choices.label: C
choices.text: The closure of the foramen ovale

questions.rationale: Because the right side of the heart must take over pumping blood to both the lungs and systemic circulation, the ductus arteriosus must remain open to shunt the oxygenated blood from the lungs.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Cardiovascular Disorder
questions.stem: A child with rheumatic fever begins involuntary, purposeless movements of her limbs. What does the nurse recognize that this indicates?
questions.rationale: As the effects of rheumatic fever affect the central nervous system, the child may develop Sydenham‘s chorea, manifested by involuntary, purposeless movements of the limbs.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Cardiovascular Disorder
questions.stem: How long should a 4-year-old child recovering from rheumatic fever need to receive monthly injections of penicillin G?
questions.rationale: Children who recover from rheumatic fever should have a chemoprophylaxis protocol of penicillin G injections (about 200,000 units per dose) for a minimum of 5 years or up to the age of 18 years to prevent further bouts of rheumatic fever.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Cardiovascular Disorder
questions.stem: What is accurate about the characteristics of high-density lipoproteins (HDLs)?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They have high amounts of triglycerides.

choices.label: B
choices.text: They have only small amounts of protein.

questions.rationale: HDLs have low amounts of triglycerides, large amounts of proteins, and low amount of cholesterol, and are excreted via the liver. They have no role in the production of steroids.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Cardiovascular Disorder
questions.stem: The nurse is planning a hypertension-prevention program. What should be the main focus of the nurse when presenting information?
questions.rationale: The main focus of a hypertension-prevention program is patient education.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Cardiovascular Disorder
questions.stem: A pediatric patient is scheduled for a noninvasive procedure to determine if his heart is structurally normal and to localize a murmur. What diagnostic test does the nurse anticipate?
questions.rationale: Echocardiography is a noninvasive procedure that localizes murmurs and determines if the heart is structurally normal.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Cardiovascular Disorder
questions.stem: How would the nurse caring for an infant with congestive heart failure (CHF) modify feeding techniques to adapt for the child‘s weakness and fatigue? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Feeding more frequently with smaller feedings

choices.label: B
choices.text: Using a soft nipple with enlarged holes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Holding and cuddling the child during feeding

questions.rationale: Infants with CHF fatigue easily. Feeding can be given more frequently in smaller amounts through a soft, large-holed nipple. Formulas with a denser caloric content can be offered. The child may be encouraged to nurse if he or she is held.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Cardiovascular Disorder
questions.stem: What are the four structural heart anomalies that make up the tetralogy of Fallot? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: The four anomalies that comprise tetralogy of Fallot are hypertrophied right ventricle, patent ductus arteriosus, stenosis of pulmonary artery, and dextroposition of the aorta.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Cardiovascular Disorder
questions.stem: What assessment(s) in a child with tetralogy of Fallot would indicate the child is experiencing a paroxysmal hypercyanotic episode? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Indicators of a paroxysmal hypercyanotic episode or a “tet” episode are spontaneous cyanosis, dyspnea, weakness, and syncope.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Cardiovascular Disorder
questions.stem: Which congenital cardiac defect(s) cause(s) increased pulmonary blood flow? (Select ail that apply.)
questions.rationale: The congenital heart defects that cause increased pulmonary blood flow are ASDs, VSDs, and patent ductus arteriosus.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Cardiovascular Disorder
questions.stem: A 16-year-old patient is diagnosed with primary hypertension. What risk factors does the nurse mention when providing education on this diagnosis to the patient and his family? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Primary, or essential, hypertension implies that no known underlying disease is present. Nevertheless, heredity, obesity, stress, and a poor diet and exercise pattern can contribute to any type of hypertension.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: The nurse is teaching the parents of a young child with iron deficiency anemia about nutrition. What food would the nurse emphasize as being a rich source of iron?
questions.rationale: Good nutritional sources of iron include boiled egg yolk, liver, green leafy vegetables, Cream of Wheat, dried fruits, beans, nuts, and whole-grain breads.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: Which statement by a mother may indicate a cause for her 9-month-old‘s iron deficiency anemia?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Formula is so expensive. We switched to regular milk right away.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “She doesn‘t really like peaches or pears, so we stick to bananas for fruit.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “TI give her a piece of bread now and then. She likes to chew on it.”

questions.rationale: Because cow‘s milk contains very little iron, infants should drink iron-fortified formula for the first year of life.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: What will the nurse administer with ferrous sulfate drops when providing them to a child on the pediatric unit?
questions.rationale: Vitamin C aids in the absorption of iron, whereas food and milk interfere with the absorption of iron.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: What is the result of a deficiency of factor IX?
questions.rationale: Christmas disease, or hemophilia B, is caused by the deficiency of factor IX.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: A 2-year-old child has been diagnosed with hemophilia A. What information should the nurse include in a teaching plan about home care?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If bleeding occurs, apply pressure, ice, elevate, and rest the extremity.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Children‘s aspirin in lowered doses may be given for joint discomfort.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A firm, dry toothbrush should be used to clean teeth at least twice a day.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Do not permit interactive play with other children.

questions.rationale: When bleeding occurs, the traditional approach is to follow RICE—test, ice, compression, and elevation.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: What will the nurse teach the parents of a child with a low platelet count to avoid?
questions.rationale: Aspirin interferes with platelet function and should be avoided to prevent the risk of prolonged bleeding.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: What should the nurse closely assess in a child receiving a transfusion?
questions.rationale: The child receiving a blood transfusion is observed for signs of a transfusion reaction including chills, itching, fever, rash, headache, and back pain.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: On admission, a child with leukemia has widespread purpura and a platelet count of 19,000/mm*. What is the priority nursing intervention?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Monitoring vital signs during platelet transfusions

choices.label: D
choices.text: Providing family education about how to prevent bleeding

questions.rationale: When platelets are low, the greatest danger is spontaneous intracranial bleeding. Neurological assessments are therefore a priority of care.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: An adolescent is diagnosed with Hodgkin‘s disease. Lymph nodes on both sides of her diaphragm have been found to be involved, including cervical and inguinal nodes. Which disease stage is this? a I b.
questions.rationale: Lymph node regions on both sides of the diaphragm are consistent with a diagnosis of stage-III Hodgkin‘s disease.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: A 3-year-old child with sickle cell disease is admitted to the hospital in sickle cell crisis with severe abdominal pain. Which type of crisis is the child most likely experiencing?
questions.rationale: Vaso-occlusive crisis, or painful crisis, is caused by obstruction of blood flow by sickle cells, infarctions, and some degrees of vasospasm.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: Which statement made by a parent indicates an understanding of health maintenance of a child with sickle cell disease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Tshould give my child a daily iron supplement.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “It is important for my child to drink plenty of fluids.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “He needs to wear protective equipment if he plays contact sports.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “He shouldn‘t receive any immunizations until he is older.”

questions.rationale: Prevention of dehydration, which can trigger the sickling process, is a priority goal in the care of a child with sickle cell disease.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: A newly married couple is seeking genetic counseling because they are both carriers of the sickle cell trait. How can the nurse best explain the children‘s risk of inheriting this disease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Every fourth child will have the disease; two others will be carriers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All of their children will be carriers, just as they are.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Each child has a one in four chance of having the disease and a two in four chance of being a carrier.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The risk levels of their children cannot be determined by this information.

questions.rationale: The sickle cell gene is inherited from both parents; therefore, each offspring has a one in four chance of inheriting the disease.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: A child with thalassemia major receives blood transfusions frequently. What is a complication of repeated blood transfusions?
questions.rationale: As a result of repeated blood transfusions, excessive deposits of iron (hemosiderosis) are stored in tissues.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: A child has just been diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia. What is the result of an overproduction of immature white blood cells in the bone marrow?
questions.rationale: An overproduction of immature white blood cells increases the child‘s susceptibility to infection.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: The child receiving a transfusion complains of back pain and itching. What is the best initial action by the nurse?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Clamp off blood and keep line open with normal saline.

questions.rationale: Ifa blood transfusion reaction occurs, the first action is to stop the blood infusion, keep the line open with normal saline, and notify the charge nurse.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: What would the nurse include in a teaching plan about mouth care of a child receiving chemotherapy?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clean teeth with a soft toothbrush.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inspect the mouth weekly for ulcerations.

questions.rationale: A soft toothbrush reduces capillary damage and mucous membrane breakdown and prevents bleeding and infection. Commercial mouthwashes may kill oral flora that combat infection. Water-Pik is useful for toughening gums.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: A 6-year-old child with leukemia asks, “Who will take care of me in heaven?” What is the best response by the nurse?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Who do you think will take care of you?”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Your grandparents and God will take care of you.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Your mom will know more about that than I do.”

questions.rationale: This response gives the child an opportunity to verbalize his or her feelings and concerns, whereas closed responses shut off communication. The asking of a “why” question is not therapeutic as it calls for justification.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: The nurse is dealing with a preschool child with a life-threatening illness. What should the nurse remember the child‘s concept of death is at this age?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Only a fear of separation from her parents

choices.label: C
choices.text: That a person becomes alive again soon after death

choices.label: D
choices.text: An understanding based on simple logic

questions.rationale: The preschooler views death as reversible and temporary.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: The nurse notes that a 4-year-old child‘s gums bleed easily and he has bruising and petechiae on his extremities. Which lab value is consistent with these symptoms?
questions.rationale: The normal platelet count is 150,000 to 400,000/mm‘. This finding is very low, indicating an increased bleeding potential.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: The nurse, caring for a child receiving chemotherapy, notes that the child‘s abdomen is firm and slightly distended. There is no record of a bowel movement for the last 2 days. What do these assessment findings suggest?
questions.rationale: Peripheral neuropathy may be signaled by severe constipation resulting from decreased nerve sensations in the bowel.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: The nurse finds an adolescent with Hodgkin‘s disease crying. The adolescent says, “I am so scared.” What is the most appropriate nursing response to this comment?

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Ts this the strongest feeling you‘ve had today?”

questions.rationale: The nurse should encourage the adolescent to express her feelings and concerns.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: The most recent blood count for a child who received chemotherapy last week shows neutropenia. What is the priority nursing diagnosis for this child?
questions.rationale: The child with neutropenia is at risk for infection.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: What important focus of nursing care for the dying child and the family should the nurse implement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Nursing care should be organized to minimize contact with the child.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Adequate oral intake is crucial to the dying child.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Families should be made aware that hearing is the last sense to stop functioning before death.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is best for the family if the nursing staff provides all of the child‘s care.

questions.rationale: Hearing is intact even when there is a loss of consciousness.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: The nurse is presenting information on the congenital disorder of hemophilia A. What fact will the nurse include?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is seen in males and females equally.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is transmitted by symptom-free females.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a defective gene located on the Y chromosome.

questions.rationale: Hemophilia A affects mostly males who received the sex-linked recessive trait from a symptom-free female. The defective gene is on the X chromosome.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: Acchild is diagnosed with iron deficiency anemia. What will the nurse explain can occur if this disorder goes untreated?
questions.rationale: Untreated iron deficiency anemias progress slowly, and in severe cases the heart muscle becomes too weak to function. If this happens, heart failure follows.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: The nurse is caring for a child with a low platelet count. What skin assessments would alert the nurse to bleeding? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: The reduction or destruction of platelets in the body interferes with the clotting mechanism. Skin lesions that are common to these disorders include petechiae, a bluish, nonblanching, pinpoint-sized lesion; purpura, groups of adjoining petechiae; ecchymosis, an isolated bluish lesion larger than a petechia; and hematoma, a raised ecchymosis. Lymphadenopathy is an enlargement of lymph nodes that is indicative of infection or disease.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: Why would the nurse urge the family of a dying 12-year-old boy to include his 8-year-old sister in care? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: She will feel less neglected by the parents.

choices.label: B
choices.text: She can make amends for past hostilities to her brother.

choices.label: D
choices.text: She can express her feelings through care.

choices.label: E
choices.text: She can experience being supportive of her parents and brother.

questions.rationale: All options are potential benefits to including the sibling in the care of a dying child except increased helplessness. She would feel less helpless.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: What should be included in the nursing care of a 12-year-old child receiving radiation therapy for Hodgkin‘s disease? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Sun block should be applied to skin after radiation to prevent burning. Low energy levels produce anorexia and anger in many young patients. Radiation delays the development of secondary sex characteristics and menses. Effects of Radiation

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: What are the classic symptoms of thalassemia major (Cooley‘s anemia)? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: All of the options are classic signs of thalassemia major except renal failure.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: How has synthetic recombinant antihemophilic factor improved the management of hemophilia? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Eliminates the need for frequent transfusions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Can be administered by family at home.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reduces cost of care of the hemophiliac.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reduces risk of HIV and hepatitis A and B transmission.

questions.rationale: The drug can be given at home by the family. Because it supplies the missing factor, transfusions are not necessary and consequently the exposure to HIV and hepatitis A and B is reduced. Cost of care is greatly reduced because hospitalizations and transfusions are not as frequently required. The drug does not prevent hemorrhage; it makes hemorrhage manageable.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: The family of a child receiving chemotherapy for leukemia should be taught to focus on which aspect(s) of the child‘s care? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Support groups are helpful for emotional support and realistic tips on care. The child on chemotherapy is anorexic and has no appetite. Maintenance of hydration is essential for the adequate therapeutic effect of the drugs. Because the drugs suppress the bone marrow, children are at risk for infection, and the suppression will not allow the antibody response needed for immunization.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: The nurse explains that the COPP medical regimen for the treatment of Hodgkin‘s disease uses a combination of which drugs? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: The COPP medical regimen includes the combination of cyclophosphamide, vincristine (Oncovin), prednisone, and procarbazine hydrochloride.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Condition of the Blood, Blood-Forming Organs, or Lymphatic System
questions.stem: A school-aged child is living with a chronic disease process. How would the nurse anticipate chronic illness will effect growth and development? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: A school-age child is in the stage of industry versus inferiority. A chronic illness might experience loss of grade level in school because of illness and inability to participate or compete can lead to sense of inferiority. Sense of independence and accomplishment can be lost. Being different from peers may impede child‘s sense of belonging.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: Which finding in a newborn is suggestive of tracheoesophageal fistula?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Failure to pass meconium in 24 hours

choices.label: C
choices.text: Palpable mass in the sternal area

questions.rationale: After birth, a newborn with tracheoesophageal fistula will vomit and choke when the first feeding is introduced.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: Acchild is brought to the pediatric clinic because he has been vomiting for the past 2 days. What acid-base imbalance would the nurse expect to occur from this persistent vomiting?
questions.rationale: Hydrochloric acid and sodium chloride from the stomach are lost from persistent vomiting. This results in alkalosis.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: On the second day of hospitalization for a 3-month-old brought in for treatment for gastroenteritis, the nurse makes all of the assessments listed below. Which assessment finding indicates ineffectiveness of treatment?
questions.rationale: Weight loss is the most significant indicator of dehydration because an infant‘s weight comprises 77% water.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: Why are rapid respirations a possible cause of dehydration?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They prevent the child from drinking.

choices.label: B
choices.text: They increase circulation, thus increasing urine production.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They cause evaporation of fluid on the mucous membranes.

questions.rationale: Rapid respirations cause increased insensible fluid loss.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: Which is the most appropriate intervention for a 3-month-old infant who has gastroesophageal reflux?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Position the infant in the crib on his or her abdomen, with the head elevated.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Administer medication as ordered to stimulate the pyloric sphincter.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Give thin rice cereal with formula before feeding solid foods.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Place the infant in an infant seat after feedings.

questions.rationale: After feedings, the infant is placed in a prone position to avoid increased intraabdominal pressure.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: The nurse is interviewing parents of an infant with pyloric stenosis. What would the nurse expect the parents to report?
questions.rationale: Vomiting is the outstanding symptom of pyloric stenosis. Food is ejected with considerable force, which is described as projectile vomiting.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: A mother reports that her child has been scratching the anal area and complaining of itching. What does the nurse suspect based on this information?
questions.rationale: With pinworms, the nurse or parent may notice that the child scratches the anal area and complains of itchiness. The other choices do not cause this reaction.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: The nurse is teaching a parent about pyrvinium (Povan). What would be included in regard to potential side effects?
questions.rationale: The nurse should advise parents that pyrvinium stains clothing and turns stools red.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: What instruction will the nurse give to parents about preventing the spread and reinfection of pinworms?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Clean the bathroom with bleach solution.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Wash bed linens in cold water.

questions.rationale: One intervention to prevent the further spread of pinworms is to keep the child‘s fingernails short. Pinworms are not spread from person to person.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: A mother reports that her 2-year-old child experiences constipation frequently. Which food would the nurse recommend to include in the child‘s diet?
questions.rationale: Dietary modifications for constipation include eating more high-roughage foods such as whole-grain breads and cereals.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: What description of a child‘s stool characteristic leads the nurse to suspect intussusception?
questions.rationale: Bowel movements of blood and mucus that contain no feces (“currant jelly” stools) are common about 12 hours after the onset of the obstruction.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: What is the treatment of choice for a child with intussusception?

choices.label: C
choices.text: IV fluids until the spasms subside

questions.rationale: A barium enema is the treatment of choice for intussusception because the passage of the barium frequently “un-telescopes” the bowel. Surgery is scheduled only if reduction is not achieved.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: Parents ask the nurse how their infant developed a Meckel‘s diverticulum. What condition, will the nurse explain, is present causing this diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The yolk sac remains connected to the intestine.

choices.label: B
choices.text: There is inflammation of the ileocecal valve.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A pouch forms when the vitelline duct fails to disappear.

choices.label: D
choices.text: There is a weakness in the abdominal wall.

questions.rationale: If the vitelline duct fails to disappear completely after birth, a blind pouch may form.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: An infant is admitted to the hospital with severe isotonic dehydration. For what is this child at the highest risk?
questions.rationale: Shock is the greatest threat to life in isotonic dehydration.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: A child is brought to the emergency department because he ingested an unknown quantity of acetaminophen (Tylenol). What does the nurse expect this child to receive following gastric lavage?
questions.rationale: Gastric lavage is followed by N-acetylcysteine (Mucomyst), the antidote for acetaminophen.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: The nurse is planning a parent education program about lead poisoning prevention. What will be included regarding primary sources of lead in the community?
questions.rationale: The primary source of lead is paint from old, deteriorating buildings.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: A frightened mother calls the pediatrician‘s office because her child swallowed dishwashing detergent. What is the most appropriate action?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Induce vomiting by giving the child syrup of ipecac.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Take the child to the local emergency department.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Give the child activated charcoal mixed with juice.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Give the child milk to soothe affected mucous membranes.

questions.rationale: Inducing vomiting is no longer recommended because it may pose additional problems. The child should be taken immediately to the nearest emergency department along with the packaging of the ingested substance.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: A child has been diagnosed with ascariasis (roundworm). Which statement made by her mother that may suggest a cause for her condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “T‘ve been airing out the house on these nice breezy days.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “My child often goes out to the garden and pulls up a carrot to eat.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “She runs barefoot so much I have to wash her feet at least twice a day.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “We just remodeled our bathroom at home.”

questions.rationale: The child can ingest roundworm eggs from contaminated soil.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: What does the nurse expect the appearance of the stools of a child with celiac disease to be?
questions.rationale: Celiac disease causes malabsorption. Stools that are large, bulky, and frothy may indicate malabsorption.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: The nurse has reviewed dietary restrictions for celiac disease with concerned parents. Which grain will the nurse explain can be eaten with celiac disease?
questions.rationale: Rice is a gluten-free grain that can be eaten by children afflicted with celiac disease. These children will have a lifelong restriction of wheat, oats, barley, and rye.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: A 7-month-old infant is admitted to the hospital with a diagnosis of acute gastroenteritis. What will be the nurse's priority goal of the infant‘s care?
questions.rationale: The priority goal of care in gastroenteritis is preventing fluid and electrolyte imbalance. Gastroenteritis

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: The nurse is speaking to the parent of a 3-year-old child who has mild diarrhea. What dietary modification would the nurse advise?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Soft foods with rice, bananas, toast, and applesauce

choices.label: B
choices.text: Small amounts of clear fluids such as gelatin

choices.label: C
choices.text: An oral rehydrating solution, such as Pedialyte

choices.label: D
choices.text: Chicken soup because it is high in sodium

questions.rationale: An oral rehydrating solution is recommended to replace fluids and electrolytes lost from frequent bowel movements.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: What would the nurse expect to find in a child admitted to the hospital for nonorganic failure to thrive?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Be limp like a rag doll

choices.label: D
choices.text: Weigh in the 10th percentile for age

questions.rationale: Some children with failure to thrive have rag-doll limpness (hypotonia) and appear wary of their caregivers.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: Which nursing interventions will be implemented for the mother of a 10-month-old infant with nonorganic failure to thrive?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Pointing out errors that the nurse observes when the mother is caring for the infant

choices.label: B
choices.text: Discussing negative characteristics of the infant with the mother

choices.label: C
choices.text: Having the nurse provide as much of the infant‘s care as possible

choices.label: D
choices.text: Teaching the mother about the developmental milestones to expect in the next few months

questions.rationale: The nurse can increase parent‘s knowledge of growth and development by providing anticipatory guidance about normal developmental milestones.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: Which statement by a mother may indicate a cause of her son‘s vitamin C deficiency?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “We get our fruits from homemade preserves.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “We use milk from our own goats.”

questions.rationale: Vitamin C is destroyed by heat.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: The nurse is instructing a mother how to administer oral nystatin suspension prescribed to treat thrush. What will the nurse include?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Pour the prescribed amount into a nipple and have the infant suck the medication.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Squirt the prescribed dose into the back of the mouth and have the infant swallow.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Give the medication mixed with a small amount of juice in a bottle.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use a sterile applicator to swab the medication on the oral mucosa.

questions.rationale: An appropriate way to administer nystatin is to moisten a sterile applicator with the medication and then swab it on the inside of the mouth.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: Why are infants more vulnerable to fluid and electrolyte imbalances than adults?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They have a smaller surface area than adults in proportion to body weight.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Water needs and losses per kilogram are lower than those for adults.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A greater percentage of body water in infants is extracellular.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Infants have a lower metabolic turnover of water.

questions.rationale: A greater percentage of body water is contained in the extracellular compartment of children under 2 years of age.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: An infant is admitted to the hospital with severe dehydration. Laboratory results show pH 7.32, PaCO2 40, HCO; 21. How does the nurse interpret these values?
questions.rationale: A pH lower than 7.35 indicates acidosis. If the child‘s pH falls in the same line as the HCO3,, the problem is metabolic (see Table 27-4).

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: Following surgery for pyloric stenosis, an infant awoke from anesthesia hungry and crying. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Delay feeding the child for 6 hours.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Offer regular formula thinned with water.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Give small amounts of regular formula thickened with cereal.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Allow 1 ounce of glucose water at frequent intervals.

questions.rationale: Small oral feedings of glucose water are given after recovery from anesthesia. Feedings are gradually increased to larger amounts of regular formula or breastmilk.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: The nurse is caring for an 18-pound child who has had one stool of diarrhea. The nurse knows that the child needs to consume how many milliliters of oral fluid to make up for the fluid loss?
questions.rationale: The formula for oral fluid replacement is 10 mL/kg. 18 pounds = 8.1 kg x 10 = 81 mL.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: Which statement made by a parent alerts the nurse to the need for additional education about poison prevention?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Ikeep the poison control center phone number easily accessible.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “All medication is kept out of reach in a locked cabinet.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Tkeep a bottle of syrup of ipecac handy.”

questions.rationale: Traditionally, syrup of ipecac was the treatment of choice to remove some types of poisons from a child‘s system and parents were advised to keep a supply on hand in the home. However, the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) revised this policy in 2003. Parents are now advised to call the poison control center and bring the container of the substance ingested to the hospital emergency department as quickly as possible because stomach lavage is rarely effective 1 hour or more after ingestion. Ipecac syrup should not be kept in the home. Uncontrolled vomiting can cause serious complications.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: Which assessment would the nurse report to the physician immediately? asia

choices.label: A
choices.text: 2-month-old with a urine output of 150 mL in 24 hours

choices.label: B
choices.text: 3-year-old with a urine output of 650 mL in 24 hours

choices.label: C
choices.text: §8-year-old with a urine output of over 1000 mL in 24 hours

choices.label: D
choices.text: 14-year-old with a urine output of 800 mL in 24 hours

questions.rationale: The urine output of a 2-month-old infant should be between 400 and 500 mL/24 hours.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: What interventions will the nurse perform when feeding a child with pyloric stenosis? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Give a formula thinned with water.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Burp the infant before and during feeding.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Position infant on left side after feeding.

questions.rationale: Children with pyloric stenosis are given formula or breastmilk thickened with cereal; the infant is burped before and during feeding to get rid of any gas in the stomach; the infant is fed slowly and refed if vomiting occurs. The infant is positioned on the right side to allow the weight of the feeding to stay in the stomach against the pyloric valve.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: What assessment(s) would lead a nurse to suspect Hirschsprung‘s disease in a 1-month-old infant? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: All options are significant indicators of Hirschsprung‘s disease.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: What sign(s) indicate(s) moderate dehydration? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: The child that is moderately dehydrated will have lost 10% of his body weight, will have dry mucous membranes, normal (nonsunken) anterior fontanelle, decreased urine output, and will be irritable.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: A child is brought into the ED with suspected appendicitis. What signs and symptoms does the nurse expect to assess? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pain on lifting thigh when supine

questions.rationale: With appendicitis on examination, characteristic tenderness in the right lower quadrant known as McBurney‘s point will occur. Other diagnostic signs include guarding (tightening of the abdominal muscles or rigidity of the abdomen on palpation); rebound tenderness (pressing the RLQ with rapid release of pressure causes severe pain); pain on lifting the thigh while in the supine position is caused by muscle irritation. C-reactive protein levels will be increased after 12 hours if any infection is present.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: Parents have adopted a child with the diagnosis of kwashiorkor. What is most likely to be observed when assessing this child? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Kwashiorkor means, in native dialect, “the disease of the deposed baby when the next one is born,” indicating that the child no longer breastfeeds because a sibling is born and takes over the breast of the mother. Oral intake then is deficient in protein. The child fails to grow normally. The muscles become weak and wasted. There is edema of the abdomen that may become generalized. Diarrhea, skin infections, irritability, anorexia, and vomiting may be present. The hair becomes thin and dry. Because protein is the basis of melanin, a substance that provides color to hair, melanin becomes deficient. This is the reason the earliest sign of this protein malnutrition is a white streak in the hair of the child (depigmentation). The child looks apathetic and weak.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Gastrointestinal Condition
questions.stem: The nurse explains the medically accepted definition of constipation is fewer than bowel movements in a 2-week period.
questions.rationale: The medically accepted definition of constipation is fewer than seven bowel movements in a 2-week period.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Genitourinary Condition
questions.stem: The nurse discussed strategies with a parent to prevent a recurrence of urinary tract infection in the child. Which statement made by the parent indicates a need for further teaching?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “My daughter should wash and wipe the perineal area from front to back.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Iam only going to have my daughter wear cotton underwear.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Ttis acceptable to take frequent bubble baths.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “She needs to drink lots of fluids and void frequently.”

questions.rationale: Oils in bubble bath and similar products are known to irritate the urethra.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Genitourinary Condition
questions.stem: When asked about correcting the hypospadias of a newborn, what does the nurse explain about this condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No intervention is necessary as the defect will correct itself over time.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Surgical repair of the hypospadias is done before 18 months of age.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Corrective surgery is usually delayed until the preschool age.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Repairing the defect will increase the risk of testicular cancer.

questions.rationale: Treatment of hypospadias consists of surgical repair and is usually performed before 18 months of age.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Genitourinary Condition
questions.stem: What is an initial sign of nephrosis that the nurse might note in a child?
questions.rationale: The edema of nephrotic syndrome is generalized and not readily noticed, even by the parents, but an early sign that can be assessed is periorbital edema.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Genitourinary Condition
questions.stem: What is it important to assess in a child receiving prednisone to treat nephrotic syndrome?
questions.rationale: Prednisone depresses the immune response and increases susceptibility to infection. Because steroids mask signs of infection, the child must be assessed for more subtle symptoms of illness.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Genitourinary Condition
questions.stem: During a physical assessment of a hospitalized 5-year-old child, the nurse notes that the foreskin has been retracted and is very tight on the shaft of the penis; the nurse is unable to return it over the head of the penis. What action should the nurse implement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Forcibly push the foreskin down over the head of the penis.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Place a warm compress on the penis.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Wait a few hours and try again.

questions.rationale: Notify the charge nurse of this occurrence of paraphimosis. The tight foreskin can impede blood flow to the penis; this should be remedied immediately.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Genitourinary Condition
questions.stem: A7-year-old child with acute glomerulonephritis has gross hematuria and has been confined to bed. What is the most appropriate nursing intervention for this child?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Providing activities for the child on restricted activity

choices.label: B
choices.text: Feeding the child a protein-restricted diet

choices.label: D
choices.text: Observing the child for evidence of hypotension

questions.rationale: Although children may feel well, activity is limited until hematuria resolves.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Genitourinary Condition
questions.stem: Which urinary diversion procedure is the least damaging to the body image of the adolescent?
questions.rationale: The ileal conduit diverts urine to the colon, and the urine is excreted with the feces. There is no external appliance, as is needed with the other diversion methods.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Genitourinary Condition
questions.stem: The mother of a 5-year-old child taking prednisone for nephrotic syndrome tells the nurse he needs to get immunizations to enter kindergarten. What does the nurse clarify about receiving immunizations while on prednisone?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Can interfere with the treatment for nephrosis.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Require that the child have antibiotic coverage.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Can be given in smaller, divided doses.

questions.rationale: No vaccinations or immunizations should be administered while the disease is active and during immunosuppressive therapy.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Genitourinary Condition
questions.stem: Diuresis has not occurred on a child with nephrotic syndrome after a month on corticosteroids. What protocol can the nurse encourage to bring about diuresis?
questions.rationale: A potent antisuppressant such as Cytoxan can bring about diuresis when corticosteroids have proven ineffective.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Genitourinary Condition
questions.stem: What foods does the nurse recommend the child with acute glomerulonephritis avoid to prevent hyperkalemia?
questions.rationale: Bananas are very high in potassium and should be avoided.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Genitourinary Condition
questions.stem: Which physical assessment technique will the nurse omit when caring for a 2-year-old child diagnosed with Wilms‘ tumor?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Performing range-of-motion exercises on lower extremities

questions.rationale: Palpation of the abdomen could disturb the tumor and cause the malignancy to spread.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Genitourinary Condition
questions.stem: Parents are speaking with the urologist about their son‘s undescended testicle. Which statement by the child‘s father causes the nurse to determine he understands the information presented?

choices.label: B
choices.text: “The testicle usually descends spontaneously during the first month of life.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Surgical correction reduces the risk for testicular tumors.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “The optimal time to surgically correct the condition is at diagnosis.”

questions.rationale: Although orchiopexy improves the condition, the fertility rate among patients may be reduced even when only one testis is undescended.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Genitourinary Condition
questions.stem: A parent tells the nurse that her child is scheduled for an x-ray of the bladder and urethra that is done while the child is urinating. What is this test known as?
questions.rationale: An x-ray examination of the bladder and urethra before and during micturition is called a voiding cystourethrogram.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Genitourinary Condition
questions.stem: A 6-year-old child with daytime enuresis complains of dysuria and urgency. What does the nurse recognize these signs and symptoms indicate?
questions.rationale: Urinary frequency and pain during micturition are symptoms of acute urinary tract infection.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Genitourinary Condition
questions.stem: What is an appropriate intervention for the edematous child with reduced mobility related to nephrotic syndrome?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Reach the child to minimize body movements.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Keep the head of the child‘s bed flat.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Keep edematous areas moist and covered.

questions.rationale: The child should be turned frequently to prevent respiratory tract infection and to prevent pressure on delicate skin.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Genitourinary Condition
questions.stem: Which statement made by a parent of a child with nephrotic syndrome indicates an understanding of discharge teaching?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Twill make sure he gets his measles vaccine as soon as he gets home.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “He can stop taking his medication next week.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Tshould check his urine for protein when he goes to the bathroom.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “He should eat a low-protein diet for the next few weeks.”

questions.rationale: The parents should be instructed to keep a daily record of the child‘s urinary proteins.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Genitourinary Condition
questions.stem: A 5-year-old boy is admitted to the hospital with acute glomerulonephritis. In taking the child‘s history, what does the nurse recognize as the probable cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Recovery from German measles 2 months ago

questions.rationale: Acute glomerulonephritis develops from 1 to 3 weeks after a streptococcal infection, which causes an allergic-type response that alters the effectiveness of the glomeruli.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Genitourinary Condition
questions.stem: The nurse is explaining to a 17-year-old female the actions to prevent urinary tract infection. Which is the best beverage for the nurse to recommend to keep urine acidic?
questions.rationale: Juices such as apple or cranberry help maintain acidity of urine.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Genitourinary Condition
questions.stem: The 6-year-old child scheduled for an orchiopexy shyly asks the nurse, “What are they going to do to me _down there‘?” What is the nurse‘s best response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “They are going to fix you up _down there*.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “They will move your testicle from your abdomen to your scrotum.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “What do you think your doctor is going to do?”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “You shouldn‘t worry. Your doctor knows exactly what to do.”

questions.rationale: Encourage the patient to talk about what he knows and what feelings he has about the surgery. School-age children have a fear of bodily harm.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Genitourinary Condition
questions.stem: What will the nurse caution the parents of a child who has had a nephrectomy that he will have to avoid?
questions.rationale: Children who have only one kidney should avoid contact sports to prevent injury to that remaining organ.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Genitourinary Condition
questions.stem: The parents of a newborn are concerned that their son‘s scrotum is enlarged and swollen on one side. What is the nurse‘s best response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Tt is very common in the newborn that one gonad is larger than the other.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Birth trauma caused bruising to the scrotum. It will reduce in size in a few days.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Ttis a collection of fluid that will most likely correct itself in a year.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “The doctor will drain this collection of blood before your baby is discharged.”

questions.rationale: These signs are indicative of a hydrocele, a collection of fluid in the scrotum that usually corrects itself in a year.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Genitourinary Condition
questions.stem: The nurse is providing information to parents of a child born with bilateral cryptorchidism. What information is accurate to include?

choices.label: A
choices.text: This is the most common form.

choices.label: D
choices.text: An inguinal hernia may be present.

questions.rationale: When one or both testes fail to lower into the scrotum, the condition is termed cryptorchidism. The unilateral form is more common. Because the testes are warmer in the abdomen than in the scrotum, the sperm cells begin to deteriorate. If both testes are affected, sterility results. Inguinal hernia often accompanies this condition. Occasionally, a testis or the testes spontaneously descend during the first year of life. An operation called an orchiopexy may be performed.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Genitourinary Condition
questions.stem: An adolescent male is admitted to the ED with severe acute scrotal pain. When documenting medical history the nurse notes cryptorchidism at birth. What diagnosis does the nurse expect?
questions.rationale: When one or both testes fail to lower into the scrotum, the condition is termed cryptorchidism. Acute scrotal pain may indicate a testicular torsion (twisting), which necessitates immediate surgery to preserve testicular function.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Genitourinary Condition
questions.stem: A7-year-old child has a BUN of 25 mg/dL. What is the nurse aware this lab value might indicate? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Increased BUN can indicate dehydration, renal disease, and/or need for steroid therapy.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Genitourinary Condition
questions.stem: What will the nurse caring for a newborn with exstrophy of the bladder include in the care? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: The infant is kept on his back or side with special attention to the skin around the exposed bladder, which is constantly bathed with urine. These infants are diapered loosely, if at all. Surgical closure is done as quickly as possible.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Genitourinary Condition
questions.stem: The nurse caring for a child with nephrotic syndrome is alert to which classic symptoms of this disorder? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: All options listed are those of nephrotic syndrome with the exception of hyperalbuminemia. The nephrotic child has hypoalbuminemia, as most of the protein has been spilled in the urine.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Genitourinary Condition
questions.stem: The nurse is aware that genitourinary surgery is especially stressful for preschool children. What factor(s) lend to this stress? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: They may perceive the treatment as punishment.

choices.label: B
choices.text: They are especially prone to separation anxiety.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They are sexually curious and developmentally fixated on their genitals.

choices.label: D
choices.text: They have a fear of castration.

questions.rationale: All options, except fear of death, are especially stressful for preschool children undergoing genitourinary surgery. Children in this age group do not have an understanding of the concept of death.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Genitourinary Condition
questions.stem: What special considerations are related to long-term prednisone therapy in preschoolers? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Delayed immunization and greater risk for infection are concerns relative to long-term prednisone therapy.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Genitourinary Condition
questions.stem: The nurse is measuring output on an infant on the pediatric unit. When weighing the diaper and subtracting the weight of the dry diaper, the nurse records 30 g and documents this as mL.
questions.rationale: Diapers may be weighed on a gram scale before application and after removal (1 g= 1 mL).

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: The nurse is careful to apply only the prescribed amount of ointment to the skin of a 2-month-old infant. How is infant skin different from adult skin?
questions.rationale: The child‘s skin has a dramatically greater ability to absorb than does that of the adult.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: What risk is increased with children who have been diagnosed with infantile eczema?
questions.rationale: Some children with eczema also develop asthma and hay fever—type allergies.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: What is the appropriate technique for the application of a topical treatment for a child with eczema?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Apply skin lotions in a circular motion.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Apply prescribed ointments with a gloved hand.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Apply as much and as frequently as relieves the symptoms.

questions.rationale: The prescribed amount of ointment is usually applied to the skin by a gloved hand in long, smooth strokes. Lanolin-based preparations should be avoided because of a possible allergy to wool.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: A 2-day-old infant is noted to have small pustules on her skin. What is the best nursing action?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Report it immediately because it may be a staphylococcus infection.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Keep the affected area dry and clean.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Teach the parents how to care for seborrheic dermatitis.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Chart the finding because it may be the beginning of a strawberry nevus.

questions.rationale: A staphylococcal infection can spread readily from one infant to another. Small pustules on the newborn must be reported immediately.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: The home health nurse discovers a family infected with pediculosis. What information can the nurse provide to the mother to start eradication of the lice?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Apply a soda—vinegar solution to the hair.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Comb through the hair with a vinegar—water solution.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Shampoo the hair with dish detergent.

questions.rationale: Combing a vinegar—water solution through the hair with a fine-tooth comb and then shampooing is an initial step toward eradication.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: A group of football players is taking oral griseofulvin for tinea pedis. What should the school nurse caution them to avoid?
questions.rationale: Consumption of alcohol while taking griseofulvin will cause severe tachycardia.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: What should the nurse suggest before a 17-year-old girl starts a protocol of isotretinoin (Accutane) for her acne?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increase the dose of the present medication.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Limit intake of chocolate, cola, and peanuts.

questions.rationale: Oral contraceptives are often prescribed for adolescents with acne. Accutane can cause birth defects, so pregnancy should be prevented.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: A child had a burn, evidenced by pink skin and blistering. The child complains of pain and is crying. How does the nurse classify this burn when documenting?
questions.rationale: A second-degree superficial burn appears blistered, moist, and pink or red. The pain associated with this burn indicates tissue viability.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: A child has sustained a second-degree deep thermal burn to the hand. What is the best first action to take?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Immerse the burned area in cold water.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Apply ice to the burned area.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Break any blisters that are present.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Apply petroleum jelly to the burned skin.

questions.rationale: First aid treatment of a second-degree deep thermal burn is immersion of the burned area in water to halt the burning process.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: Which allergy would contraindicate the use of silver sulfadiazine (Silvadene) as a topical agent for burns?
questions.rationale: The use of Silvadene cream on burns is contraindicated if the patient has a sulfa allergy.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: What would help the child with a serious burn meet nutritional needs during the subacute phase of recovery?

choices.label: A
