choices.text: Decrease calories because the child will be on bed rest and will not need as many.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increase calories and protein to compensate for the healing process.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increase fat to replace the layer of fat next to the burned skin.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Decrease carbohydrates and starches because the pancreas is strained by the healing process.

questions.rationale: Frequent meals and snacks high in calories, protein, and iron are needed to meet the increased metabolic needs of the child with burns.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: Which statement made by a parent indicates an understanding of the topical application of medications for a skin condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Tapply the medication after I give my child a bath.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Trub the ointment in a circular motion over the rash.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Tincreased the amount of cream because the rash was not improving.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Tuse powder and cornstarch to keep the skin dry.”

questions.rationale: Absorption of topical medications is best when preparations are applied after a warm bath.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: On the first day following a severe burn, the body‘s fluid reserves have left the circulating volume and entered the interstitial space, causing massive edema. What should the nurse monitor for very closely in the burn victim?
questions.rationale: With the fluid shift associated with severe burns, the nurse must be observant for the reduction of urine, an indication of altered renal function.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: Ata 2-month well-child visit, parents ask the nurse about the red area on the infant‘s neck. They tell the nurse that the mark appeared a few weeks after birth. What does the nurse recognize this skin lesion as?
questions.rationale: The strawberry nevus is a common hemangioma consisting of dilated capillaries in the dermal space, which may not become apparent for a few weeks after birth.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: A mother is concerned about what might have caused a heat rash on her infant. The nurse observes tiny pinhead-sized reddened papules on the infant‘s neck and axilla. What does the nurse explain as the most likely cause of this rash?
questions.rationale: Miliaria, or prickly heat rash, is caused by excess body heat and moisture.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: What is the correct nursing response to a mother who asks, “How can I get rid of the baby‘s cradle cap?”

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Rub baby oil on the infant‘s head at night and shampoo the hair the next morning.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Use a brush with firm bristles to loosen the scales on the baby‘s head several times a day.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Wash the baby‘s head every night with a dandruff-control shampoo.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Lubricate the baby‘s head every morning with a small amount of olive oil.”

questions.rationale: Scales may be softened by applying baby oil to the head the evening before, and shampooing the hair in the morning.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: Which statement made by a parent indicates the need for further teaching about strategies to control itching for the infant with eczema?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Wool is the best fabric for the infant‘s clothing.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “T put cotton gloves on the infant‘s hands.”

questions.rationale: Clothing should be made of cotton. Wool is avoided because of its allergy potential.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: What will the nurse include when teaching about general skin care measures that could help prevent acne?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Eliminating chocolate, peanuts, and cola from the diet

choices.label: B
choices.text: Washing the face with a cleansing product frequently

choices.label: C
choices.text: Planning indoor activities to avoid sun exposure

choices.label: D
choices.text: Eating a balanced diet and getting sufficient rest

questions.rationale: General hygienic measures of cleanliness, rest, and avoidance of emotional stress may help prevent exacerbations.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: The nurse caring for a patient with severe frostbite observes a purple flush on the hands and feet. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Place a warm towel over the extremities.

questions.rationale: A purple flush indicates the return of sensation and causes extreme pain.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: A child is brought to the emergency department with burns on the face and chest. What is the nurse‘s first priority?
questions.rationale: Airway assessment and establishing an airway are the initial priorities.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: An adolescent girl with acne is being treated with an antibiotic in addition to topical applications. What side effect does the nurse caution the girl to expect?
questions.rationale: Antibiotic therapy can cause a monilial vaginitis.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: The nurse observes a tarry stool from a 16-year-old burn victim who has been in the ICU for 2 weeks. Which complication does the nurse anticipate?
questions.rationale: Curling‘s ulcer is a complication of burn victims resulting from the stress of their trauma.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: A child is brought to the emergency department with severe frostbite. Which body parts should be warmed first?
questions.rationale: In extreme cases of exposure to freezing temperatures, the head and torso should be warmed before the extremities.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: An adolescent is at the pediatrician‘s office because he has been experiencing intense itching, particularly in the axilla and between the fingers. The itching is worse during the night and he has not been sleeping well. With what is this symptom associated?
questions.rationale: Intense itching, especially at night, is characteristic of scabies. Distribution of this document is illegal extra per year? ius

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: What should the nurse stress to the mother of a child with impetigo?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The condition is caused by the herpes simplex virus type I.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The crusts on the lesions should be left in place.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The lesions may spread, but the disease is not contagious.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Small cuts and bites should be treated promptly.

questions.rationale: Small cuts and bites should be treated promptly to prevent the invasions of the bacteria that cause impetigo. The crusts from the lesions should be gently removed. The disease is contagious.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: The nurse is caring for a 3-year-old child with severe burns. What is the nurse aware is the minimum adequate hourly urine output?
questions.rationale: The minimum acceptable hourly urine output for children over the age of 2 years is 20 to 30 mL/hr.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: An adolescent patient at a pediatric clinic presents with a butterfly rash. What diagnosis does the nurse suspect?
questions.rationale: Butterfly rash over the nose and cheeks can be associated with photosensitivity and may be associated with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: The nurse is documenting a description of a skin assessment. What term can be used for an elevated, fluid-filled blister?
questions.rationale: A vesicle is an elevated, fluid-filled blister (cold sore, chicken pox).

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: What should the nurse keep in mind when providing care to the school-age child hospitalized with a burn injury?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Analgesics should be given immediately after dressing changes.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Contact with peers should be maintained.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Parents usually handle injury worse than the child.

questions.rationale: A burn injury is taxing to the child and parents. It requires long periods of hospitalization and frequent readmissions. The accident itself is terrifying for the child but is made even worse if caused by disobedience. Nurses encourage children to express their feelings. Analgesics are administered before painful procedures. The long-term patient requires diversions of various types. School tutors are requested, and contact is maintained with peers through cards or e-mail.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: Parents of a child show the nurse that their child has a flat strawberry nevus. What information can the nurse provide in educating the parents regarding strawberry nevus? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is a rare skin variation.

questions.rationale: The strawberry nevus is a common hemangioma (consists of dilated capillaries in the dermal space) that may not become apparent for a few weeks after birth. Although it is harmless and usually disappears without treatment, it is disturbing to parents, especially when it appears on the head or face. At first it is flat, but it gradually becomes raised. The lesions gradually blanch, with 60% disappearing spontaneously by 5 years of age and 90% disappearing by 9 years of age. Laser treatment or excision may be considered if the area becomes ulcerated.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: What would the nurse teach parents to do in order to avoid diaper rash? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Keep perineum covered at all times.

questions.rationale: Keeping the skin dry and protected with emollients, leaving the area exposed to light and air periodically, changing the diaper frequently, and avoiding plastic pants will prevent diaper rash.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: The nurse speaking to a group of junior high school students informs them that acne can be exacerbated by which drug(s)? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Long-term use of steroids, phenytoin, phenobarbital, lithium, and vitamin Bj2 can cause acne.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: What intervention(s) would the nurse preparing a teaching plan for the care of a child with infantile eczema include? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bathe the child using products with a light fragrance.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use oatmeal and baking soda as bath additives.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Add bath oil to bath water after the child has soaked.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Apply lanolin-based lotions after the bath.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Bathe child several times a day.

questions.rationale: Use of oatmeal, baking soda, and baking powder is soothing. Adding oil to the bath water after the child has soaked for a while makes the oil application more effective. Items with any fragrance should be avoided as well as lanolin-based products. Many dermatologists advise minimal bathing.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: Which factor(s) activate the herpes simplex virus type I? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: The herpes simplex virus type I can be activated to cause a cold sore by exposure to stress, sun, initiation of menses, and fever. Food allergies do not activate the virus as a rule.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: A 5-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department with a second-degree burn of his entire right arm and hand, anterior trunk and genital area, and front of right thigh. The nurse assesses the total body surface area (TBSA) percentage burn as %.
questions.rationale: Using the Burn Size Estimation Table on page 695, the nurse can determine that for a 5-year-old child, the upper and lower arm = 5.5%, the hand = 2.5%, anterior trunk = 13%, genital area = 1%, and half of the thigh = 4%. Together this totals to 26% BSA burn.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Skin Condition
questions.stem: The nurse assesses a major burn as a full-thickness burn involving % or more of the body surface.
questions.rationale: A full-thickness burn involving 10% or more of the body surface is considered a major burn.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: A nurse is planning to teach a family about Tay-Sachs disease. What will the nurse relay about the pattern of inheritance for inborn errors of metabolism?
questions.rationale: A: The pattern of inheritance is generally autosomal recessive.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: What occurs as a result of an inadequate secretion of insulin?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increased fat breakdown leads to ketonemia.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Serum glucose levels are markedly decreased.

choices.label: D
choices.text: More rapid conversion and storage of carbohydrates to glucose occurs.

questions.rationale: When insulin is deficient, the body cannot metabolize carbohydrates for energy. The body is also unable to store and use fat properly. Incomplete fat metabolism produces ketone bodies that accumulate in the blood.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: On what understanding does the nurse plan the care of a child with a new diagnosis of type 1 diabetes mellitus?

choices.label: A
choices.text: There is an absolute deficiency of insulin.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Insufficient quantities of insulin are produced by the pancreas.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oral hypoglycemic agents can control it.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Insulin deficiency is caused by another disease affecting the pancreas.

questions.rationale: Type 1 insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus is characterized by an absolute or complete deficiency of insulin.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: Acchild receives a combination of regular and NPH insulin at 8:00 AM. At 8:45 AM the breakfast trays have not yet arrived from the kitchen. What is the best action by the nurse?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Give the patient a snack of graham crackers and milk.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ambulate the patient in the hall for a short time.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Give the patient more insulin according to the sliding scale.

questions.rationale: A child who receives regular insulin before meals may have an insulin reaction if food is not eaten within 20 minutes. A snack of graham crackers and milk will prevent an episode of hypoglycemia.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: Although the child with type 1 diabetes had her prescribed insulin at 7:30 AM, the child is complaining of hunger and thirst and is drowsy at 10:30 AM. What should the nurse do first?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Walk the patient in the hall for 10 minutes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Allow the patient a short nap.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Give her a cup of orange juice.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Test her blood with a glucometer and give insulin according to the sliding scale.

questions.rationale: The immediate remedy is to give orange juice to raise the blood glucose. Giving more sugar will increase the blood glucose in a hyperglycemic child. Walking exercise will use up even more glucose. The treatment for hyperglycemia is to give the patient more insulin.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: Which comment made by a school-age child indicates that he needs more teaching about diabetes mellitus and exercise?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Tcarry a piece of hard candy with me in case I start to feel shaky.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Imake sure I have emergency money when I have soccer practice or a game.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Sometimes I skip my breakfast when I have a game in the morning.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Iplay in soccer games that are scheduled after dinner.”

questions.rationale: Blood glucose is high after meals. The child with type 1 diabetes mellitus who skips a meal before exercise is at risk for hypoglycemia.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: Which statement made by a 7-year-old child with type 1 diabetes mellitus indicates a need for more teaching?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “My pancreas is sick and needs insulin until it is well.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “I will need to take my insulin every day.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “TIneed to keep a piece of candy in my pocket in case I start to feel shaky.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “My mom has to give me insulin shots twice a day.”

questions.rationale: The child with type 1 diabetes mellitus has an insulin deficiency and will require lifelong management of this disease. Insulin does not cure the pancreas.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: Which general dietary measure should the nurse include in a teaching plan for the child with type 1 diabetes mellitus?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Control intake of carbohydrates and consume fewer calories.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Focus on complex carbohydrates and eat foods high in fiber.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Obtain most calories from proteins and fats.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Eat a diet low in fat and low in complex carbohydrates.

questions.rationale: The nutritional needs of a child with diabetes mellitus are essentially the same as those of the nondiabetic child, with the exception of the elimination of concentrated carbohydrates such as sugar. Fiber has been shown to reduce blood glucose levels.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: Acchild with diabetes is brought to the emergency department. He is flushed and drowsy, and his skin is dry. His father states that the child has been feeling progressively worse since the morning. What is this child most likely experiencing?
questions.rationale: In ketoacidosis, the child‘s skin is dry, and the face is flushed. Patients appear dehydrated. They may perspire and be restless. The breath has a fruity odor, and there is no rest period between inspiration and expiration.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: A mother reports that her 4-month-old infant is lethargic, sleeps 18 hours a day, and snores. The nurse recognizes these signs are characteristic of what?
questions.rationale: The infant with hypothyroidism will appear sluggish, and the tongue will be enlarged, causing noisy respiration.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: What is an important consideration for the school-age child taking DDAVP for diabetes insipidus?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Observe for signs of water deprivation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Arrange for the child to use the bathroom when needed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Limit fluid intake other than during the lunch period.

questions.rationale: The child with diabetes insipidus needs liberal access to bathrooms and water fountains. Arrangements may have to be made with the school to allow access.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: What condition does the nurse suspect when a child with type 1 diabetes mellitus has hyperglycemia, diaphoresis, and headaches in the morning?
questions.rationale: The Somogyi phenomenon (rebound hyperglycemia) occurs when the blood glucose level is lowered to the point at which the body‘s counter-regulatory hormones are released, producing the symptoms described.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: What would be the most appropriate nursing response to a woman who says, “My sister had a child with Tay-Sachs disease, and I want to know if I could have a child with this condition”?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “The disease is rare. It is unlikely that you would have a child with Tay-Sachs disease.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “A screening test can be done to determine if you are a carrier of the gene.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “The gene for Tay-Sachs disease is transmitted by the father.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “The cause of Tay-Sachs disease is thought to be an autoimmune response to a virus.”

questions.rationale: Carriers can be identified by screening tests. Tay-Sachs disease has an autosomal recessive pattern of transmission.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: What statement by a parent leads the nurse to determine a parent is administering levothyroxine (Synthroid) correctly?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “TIstopped giving the medication because my daughter was losing her hair.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Iam using a different brand now because it costs less money.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Tdon‘t give the medication on the weekends.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “I give the medication at 8:00 AM every day.”

questions.rationale: Synthroid should be given at the same time each day, preferably in the morning.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: After a closed head injury, the unconscious 10-year-old child begins to excrete copious amounts of pale urine with an attendant drop in blood pressure (BP). Based on these symptoms, what does the nurse suspect has developed?
questions.rationale: Diabetes insipidus can be acquired as the result of a head injury or tumor, and suppression of the posterior pituitary causes copious urine output with an attendant drop in BP. The child can become dehydrated very quickly if some remedy is not applied.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: The nurse is teaching the parents of a child with diabetes insipidus about water intoxication. The nurse would tell the parents to be alert for what symptom?
questions.rationale: Signs of water intoxication include edema, lethargy, nausea, and central nervous system signs.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: The parents of a child newly diagnosed with diabetes mellitus tell the nurse, “Our son‘s body is resistant to insulin.” With what does the nurse recognize this description is consistent?
questions.rationale: Type 2, non—insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus is caused by insulin resistance or failure of the body to use the insulin.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: What does the nurse instruct a 12-year-old to do when teaching how to administer insulin?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Make sure injection sites are 6 inches apart.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Select an injection site that was recently exercised.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inject the needle at a 90-degree angle.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Give the injection deep into the muscle.

questions.rationale: Children often find it easier to learn to inject the needle at a 90-degree angle.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: The nurse discussed treatment of hypoglycemia with an adolescent. Which statement by the adolescent leads the nurse to determine the patient understood the instructions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “When my blood glucose is low or if I begin to feel hungry and weak, I will eat six LifeSavers.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “When my blood glucose is low or if I begin to feel hungry and weak, I will give myself Lispro insulin.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “When my blood glucose is low or if I begin to feel hungry and weak, I will have a slice of cheese.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “When my blood glucose is low or if I begin to feel hungry and weak, I will drink a diet soda.”

questions.rationale: The immediate treatment of hypoglycemia consists of administering sugar in some form such as orange juice, hard candy, or a commercial product. Cheese will eventually raise the blood glucose, but not as quickly as candy.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: Why does the nurse instruct an 11-year-old diabetic child to use the side of the finger for blood testing?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Itis less likely to become infected.

questions.rationale: The sides of the finger have fewer nerve endings and more capillaries but are not easier to puncture than the fingertip. The risk for infection is remote for either site.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: What is the function of an insulin pump?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Releases insulin as blood glucose rises.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Decreases need for painful glucose monitoring.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Delivers a prescribed amount of insulin twice a day.

questions.rationale: The insulin pump that is attached to a subcutaneous tube releases a continuous infusion of insulin.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: The nurse is preparing to administer a long-acting insulin. Which insulin is considered long acting?
questions.rationale: Insulin glargine is a long-acting insulin. Regular is short acting. Lispro and Aspart are rapid acting.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: When discussing possible causes of diabetes in children, the nurse mentions chromosomal defects. Which chromosomes are associated with diabetes? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Defects in chromosomes 6, 7, 12, and 20 and other genetic disorders are associated with diabetes mellitus syndrome.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: Which food sources are high in soluble fiber? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Foods high in soluble fiber include raw fruits, beans, and bran cereal.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: What does the nurse remind the adolescent with diabetes that soluble fiber in the diet can reduce? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Soluble fiber can reduce blood glucose, serum cholesterol, absorption of sugar, and insulin requirements. It has no effect on infections.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: Which process(es) does the nurse explain the endocrine system is primarily responsible for controlling? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: The endocrine system governs maturation, reproduction, stress response, and sexual maturity. Sexual identity is a psychosocial response.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: The home health nurse is monitoring an 8-month-old child with hypothyroidism taking levothyroxine (Synthroid). Which symptoms does the nurse recognize as signs of overdose? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: All the options with the exception of weight gain and vomiting are indications of overdose of Synthroid. Weight loss is a symptom of overdose, however.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: What makes keeping diabetes in control in an adolescent difficult? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: The adolescent who is in a growth spurt and filled with raging hormones resents and denies the need to be dependent on a medication. Medication schedules and diet restrictions do not correlate well with the adolescent's lifestyle of eating fast foods. Denial of disease is prevalent in the adolescent.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: Acchild with diabetes mellitus is observed to have cold symptoms. What signs and symptoms will alert parents of the possibility of ketoacidosis? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Symptoms of ketoacidosis are compared with those of hypoglycemia. Signs and symptoms include a fruity odor to the breath, nausea, decreased level of consciousness and dehydration. Lab values include ketonuria, decreased serum bicarbonate concentration (decreased CO levels) and low pH, and hypertonic dehydration.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: The nurse is discussing insulin shock with parents of a child recently diagnosed with diabetes mellitus. What will the nurse respond when the parents ask why children are more prone to insulin reactions? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: “The condition is more unstable in children.”

questions.rationale: Children are more prone to insulin reactions than adults because of the following: the condition itself is more unstable in young people; they are growing; their activities are more irregular.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: The nurse reminds the parents of a diabetic with an insulin pump that the tubing of the pump should be changed aseptically every. hours.
questions.rationale: The tubing of the insulin pump should be changed every 48 hours.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: The nurse explains that the diagnosis of diabetes is made when the fasting blood glucose level is mg/dL on two separate occasions, and the history is positive for indication of the disease.
questions.rationale: An elevated blood glucose level of 126 mg/dL on two separate occasions is grounds for the diagnosis of diabetes mellitus when the history is positive for the disease.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with a Metabolic Condition
questions.stem: The nurse assessing a glycosylated hemoglobin (HbAi.) test is aware that this test can evaluate average glucose levels over a period of to months.
questions.rationale: 3,4 3to4 three, four three; four three to four Glucose attaches to the red cells over the life span of the cell and can be read as percentages. An HbA; reading of 6% to 9% is normal; a reading of 12% or higher is indicative of DM.

questions.chapter_title: Childhood Communicable Diseases, Bioterrorism, Natural Disasters, and the Maternal-Child Patient
questions.stem: Which classification of medication would make a child most susceptible to an opportunistic infection?
questions.rationale: Steroids are immunosuppressive drugs that make the child very susceptible to opportunistic infections.

questions.chapter_title: Childhood Communicable Diseases, Bioterrorism, Natural Disasters, and the Maternal-Child Patient
questions.stem: An 8-year-old child asks the nurse how she got the antibodies that kept her from getting whooping cough. What is the nurse‘s best explanation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “You received borrowed antibodies from another person who had whooping cough.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “You were given a tiny case of whooping cough and then you made your own antibodies.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “An immunization strengthened antibodies you were born with.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “You received only temporary borrowed antibodies and you need to have another shot every 5 years.”

questions.rationale: Vaccines contain live weakened or dead organisms not strong enough to cause disease but they stimulate the body to develop an immune reaction and antibodies. This is active acquired immunity.

questions.chapter_title: Childhood Communicable Diseases, Bioterrorism, Natural Disasters, and the Maternal-Child Patient
questions.stem: How would the nurse document a rash that has erythematous, circular raised lesions?
questions.rationale: A papule is a circular, reddened elevated area on the skin.

questions.chapter_title: Childhood Communicable Diseases, Bioterrorism, Natural Disasters, and the Maternal-Child Patient
questions.stem: Which finding would lead the nurse to delay the administration of DTaP for an infant?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Temperature of 40.5°C (105°F) from the previous inoculation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Traveling to Europe in a week

questions.rationale: A contraindication to giving the DTaP vaccine is a 40.5°C (105°F) temperature following the previous vaccination.

questions.chapter_title: Childhood Communicable Diseases, Bioterrorism, Natural Disasters, and the Maternal-Child Patient
questions.stem: What type of precautions are necessary when caring for a toddler with varicella?
questions.rationale: Airborne-infection precautions are used for patients with conditions such as tuberculosis, varicella, and rubella. Small airborne particles caught on floating dust in the room can be inhaled from anywhere in the room.

questions.chapter_title: Childhood Communicable Diseases, Bioterrorism, Natural Disasters, and the Maternal-Child Patient
questions.stem: Which statement assures the nurse that parents understand how long a child who has varicella is contagious?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “My child should stay home from school for 6 days after the pox appear.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “My child can return to school when the rash fades.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “My child must stay away from other children until all of the lesions have healed.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “My child is contagious as long as he has a fever.”

questions.rationale: The child with varicella is contagious for 6 days after the appearance of the rash.

questions.chapter_title: Childhood Communicable Diseases, Bioterrorism, Natural Disasters, and the Maternal-Child Patient
questions.stem: Which statement made by a sexually active adolescent girl indicates an understanding of the prevention of sexually transmitted diseases?

choices.label: B
choices.text: “I think you can get a vaccination for STDs now.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Tinsist that my partner wear a condom.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Iam protected because I take the pill.”

questions.rationale: The use of condoms to prevent STDs is not considered 100% effective but is recommended for sexual intercourse.

questions.chapter_title: Childhood Communicable Diseases, Bioterrorism, Natural Disasters, and the Maternal-Child Patient
questions.stem: What is the priority nursing diagnosis for a hospitalized infant who is HIV positive?
questions.rationale: The infant who is HIV positive has impaired immunologic functioning and is at high risk for infection.

questions.chapter_title: Childhood Communicable Diseases, Bioterrorism, Natural Disasters, and the Maternal-Child Patient
questions.stem: The mother of a newborn asked the nurse, “When will my baby get the hepatitis B vaccine?” When will the nurse explain the first dose of Comvax should be given to infants born to a hepatitis B-positive mother?
questions.rationale: The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends that Comvax, the only thimerosal-free hepatitis B vaccine, should be used for infants born to HBsAg-positive mothers within 12 hours of birth.

questions.chapter_title: Childhood Communicable Diseases, Bioterrorism, Natural Disasters, and the Maternal-Child Patient
questions.stem: A 10-year-old child is diagnosed with hepatitis A. What is the most likely way the child contracted this disease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Came in contact with infected blood.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Came in contact with droplets in the air.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Was bitten by a mosquito or a tick.

questions.rationale: Hepatitis A results from ingestion of contaminated water or shellfish.

questions.chapter_title: Childhood Communicable Diseases, Bioterrorism, Natural Disasters, and the Maternal-Child Patient
questions.stem: An infant is hospitalized for RSV bronchiolitis. Which type of precautions would the nurse use when caring for the infant?
questions.rationale: Contact precautions are used when the condition transmits organisms via skin-to-skin contact or indirect touch of a contaminated fomite.

questions.chapter_title: Childhood Communicable Diseases, Bioterrorism, Natural Disasters, and the Maternal-Child Patient
questions.stem: A 9-year-old child hospitalized for neutropenia is placed in protective isolation. What is the most appropriate response for the nurse to make when the child asks, “Why do you have to wear a gown and mask when you are in my room?”

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Nurses and doctors wear gowns and masks because you have a condition that could be spread to others.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “The gown and mask are to protect you because you could get an infection very easily.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “I‘m wearing this because there are a lot of bacteria in the hospital.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “I might look scary but you won‘t need this after you have had medication for 24 hours.”

questions.rationale: Protective isolation is used for patients who are not communicable but have a lowered resistance and are highly susceptible to infection.

questions.chapter_title: Childhood Communicable Diseases, Bioterrorism, Natural Disasters, and the Maternal-Child Patient
questions.stem: The nurse is planning to administer immunizations at a well-child visit when a parent reports the 18-month-old child is allergic to eggs. Which vaccine would be contraindicated?
questions.rationale: The influenza vaccine should not be given to children who are allergic to eggs.

questions.chapter_title: Childhood Communicable Diseases, Bioterrorism, Natural Disasters, and the Maternal-Child Patient
questions.stem: The nurse is preparing to administer immunizations at a well-child clinic. Which method of administration will the nurse implement?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hib vaccine prepared in a separate syringe

choices.label: D
choices.text: Varicella 1 week after the MMR vaccine

questions.rationale: Hib vaccine must be given in a separate syringe from other vaccines administered at the same time.

questions.chapter_title: Childhood Communicable Diseases, Bioterrorism, Natural Disasters, and the Maternal-Child Patient
questions.stem: A child was sent to the school nurse because of a rash. The nurse noted the rash was present on the trunk, extremities, and face. The child‘s cheeks were bright red. With what is the nurse aware this type of rash is consistent?
questions.rationale: In fifth disease, the child has a generalized rash and the cheeks have a slapped-cheek appearance.

questions.chapter_title: Childhood Communicable Diseases, Bioterrorism, Natural Disasters, and the Maternal-Child Patient
questions.stem: What statement leads the nurse to determine that a child‘s parent understands information related to tick bites?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “T‘ll have my son wear dark clothing on his hike.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “We should all get the Lyme disease vaccine before our trip.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “T‘ll get a prescription for amoxicillin to take with us.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “We will wear long pants and long-sleeved shirts in the woods.”

questions.rationale: People should keep skin covered by wearing protective clothing in wooded areas to prevent tick bites.

questions.chapter_title: Childhood Communicable Diseases, Bioterrorism, Natural Disasters, and the Maternal-Child Patient
questions.stem: An adolescent is taking tetracycline for a sexually transmitted disease. What would the nurse stress when providing instruction about this medication?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Get plenty of fresh air and sunlight.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Take an antacid if the medication causes an upset stomach.

questions.rationale: The nurse would teach the adolescent to take all of the prescribed medication to avoid making the microorganism resistant to tetracyclines.

questions.chapter_title: Childhood Communicable Diseases, Bioterrorism, Natural Disasters, and the Maternal-Child Patient
questions.stem: The nurse explains to the parents that their child is in the prodromal stage of varicella. What does this mean?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The child is now immune to varicella.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The child has varicella but has not yet broken out.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The child is infected with varicella but is not contagious.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The child does not have varicella but has been exposed to it.

questions.rationale: The prodromal stage is the initial stage of the communicable disease in which the child is infected and contagious but does not yet have outward signs of the disease.

questions.chapter_title: Childhood Communicable Diseases, Bioterrorism, Natural Disasters, and the Maternal-Child Patient
questions.stem: Which is an example of an opportunistic infection?
questions.rationale: Pneumocystis jiroveci is the most common of opportunistic diseases.

questions.chapter_title: Childhood Communicable Diseases, Bioterrorism, Natural Disasters, and the Maternal-Child Patient
questions.stem: A child is admitted to the pediatric unit with a diagnosis of cellulitis on the right upper thigh. Patient history reveals the child had a 2-cm laceration on the right thigh prior to infection. When explaining the chain of infection, how does the nurse identify this laceration?
questions.rationale: The chain of infection refers to the way in which organisms spread and infect the individual. A portal of entry is a route by which the organisms enter the body (e.g., a cut in the skin). A portal of exit is the route by which the organisms exit the body (e.g., feces or urine). A reservoir for infection is a place that supports the growth of organisms (e.g., standing, stagnant water). A vector is an insect or animal that carries and spreads a disease.

questions.chapter_title: Childhood Communicable Diseases, Bioterrorism, Natural Disasters, and the Maternal-Child Patient
questions.stem: What are the most likely reasons a female adolescent with STDs resist reporting the condition? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: She is reluctant to name contacts.

choices.label: D
choices.text: She doesn‘t want to take the medication.

questions.rationale: Adolescents are uncomfortable about the pelvic examination and require a lot of support. Adolescents doubt the confidentiality of the agency and are reluctant to name contacts.

questions.chapter_title: Childhood Communicable Diseases, Bioterrorism, Natural Disasters, and the Maternal-Child Patient
questions.stem: What sources are examples of acquired immunity? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Acquired immunity is acquiring the antibodies by way of having the disease or having the vaccination. Gamma globulin is simply a support to the immune system. Immune globulin is receiving the antibodies from some other source, giving the person an immediate immunity but one that does not last. Acquired Immunity

questions.chapter_title: Childhood Communicable Diseases, Bioterrorism, Natural Disasters, and the Maternal-Child Patient
questions.stem: The well-child clinic nurse is preparing to give which immunizations to a healthy 2-month-old infant? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: All the options are the expected inoculations of a healthy 2-month-old with the exception of MMR. Mumps, measles, and rubella are not expected until the child is 1-year old.

questions.chapter_title: Childhood Communicable Diseases, Bioterrorism, Natural Disasters, and the Maternal-Child Patient
questions.stem: The nurse is explaining to a family about disaster preparedness. What will the nurse instruct the family to prepare in a disaster kit in case of emergency? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: The nurse can assist families to prepare for natural disasters, such as hurricanes or floods, or man-made disasters, such as bioterrorist attacks or bombings. The American Medical Association (AMA) office guidelines for preparing a family and community disaster plan state that the family should keep several days‘ supply of food, water, pet food, warm clothing, blankets, copies of vital documents, and toiletries on hand. A battery-powered radio and extra medications, eyeglasses, and basic first aid supplies are also essential.

questions.chapter_title: Childhood Communicable Diseases, Bioterrorism, Natural Disasters, and the Maternal-Child Patient
questions.stem: The nurse is assisting with an admission assessment of a child with scarlet fever. Which actions will the nurse expect to implement? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: A diagnosis of scarlet fever would indicate throat culture and assessment for desquamation. Bed rest with quiet activity is indicated. Droplet precautions would not be implemented for scarlet fever. Isoniazid is administered for tuberculosis.

questions.chapter_title: Childhood Communicable Diseases, Bioterrorism, Natural Disasters, and the Maternal-Child Patient
questions.stem: A parent is concerned because her son was exposed to varicella at preschool. The nurse would tell this parent that the incubation period for varicella is 14 to. days.
questions.rationale: The incubation period for varicella is 2 to 3 weeks, usually 13 to 17 days.

questions.chapter_title: Childhood Communicable Diseases, Bioterrorism, Natural Disasters, and the Maternal-Child Patient
questions.stem: The nurse demonstrates proper hand hygiene pointing out that the process should take a minimum of. seconds.
questions.rationale: Hand hygiene should take a minimum of 15 seconds to complete.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with an Emotional or Behavioral Condition
questions.stem: A parent asks the nurse to describe what is meant by a “learning disability.” Which is the nurse‘s most helpful response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “A child may have difficulty with perception, language, comprehension, or memory.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “It is characterized by inattention, impulsiveness, and hyperactivity.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “The child‘s intellectual ability limits his learning.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “The child has difficulty learning because of brain damage.”

questions.rationale: Learning disability is an educational term. Children with learning disabilities may have average to above-average intelligence, but they may experience difficulties in perception, language, comprehension, and conceptualization.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with an Emotional or Behavioral Condition
questions.stem: What would be the appropriate response to an adolescent who states, “This has been the worst day of my life?”

choices.label: A
choices.text: “You should focus your mind on positive thoughts.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “Everybody has a bad day now and then.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “You‘re young. What could be so terrible?”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “Tell me about the worst day of your life.”

questions.rationale: The nurse establishes a rapport with the adolescent by acknowledging his or her feelings and giving the adolescent full attention.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with an Emotional or Behavioral Condition
questions.stem: The nurse asks, “Do your parents drink every day?” The adolescent suddenly shouts, “I‘m not going to talk about that! It‘s none of your business, anyway! Leave me alone!” How does the nurse interpret the adolescent‘s behavior?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The adolescent is acting out and needs to be brought under control so the conference can continue.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The adolescent is trying to shift the focus of the conference away from himself, and the nurse needs to refocus.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The adolescent is demonstrating that this problem requires the assistance of a psychiatrist.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The adolescent is responding to the discrediting of his parents, which causes anxiety.

questions.rationale: Discrediting parents threatens the child‘s security and creates anxiety.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with an Emotional or Behavioral Condition
questions.stem: The nurse is answering phone calls at a local suicide prevention hotline. Which statement would be recognized as the greatest risk of suicide?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Tjust needed to talk to someone to keep myself from thinking silly thoughts about killing myself.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “My parents aren‘t home and won‘t be back for 4 hours. That should be enough time for the pills to work. I‘ve got a hundred of them.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “My dad will be home first, so he‘ll find me. So I think I‘ll use his gun. I hope he didn‘t lock the cabinet.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “My girlfriend is here with me. She told me to call because I was talking crazy about killing myself.”

questions.rationale: The risk of death increases when there is a definite plan of action, the means are readily available, and the person has few resources for help and support.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with an Emotional or Behavioral Condition
questions.stem: A 15-year-old boy was previously active in a band and saved money to buy a special guitar. What would a nurse assess as an early sign of depression in this boy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: He gives up the band to spend time with his girlfriend.

choices.label: B
choices.text: He spends all of his time at the library studying to qualify for the honor society.

choices.label: C
choices.text: He gives his guitar away and spends his time listening to music in his room.

choices.label: D
choices.text: He withdraws all of his money out of the bank to buy an expensive leather jacket.

questions.rationale: A major depression is characterized by a prolonged behavioral change from baseline that interferes with school, family life, and age-specific activities, frequently signaled by giving prized possessions away.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with an Emotional or Behavioral Condition
questions.stem: A mother is concerned because her adolescent son is always in trouble for fighting at school and always seems to be angry. She mentions that her husband drinks a bit. Which understanding will guide the nurse‘s response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The boy is displaying antisocial behavior and should be evaluated for mental illness.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The boy is displaying one of the typical defense patterns of children of alcoholics and should receive immediate treatment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The mother is displaying her own anger with her husband‘s drinking, and she needs immediate intervention.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The boy is only one member of the family affected by alcoholism, and all members should receive immediate intervention.

questions.rationale: Early recognition of and intervention for children of alcoholics are paramount. This adolescent is using the coping pattern of acting-out behaviors to deal with the family situation.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with an Emotional or Behavioral Condition
questions.stem: What is the most appropriate classroom intervention for a child with attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) for the school nurse to suggest?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Seat the child in the back of the room to prevent distractions for other children.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pair the child with a student buddy to offer reminders to pay attention.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Divide work assignments into shorter periods with breaks in between.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Separate the child from others to increase his focus on schoolwork.

questions.rationale: The child with ADHD needs breaks between periods of work and study.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with an Emotional or Behavioral Condition
questions.stem: How does the nurse describe a person who is bulimic?
questions.rationale: Bulimia is characterized by alternating binge eating and purge behavior.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with an Emotional or Behavioral Condition
questions.stem: A 14-year-old girl with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) tells the nurse other adolescents tease her because she washes her hands many times during the school day. For what does this disorder put the adolescent at greater risk?
questions.rationale: OCD is related to depression and other psychiatric disorders. Suicidal behavior is a high risk for adolescents with OCD.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with an Emotional or Behavioral Condition
questions.stem: Which statement made by a parent of an adolescent with anorexia nervosa indicates an understanding of this condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “There really isn‘t anything to worry about. Don‘t they say you can never be too thin?”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “My daughter just doesn‘t have much of an appetite.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “She is just trying to punish me for divorcing her father.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “She seems to see herself as fat, even though her weight is below normal.”

questions.rationale: Individuals with anorexia nervosa have a disturbed body image, which this parent correctly recognizes.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with an Emotional or Behavioral Condition
questions.stem: What is an appropriate nursing intervention for a hospitalized child who is autistic?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Place the child in a location where she can watch all of the activity on the unit.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use the child‘s chronological age as a guide for communication.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Keep the child‘s room free of toys or objects that she might want to take home with her.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Organize care to provide as few disruptions to the routine as possible.

questions.rationale: During hospitalization, the nurse should provide a highly structured environment with few distractions for a child who is autistic.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with an Emotional or Behavioral Condition
questions.stem: A nurse is planning to speak with a parent support group about childhood autism. What will the nurse include?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Significant signs of the disorder manifest by 1 year of age.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The earliest signs of autism are impulsivity and overactivity.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Autism is usually diagnosed when the child goes to elementary school.

questions.rationale: Failure to use eye contact and look at others, poor attention span, and poor orienting to one‘s name are significant signs of dysfunction by 1 year of age.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with an Emotional or Behavioral Condition
questions.stem: An adolescent is brought to the emergency department after an automobile accident. When the nurse approaches the adolescent, he becomes combative. The nurse notes his speech is slurred and his gait is ataxic. What does the nurse suspect the adolescent has used?
questions.rationale: Behavioral signs of alcohol ingestion include slurred speech, short attention span, drowsiness, combativeness, and violence.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with an Emotional or Behavioral Condition
questions.stem: When the nurse is collecting a nursing history, an adolescent states that she has tried speed. For what does the nurse recognize this as the street name?
questions.rationale: “Speed” is the street name for methamphetamine.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with an Emotional or Behavioral Condition
questions.stem: How would the nurse identify a member of the child guidance team who is a medical doctor with special training in psychoanalytic theory?
questions.rationale: The psychiatrist is a medical doctor; the psychoanalyst may be a medical doctor or a psychologist. The psychologist is not a medical doctor, and neither is the counselor.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with an Emotional or Behavioral Condition
questions.stem: A young child on the pediatric unit cannot express himself well. What therapeutic intervention might the nurse implement that allows children to act out their feelings?
questions.rationale: Play therapy allows a young child to act out with dolls or figures concerns that the child may be unable to adequately express verbally.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with an Emotional or Behavioral Condition
questions.stem: The nurse explains that use of stimulants will decrease hyperactivity in the autistic child. What is a negative aspect of stimulants?
questions.rationale: Stimulants that decrease the hyperactivity in the autistic child also impair cognition and may increase the potential of self-injuring behavior.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with an Emotional or Behavioral Condition
questions.stem: A 9-year-old child has been admitted to the hospital after “huffing” lighter fluid and is ina high euphoric state. For what should the nurse assess?
questions.rationale: Inhaling hydrocarbons depresses the central nervous system, including respiratory rate and general sensorium.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with an Emotional or Behavioral Condition
questions.stem: The pediatric nurse listens to a 9-year-old child read to his 6-year-old roommate. What action by 9-year-old child leads the nurse to question possible dyslexia?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Becomes hyperactive and ceases to read.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reads the word dog as God.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Makes up a story rather than reading the text.

questions.rationale: Dyslexics often transpose a word as they read; for example, the word is dog, but it appears to the dyslexic child as the word God.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with an Emotional or Behavioral Condition
questions.stem: How is a gateway substance defined?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Drug used to wean from stronger drugs

choices.label: D
choices.text: Substance that can lead to use of stronger drugs

questions.rationale: A gateway drug is a substance that creates a high that can lead to the use of stronger drugs.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with an Emotional or Behavioral Condition
questions.stem: Which substance puts a person at the greatest risk for HIV and hepatitis B?
questions.rationale: The use of opiates coupled with sharing needles put the user at risk for HIV and hepatitis B.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with an Emotional or Behavioral Condition
questions.stem: What role has the child of an alcoholic assumed if he tries to do everything perfectly?
questions.rationale: Of the four roles for the child of the alcoholic, the super coper is one who tries to do everything perfectly and feels overly responsible. The perfect child is the child who tries to earn love by never causing any trouble.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with an Emotional or Behavioral Condition
questions.stem: The nurse working with children from dysfunctional families must be prepared to address what associated problem(s)? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Children from dysfunctional families exhibit lack of trust, act out, and show signs of depression.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with an Emotional or Behavioral Condition
questions.stem: The nurse counsels parents that the early school years create nervous tension in the child manifested by which abnormal behavior(s)? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Stuttering, aggressive behavior, and finger or thumb sucking that appear suddenly with no previous history are a clue to increased nervous tension in the young school-age child. Masturbation and food fads are normal behavioral phenomena for the early school-age child.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with an Emotional or Behavioral Condition
questions.stem: The nurse states that the members of a mental health team for child guidance include which member(s)? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: The traditional members of the child guidance team are the psychiatrist, pediatrician, psychologist, and social worker. The dietitian is not usually on the treatment team.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with an Emotional or Behavioral Condition
questions.stem: The school nurse cautions a group of parents about the prevalence of children who get high by inhaling hydrocarbons and fluorocarbons. Which products contain these substances? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Although there are many products that could be inhaled, the most frequently used products are glue, cleaning fluid, aerosol sprays, Freon, shoe polish, and gasoline products.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with an Emotional or Behavioral Condition
questions.stem: The nurse is planning the care of an adolescent with anorexia nervosa. What characteristic(s) cause this disorder? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: All options except pervasive high self-esteem are considered to be a cause of anorexia nervosa. Pervasive low self-esteem also is considered a cause of anorexia nervosa.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with an Emotional or Behavioral Condition
questions.stem: The nurse is assessing a 16-year-old female for characteristics of anorexia nervosa. Which assessment finding(s) would lead the nurse to suspect the possibility of this diagnosis? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: The primary symptom of anorexia nervosa is severe weight loss. Adolescents who wish to be fashion models or actresses or who participate in sports, dance, or gymnastics activities may be at risk for developing an eating disorder. On physical examination, some of the following conditions may be evident: dry skin, amenorrhea, lanugo hair over the back and extremities, cold intolerance, low blood pressure, abdominal pain, and constipation.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with an Emotional or Behavioral Condition
questions.stem: A nurse is hired to work in a psychiatric facility on a unit specializing in obsessive-compulsive disorders (OCD). Which diagnoses might the nurse expect to encounter? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Oppositional defiant disorder is described as an ongoing pattern of anger-guided disobedience, a hostile or defiant response to authority and is not considered a form of OCD.

questions.chapter_title: The Child with an Emotional or Behavioral Condition
questions.stem: A child is diagnosed with attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Which characteristics would the nurse assess in this child? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: ADHD is characterized by inattention, hyperactivity, impulsivity, and distractibility.

questions.chapter_title: Complementary and Alternative Therapies in Maternity and Pediatric Nursing
questions.stem: A pregnant woman tells the nurse that she got relief from nausea when she had a therapy that involves pressure and massage on meridian sites. What type of therapy does this describe?
questions.rationale: Acupressure uses finger pressure and massage on the meridian sites. It can be used during pregnancy to control nausea, backache, and pain. It has been useful for minor postpartum problems such as constipation.

questions.chapter_title: Complementary and Alternative Therapies in Maternity and Pediatric Nursing
questions.stem: Which child should not receive massage therapy?
questions.rationale: Children with Down syndrome are prone particularly to cervical spine anomalies and may be injured by massage therapy.

questions.chapter_title: Complementary and Alternative Therapies in Maternity and Pediatric Nursing
questions.stem: A 12-year-old with rheumatoid arthritis finds aromatherapy helpful for relieving her joint discomfort. Which essential oil is useful for children with chronic pain?
questions.rationale: Lavender, chamomile, and sandalwood essential oils are useful in aromatherapy for children with chronic pain.

questions.chapter_title: Complementary and Alternative Therapies in Maternity and Pediatric Nursing
questions.stem: A pregnant woman wishes to use aromatherapy during her labor and delivery. What is the most appropriate essential oil for the nurse to recommend?
questions.rationale: Citrus is one essential oil that has been shown to be useful during labor and delivery.

questions.chapter_title: Complementary and Alternative Therapies in Maternity and Pediatric Nursing
questions.stem: A parent asks the nurse, “What is guided imagery?” Which statement is the most accurate response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Tt is a technique where the patient focuses on an image to relieve stress.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “It involves using water to promote relaxation.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “The patient enters a hypnotic state of sleep to promote relaxation.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “It helps the patient recognize tension in the muscles with responses on an electronic machine.”

questions.rationale: In guided imagery, by focusing on a specific image, stress reduction and improved performance can result.

questions.chapter_title: Complementary and Alternative Therapies in Maternity and Pediatric Nursing
questions.stem: A woman taking St. John‘s wort and ginseng daily is scheduled to have a hysterectomy in 3 weeks. What instruction should the nurse provide?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The herbs are not likely to cause any problems during the surgery.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The St. John‘s wort must be stopped prior to surgery, but she can continue the ginseng.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The ginseng should be stopped 1 week before surgery.

choices.label: D
choices.text: She should discontinue taking both herbs 2 weeks before surgery.

questions.rationale: Both St. John‘s wort and ginseng can cause problems during surgery, and their use should be discontinued 2 weeks before surgery.

questions.chapter_title: Complementary and Alternative Therapies in Maternity and Pediatric Nursing
questions.stem: Which herb can the nurse suggest to be used for discomforts associated with menopause, such as hot flashes?
questions.rationale: Black cohosh diminishes hot flashes by reducing luteinizing hormone. It also reduces joint pain and other menopausal discomforts.

questions.chapter_title: Complementary and Alternative Therapies in Maternity and Pediatric Nursing
questions.stem: A young mother asks, “Is there an alternative medicine for children with asthma?” Which form of alternative medicine would be the most helpful for the nurse to suggest?
questions.rationale: The use of guided imagery has helped relieve some of the symptoms of asthma.

questions.chapter_title: Complementary and Alternative Therapies in Maternity and Pediatric Nursing
questions.stem: What is the difference between complementary therapy and alternative therapy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Complementary therapy must be administered by a medical doctor.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Complementary therapy is administered with conventional therapy.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Complementary therapy is administered to a group of patients at the same time.

questions.rationale: Complementary therapy is administered with conventional therapy, such as massage with muscle relaxants for low back pain.

questions.chapter_title: Complementary and Alternative Therapies in Maternity and Pediatric Nursing
questions.stem: The nurse uses a diagram to show the location of meridians. How will the nurse explain the definition of meridians?

choices.label: B
choices.text: They are invisible pathways for energy.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They are lines that divide the body into 10 zones.

choices.label: D
choices.text: They are areas of skin that are specifically innervated.

questions.rationale: Meridians are invisible pathways through which energy travels to effect acupuncture treatment.

questions.chapter_title: Complementary and Alternative Therapies in Maternity and Pediatric Nursing
questions.stem: Which herbal remedy used by a patient taking warfarin should the nurse report to the physician?
questions.rationale: Angelica prolongs prothrombin time and will synergize the effect of the warfarin.

questions.chapter_title: Complementary and Alternative Therapies in Maternity and Pediatric Nursing
questions.stem: What should the nurse remind a parent who is considering homeopathic remedies for treatment of her child‘s asthma?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Should be drunk with large amounts of fluid.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Can be taken with traditional Western medications.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Can be enhanced by drinking hot tea.

choices.label: D
choices.text: May contain mercury, alcohol, or arsenic.

questions.rationale: Homeopathic remedies often contain mercury, alcohol, or arsenic and are taken sublingually. All Western medications should be stopped when the homeopathic therapy is begun. Caffeine drinks are to be avoided during homeopathic treatment.

questions.chapter_title: Complementary and Alternative Therapies in Maternity and Pediatric Nursing
questions.stem: The focus of acupressure is to restore the balance of what?
questions.rationale: Acupressure is focused on the return of the balance of Chi to control disease processes.

questions.chapter_title: Complementary and Alternative Therapies in Maternity and Pediatric Nursing
questions.stem: A breastfeeding mother tells the nurse she is taking large doses of vitamin C to keep up her energy. What should the nurse warn that large doses of vitamin C can cause in an infant?
questions.rationale: Vitamin C can be passed on to a breastfeeding child through breast milk and can cause colic.

questions.chapter_title: Complementary and Alternative Therapies in Maternity and Pediatric Nursing
questions.stem: The pregnant patient with a stasis ulcer asks if she might be a candidate for hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT). What is the nurse‘s best response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: “Yes. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy should have no harmful effect on your baby.”

choices.label: B
choices.text: “No. High amounts of oxygen in your system will cause changes in your baby‘s heart.”

choices.label: C
choices.text: “Yes. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is a much better option than using antibiotics.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: “No. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy may cause the placenta to separate from the uterine wall.”

questions.rationale: High concentrations of oxygen in the mother‘s blood can cause closure of the ductus arteriosus and cause fetal death.

questions.chapter_title: Complementary and Alternative Therapies in Maternity and Pediatric Nursing
questions.stem: A patient is providing history information to the admitting nurse about treatment used for chronic pain. The patient reports she participates in a type of relaxation therapy that enables her to recognize tension in the muscles via responses on an electronic machine and visual electromyography responses. What type of therapy does the nurse record on admission record?
questions.rationale: Biofeedback is a type of relaxation therapy that enables the patient to recognize tension in the muscles via responses on an electronic machine and visual electromyography responses. The process is also used by traditional health care providers for drug addiction and chronic pain control.

questions.chapter_title: Complementary and Alternative Therapies in Maternity and Pediatric Nursing
questions.stem: What conditions would a nurse expect to see treated with hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT)? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) uses an airtight enclosure to provide compressed air or oxygen under increased pressure. HBOT is used to revive children with carbon monoxide poisoning, to aid wound healing, and to treat the diving syndrome known as decompression illness. HBOT is contraindicated during pregnancy, because the increased oxygen saturation can cause the ductus arteriosus to close, resulting in fetal death.

questions.chapter_title: Complementary and Alternative Therapies in Maternity and Pediatric Nursing
questions.stem: The mother of a pediatric patient asks the nurse about safety concerns with using herbal supplements with children. Which herbal products would the nurse educate this mother are safe to use in most of the pediatric population? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Ginger, fish oil, chamomile, and aloe vera are safe herbal products for children. However, some herbs, such as ephedra, can be fatal to children.

questions.chapter_title: Complementary and Alternative Therapies in Maternity and Pediatric Nursing
questions.stem: The nurse points out that light therapy is used in the treatment of patients with which disorder(s)? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Light therapy has proven effective in the treatment of persons with seasonal affective disorders. Light therapy is also used in the treatment of jaundiced babies.

questions.chapter_title: Complementary and Alternative Therapies in Maternity and Pediatric Nursing
questions.stem: What advantage(s) of alternative health care should the nurse outline when providing information to patients? (Select all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Offering more patient control of health care

choices.label: B
choices.text: Offering a variety of health care advisors

choices.label: C
choices.text: Keeping patients from having to make decisions

choices.label: D
choices.text: Using natural products rather than chemical ones

questions.rationale: Alternative health care actually promotes the patient‘s decision making in care.

questions.chapter_title: Complementary and Alternative Therapies in Maternity and Pediatric Nursing
questions.stem: Which approaches to care are combined with osteopathy? (Select all that apply.)
questions.rationale: Osteopaths combine manipulative therapy including pressure point therapy with traditional (allopathic) medicine.

questions.chapter_title: The Past, Present, and Future
questions.rationale: Obviously, if you know her, the answer is big fat fucking bitch, duh
questions.stem: A nurse just completed an assessment on her patient, Kaiya. Knowing what you do about her, what do you think the nurses assessment revealed? That she is a____?
